nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-018 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: On an admitted N-dimensional complex inner-product space V with orthonormal basis e_i, creation c_i^dagger = e_i wedge - and interior annihilation c_i on the exterior algebra of V (dimension 2^N) satisfy {c_i, c_j} = 0 and {c_i, c_j^dagger} = delta_ij; in particular (c_i)^2 = 0.
imported_structure: complex mode space V with inner product (admitted)
exterior Fock space as the carrier for fermionic states (admitted)
nodes.bottleneck: Mechanize the CAR identities on the exterior algebra; the statistics choice (exterior versus symmetric algebra) is an admitted postulate, and identifying modes with spin-1/2 particles needs the relativistic spin-statistics theorem, outside this finite setting.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-019 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: In the increasing occupation ordering on 6 modes, the sign of the hop c_target^dagger c_source on every occupation bitmask equals the product of the Jordan-Wigner parities of the annihilation and the creation step, checked exhaustively over all 2^6 states and ordered mode pairs.
imported_structure: Jordan-Wigner mapping between spin-1/2 Pauli operators and CAR operators (standard literature result)
nodes.bottleneck: The general Jordan-Wigner bijection c_j = (prod_{k<j} -sigma^z_k) sigma^-_j between spin-1/2 chains and CAR operators is a standard result imported here, not derived or mechanized in this checkout.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-020 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: For N CAR modes, gamma_{2j-1} = c_j + c_j^dagger and gamma_{2j} = -i(c_j - c_j^dagger) are self-adjoint with {gamma_a, gamma_b} = 2 delta_ab, generate the Clifford algebra on 2N generators, and P = prod_j (-i gamma_{2j-1} gamma_{2j}) is the fermion parity (-1)^N_op.
imported_structure: Majorana operator decomposition of CAR modes (standard literature result)
fermion parity superselection (physical postulate)
nodes.bottleneck: Standard algebra imported, not derived here; the trunk mechanizes only the two-generator case (DS-QM212-MAJORANA-PROBLEM). Parity superselection is a physical postulate, not a consequence of the algebra. CampaignMajoranaCliffordParity supplies CAR-conditional self-adjointness, anticommutators, equality of generated complex subalgebras, occupation projections, the signed local parity identity and ordered parity action on supplied common occupation eigenvectors. A formal one-mode positive trace-one density matrix need not commute with parity. The all-mode abstract Clifford identification, source CAR/Fock refinement and occupation-basis completeness remain outside these witnesses; no physical superselection law is inferred.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-021 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: The CAR constrain the operators c_i, not the Hamiltonian: H = 0, free hopping -t sum c_i^dagger c_j and the Hubbard H(t, U) are distinct Hermitian number-conserving operators on the same CAR Fock space, so a physical Hamiltonian is an added admission (explicit 2-site Hubbard matrix computed by hand).
imported_structure: Hermitian Hamiltonian H = H^dagger (admitted)
particle-number conservation [H, N] = 0 (admitted)
locality graph and real hopping t (admitted)
Hubbard on-site interaction U (admitted)
nodes.bottleneck: Hermiticity, number conservation, a locality graph, a one- and two-body truncation and the interaction U remain explicit admissions in every downstream sign record.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-022 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: For a finite self-adjoint H with H_xx = V_x, H_xy = -a_xy (-1)^{eps_xy} (a_xy > 0, eps symmetric), beta >= 0 and E* >= max V_x, Z = e^{-beta E*} sum_m beta^m/m! sum over closed length-m configuration paths of prod K_{x_{j+1} x_j} with K = E* I - H, and each nonzero closed term has sign (-1)^{sum of eps along the path}.
imported_structure: positive edge magnitudes a_xy, parities eps_xy and diagonal energies V_x on an orthonormal configuration basis (supplied; ledger ORIGIN-001)
nodes.bottleneck: The sign of a closed term is a property of the supplied magnitudes, parities and representation; vertex sign gauges remove all negative entries exactly when every configuration cycle is even (FSP-SWITCHING-NORMAL-FORM). Trotter slicing and its error are separate.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-023 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: For a declared path representation with weights W(c), <Sign> = Z / Z_abs with Z = sum sigma(c)|W(c)| and Z_abs = sum |W(c)|; when Z > 0, Delta f := -(1/(beta N)) log <Sign> >= 0, so <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) holds by definition.
imported_structure: declared path representation (basis and operator expansion)
nodes.bottleneck: Exponential decay in beta N is a hypothesis (Delta f bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in N and beta), not a theorem; Z_abs is an operational absolute ensemble, not in general a physical bosonic system.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-024 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: For M_s independent samples from |W|/Z_abs, the sign mean has variance (1 - <Sign>^2)/M_s, so relative error epsilon needs M_s >= (1 - <Sign>^2)/(epsilon^2 <Sign>^2); if <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) this is Omega(exp(2 beta N Delta f)).
imported_structure: independent sampling from the absolute-weight distribution (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: Correlated Markov-chain samples, observable numerators and the extensive-gap hypothesis need separate treatment; this bound concerns direct reweighting only, not every estimator or representation.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-025 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: For the 3-site spinless triangle, t = 1, U = 0, two fermions, beta = 2 and three Euler slices, the occupation-basis expansion has 27 paths, 6 negative of weight 8/27 and positive weights in {4/9, 1}, so no equal-weight pairing exists there; in the one-body eigenbasis H is diagonal with E in {-1, -1, 2} and Z = 2e^2 + e^-4.
nodes.bottleneck: Frustration alone does not imply disjoint weight spectra or hardness (ledger GIN-C4, INV-DISJOINT-SPEC); the general Lean lemma covers only the step from disjoint spectra to no weight-preserving sign-reversing involution.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-026 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: Troyer-Wiese (2005): the NP-complete decision whether a 3D +-J Ising spin glass has ground energy below a threshold reduces in polynomial time to estimating the thermal energy of the frustrated quantum model -sum J_ij sigma^x_i sigma^x_j at beta J >= N ln 2 + ln(12N); a deterministic polynomial estimator for that family would give P = NP, a randomized one NP subset of BPP.
imported_structure: Troyer and Wiese, PRL 94, 170201 (2005), cond-mat/0408370, equations (10)-(11) and footnote 9
NP-completeness of the 3D Ising spin-glass ground-state decision problem (Barahona)
nodes.bottleneck: This is a worst-case statement about a model family under a precision promise; it is not formalized here, is not a reduction to the Hubbard model, and does not make any fixed finite system or every fermionic Hamiltonian intractable.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-027 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For any carrier with weights in N and signs +-1, an involution tau with w(tau c) = w(c) and sign(tau c) = -sign(c) has no fixed point and each pair satisfies w(c) sign(c) + w(tau c) sign(tau c) = 0; zero signed sum does not require such a pairing (+2, -1, -1), and a cancelling doublet can carry a nonzero observable numerator.
imported_structure: supplied weight-preserving sign-reversing involution
nodes.bottleneck: Summing pairs to get sum_c w(c) sign(c) = 0 on a finite set is a prose orbit-partition step (manuscript Section 4.2), not mechanized; observable numerators need A o tau = A; the involution is sufficient, not necessary (INV-INVOL-CANC).

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-029 claims COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: For the four-site periodic ring, U = 0, two spin-up fermions, beta = 3/2 and four Euler slices, all 32 negative Euler-transfer paths are matched to disjoint positive paths of exactly equal rational weight within one weight fiber, and a posting-list query over k modes uses k posting-list operations.
nodes.bottleneck: Pairing is on exact weight fibers of enumerated paths, not a spectator-preserving symmetry (INV-GIN-PARITY); it does not preserve general observables, and path enumeration grows exponentially. CT-AUX update stability for multi-orbital models has no evidence here.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-030 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: For d0 in Q^{m x n} and W = im d0, N_W(x) = x - sum_i x_{p_i} r_i (nonzero RREF rows r_i of d0^T with pivots p_i) is sound, idempotent and complete for x ~ y iff x - y in W, and is independent of the generating matrix; Lean checks the three laws for the fixed integral image span(1, 2) in Z^2.
imported_structure: fixed rational coboundary matrix d0 and coordinate order
nodes.bottleneck: N_W is not an l1 minimizer (span(1,2), x = (1,0) gives norm 2 versus 1); the quotient norm is a separate exact linear program with a refusal budget (NF-003). A valid YAML contract or routing label is not a normalizer.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-032 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: With link phases U_ij = exp(i A_ij) on ordered vertex pairs and oriented closed-path products U_p over a finite plaquette family, the Wilson action S = beta_g sum_p (1 - Re U_p) is invariant under local U(1) gauge transformations and is nonnegative for beta_g >= 0.
nodes.bottleneck: Lean: CampaignFspU1WilsonAction.fsp_u1_wilson_action states gauge invariance (for every g: V -> U(1) and for every angle shift A_ij -> A_ij + theta_i - theta_j) and nonnegativity for beta_g >= 0, for any vertex type and any finite family of closed paths; the periodic hypercubic lattice (ZMod L)^d is one instance. beta_g >= 0 is required: one self-link plaquette with phase -1 and beta_g = -1 gives S = -2. Links are functions of ordered vertex pairs, so for L <= 2 the two parallel links between neighbours are identified. No fermion-sign consequence, continuum limit, reflection positivity, transfer matrix or non-abelian action is claimed. Audited PROVED_LEAN applies only to the narrowed DAG statement; the source record FSP-DERIV-032 claims strict positivity and a Haar-measure bound, neither established here.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-033 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: The Wilson-Dirac operator satisfies gamma5 D_W gamma5 = D_W^dagger, so its nonreal eigenvalues come in conjugate pairs and det D_W is real; for two degenerate flavors det(D_W)^2 >= 0.
imported_structure: Wilson-Dirac lattice fermion operator with r = 1 (standard lattice QCD)
nodes.bottleneck: A single-flavor det D_W can be negative; the JSONL claim that det D_W is nonnegative is only the two-flavor square. The gamma5 adjoint, reality of det D_W, and the two-flavor square for this operator are not Lean theorems in this checkout. Euclidean Clifford data in dimensions 2 and 4 are checked in Lean. An exact check on one periodic 2x2 lattice, mass -1, U(1), finds det = -3.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-034 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: Adding S_theta = i theta Q_top with real lattice charge Q_top multiplies the Boltzmann weight by exp(-i theta Q_top), which is nonreal unless theta Q_top lies in pi Z for every configuration, so positive-weight importance sampling is lost for generic theta != 0.
imported_structure: lattice topological charge Q_top and theta vacuum term (standard)
nodes.bottleneck: Severity of the resulting sign problem is phenomenology from the literature; the checkout has no theta-term model.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-035 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: Target: on a finite slab lattice the chiral variation of the boundary fermion determinant cancels the bulk Chern-Simons variation. Not established in this checkout. One tested candidate does not realize it, as expected: on open Wilson slabs with U(1) links, the gauge change acts on the Wilson matrix by a diagonal similarity, so the full, interior, boundary Schur and fixed site-matched chiral-block determinants are gauge invariant by construction, while a lifted cup-product CS term whose coefficient is not derived from the fermions changes by 1/32. This is a fixed-basis truncation of a vector-like regulator, not an obstruction to lattice inflow.
imported_structure: Callan-Harvey continuum anomaly inflow (literature)
nodes.bottleneck: Construct a regulated chiral boundary determinant whose projector, basis or measure depends on the gauge field (domain-wall or overlap/Ginsparg-Wilson type), derive from the same fermions the bulk Chern-Simons term they induce, and show that the two gauge variations cancel. The fixed-basis Wilson-slab test cannot register an anomaly, because site-matched fixed bases give similarity-invariant determinants; its bare lifted CS candidate is neither induced by the fermions nor well defined on U(1) links (an integer lift of the same links changes it by 1/8). The continuum Callan-Harvey mechanism remains a literature import.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-036 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: For lattice SU(2) with Dirac fermions in the real adjoint representation, an antiunitary symmetry of the Dirac operator makes det D_adj real for every gauge configuration.
imported_structure: lattice SU(2) gauge theory with adjoint Dirac fermions (standard)
nodes.bottleneck: For a single Majorana adjoint flavor the measure is a Pfaffian whose sign can change; reality is not positivity. CampaignFspSu2AdjointRealDet.lean establishes the 3x3 SO(3) adjoint representation of unit quaternions, Z_2 center blindness R(-q) = R(q), the antiunitary intertwiner reality identity C conj(D) = D C -> Im(det D) = 0, reality of the 4D lattice adjoint Wilson-Dirac determinant wilsonDiracAdjoint4_det_im_zero, a negative-determinant witness (det = -1 < 0), and the 2x2 and 4x4 skew-symmetric Majorana Pfaffian square identities and sign-flip pairs. Full continuum SU(2) path-integral construction and general 2n x 2n Berezin Grassmann integration remain literature imports.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-037 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: For lattice Dirac operators with chemical potential, gamma5 D(mu) gamma5 = D(-mu*)^dagger, hence det D(mu)^* = det D(-mu*); for real mu != 0 this relates D(mu) to D(-mu) only and det D(mu) is in general complex.
imported_structure: lattice QCD with staggered quarks at chemical potential (standard)
nodes.bottleneck: Standard continuum/thermodynamic QCD chemical-potential sign-problem framework imported; lean4/CampaignFspQcdChemicalPotentialDet.lean establishes the exact gamma_5-chemical-potential determinant conjugation identity (det D(mu))* = det D(-mu*), reality at mu = 0 and purely imaginary mu = i mu_I, the Hasenfratz-Karsch and Kogut-Susskind staggered operator identities, the explicit SU(3) clock link U = diag(i,i,-1) with Im Tr(U) = 2 != 0, the 6x6 chiral SU(3) determinant witness det D_SU3(2) = 63/8 - 27i and det D_SU3(1/2) = 63/8 + 27i, and the diagonal SU(2) reality contrast, while checks/independent/fsp-qcd-chemical-potential-det.py checks 1D and 2D staggered SU(3) vs SU(2) lattices.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-038 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: Claimed: averaging over Z3 center phases cancels the signs of fractional-triality quark paths and leaves color-singlet zero-triality contributions; no model, projection identity or computation for this exists in this checkout.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-039 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: At mu = i mu_I with real mu_I, gamma5 D(i mu_I) gamma5 = D(i mu_I)^dagger, so det D(i mu_I) is real; nonnegativity needs two degenerate flavors (or a staggered operator m + K with K anti-Hermitian, m > 0), and Z(mu_I) has Roberge-Weiss periodicity 2 pi T / 3.

CampaignFspImaginaryMuRealDet covers arbitrary finite bipartite transport blocks at unit fugacity: staggered adjoint symmetry, determinant reality, two-flavor nonnegativity and positive-mass staggered positivity. Its centerSum_periodic concerns a declared finite center-orbit sum only; it supplies no QCD measure, spin-taste reconstruction, phase transition or analytic-continuation theorem. The full node remains imported.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-040 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: Claimed: a finite-lattice 2D N=1 Wess-Zumino model with supercharges obeying {Q_a, Q_b} = 2 delta_ab H, H >= 0 and exact boson-fermion pairing of nonzero levels; no such lattice construction exists in this checkout, and lattice discretizations generally keep at most a subalgebra exact.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q0 claims OPEN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: Every step of a noisy quantum computation, syndrome extraction and repair included, adds residual, and repair consumes capacity while adding residual of its own; the question is whether this makes reliable completion a self-referential no-go or a threshold condition that holds only under named resource assumptions (fresh supply, net-efficient repair, bounded overhead growth, physical error below threshold).
nodes.bottleneck: The finite model answers the question as a threshold condition (QCV-Q1 to QCV-Q6); whether any physical system meets the named assumptions is not derived and no verdict on physical viability is given.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q1 claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: Backlog q(t+1) = max(0, q(t) + lam + g*mu - mu) in units of the Phi_1 repair cost, where lam is the residual generated per round by the computation, mu = kappa*r the repair rate from r fresh ancillas per round at kappa units each, and g the residual generated per unit of repair; with g = 0 this is the DS-QM101 queue; a distance-three level with a fault locations has constant c = a(a-1)/2.
imported_structure: declared generation rate lam
declared self-generated fraction g of repair
declared capacity kappa per fresh ancilla
declared fresh supply r per round
nodes.bottleneck: lam, g, kappa and r are declared inputs; no value is derived or measured for any code, and Phi_1 of a residual is not computed here.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q1B claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: In the QCV-Q1 model with q0 >= 0, the backlog is bounded iff lam <= (1-g)*mu; for g >= 1 and lam > 0 no mu >= 0 bounds it; for g < 1 and mu = kappa*r, with kappa > 0, it is bounded iff r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa); with r = 0 and lam > 0 it equals q0 + t*lam.
nodes.bottleneck: A statement inside the declared model; it does not say any code has g < 1 or that any supply r is available.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q1C claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: The union-bound recurrence p(k+1) = a*p(k) with a >= 1 and p(0) > 0 does not tend to zero; for 2 <= a <= b fault locations the certified threshold 1/pairCount(b) is at most 1/pairCount(a).
nodes.bottleneck: The location counts are declared; nothing here says how many repair locations a physical code needs.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-IMP-THRESHOLD claims IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: The fault-tolerance threshold theorems (Shor 1996; Aharonov and Ben-Or 1997; Kitaev 1997; Knill, Laflamme and Zurek 1998; Aliferis, Gottesman and Preskill 2006) are cited under each theorem's own noise, locality and overhead hypotheses; they are not re-proved.
imported_structure: threshold theorems for concatenated codes under their stated noise models
nodes.bottleneck: Exact constants and noise hypotheses of each theorem are not reproduced; the finite recurrence in QCV-Q2 is the only part checked.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q2 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For the recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2 over Q, c*p(k) = (c*p(0))^(2^k); for c > 0 and p(0) >= 0: if c*p(0) < 1 then p(k) tends to zero with c*p(k) <= (c*p(0))^(k+1) and, for c*p(0) <= 1/2, p(k) <= (1/2)^(2^k)/c; if c*p(0) = 1 then p(k) = 1/c for all k; if c*p(0) > 1 then p(k) diverges; so p(k) tends to zero iff p(0) < 1/c.
nodes.bottleneck: The recurrence is the hypothesis; no noise model is shown to obey it and no constant c is computed for any code.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q3 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For p(k+1) = c(k)*p(k)^2 with c(k) >= 0, p(k) = p(0)^(2^k)*amp(k) with amp(0) = 1, amp(k+1) = c(k)*amp(k)^2, and some p(0) > 0 has p(k) tending to zero iff some M > 0 has amp(k) <= M^(2^k) for all k; the criterion holds for c(k) <= C, for c(k) <= A*B^(k+1) with A, B >= 1, for c(k) = (k+1)^2, and for c(k) <= a*b^N(k) with block size N(k+1) <= s*N(k), s < 2; it fails for c(k) >= a*b^(2^k) with a > 0, b > 1, and for c(k) >= a*b^N(k) with 2^k <= N(k), b > 1, where no positive p(0) has p(k) tending to zero.
nodes.bottleneck: The families are exact illustrations of the criterion, not claims that any physical overhead has such a form; correlated-noise strength as an exponential of block size is a declared toy.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-IMP-ABIN claims IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: Aharonov, Ben-Or, Impagliazzo and Nisan (1996) show that noisy reversible or quantum computation with no supply of fresh low-entropy bits cannot preserve its input beyond a short depth; the result is cited, not re-proved or imported as a proof here.
imported_structure: ABIN 1996 limitation theorem for noisy reversible computation
nodes.bottleneck: The exact statement and its noise model are in the cited paper; QCV-Q4 establishes a finite exact analogue for global depolarizing noise only.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q4 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For complex matrices of any size d and the variational trace norm tn(X) = sup over unitaries U of |tr(UX)|, the global depolarizing channel satisfies tn(Delta_p(rho) - Delta_p(sigma)) = (1-p)*tn(rho - sigma) for equal-trace rho, sigma and p <= 1; along any history of unitaries V(i) with depolarizing rates p(i) in [0,1], tn(run rho - run sigma) = (product of (1-p(i)))*tn(rho - sigma), which is at most (1-p)^t*tn(rho - sigma) when every p(i) >= p, and (1-p)^t <= 1/(1+p*t).
imported_structure: variational trace norm equals the Schatten-1 norm (Ky Fan, cited)
global depolarizing noise at a declared rate after every step
nodes.bottleneck: The trace norm is the variational form, whose equality with the sum of singular values is cited; the noise is global depolarizing with a declared rate per step, not independent per-qubit noise, and the statement is about histories without fresh resets.

nodes.bottleneck: The identification of the qubit trace norm with the Bloch distance uses the cited eigenvalue fact; Python and Rust replays are exact on declared instances only.

fresh ancillas at rate r

For u in Q(i) (the Lean proofs of (a) and (b) do not use |u|=1), the two-qubit vector psi_u = (1,1,1,u)/2 has coefficient matrix M_u = [[1,1],[1,u]]/2 of determinant (u-1)/4. (a) psi_u is a product vector if and only if u=1. (b) The squared concurrence, defined as 4|det M|^2, equals |u-1|^2/4 for M_u; for u=(3+4i)/5, where |u|=1, it equals 1/5. (c) For all 2x2 matrices A and B over Q(i), det(A M B^T) = det(A) det(M) det(B), so det M = 0 implies det(A M B^T) = 0: local operations cannot raise a product vector to Schmidt rank 2; and diag(1,1,1,u) applied to the product vector (1,1,1,1)/2 gives psi_u. The physical inference from such entanglement to a non-classical mediator is imported, not part of this target.
nodes.bottleneck: Statement (d), an exact separating functional on the 4x4 density matrix relative to the product family in the form of DS-QM071, is not proved. The Lean module defines schmidtWitnessExpectation(M) = |det M|^2, a quadratic function of the amplitude matrix that vanishes on product vectors and is positive on psi_u for u != 1; that is a restatement of (a), not a linear functional on density matrices, and it is not shown to vanish on mixtures of product states or tied to DS-QM071. The rank inequality rank(A M B^T) <= rank(M) for general rank is stated only through the 2x2 determinant identity (preservation of det M = 0). No physical claim is attached.

nodes.statement: Haag and Kastler (1964) formulate quantum field theory through a net that assigns to bounded spacetime regions the algebras of observables localized there, with the standard structural requirements later grouped as isotony (larger regions have larger algebras), locality (algebras of spacelike separated regions commute) and Poincare covariance, and with states as positive functionals. This node records the framework; the paper's own list of postulates is not reproduced.

nodes.statement: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for site-factorized operators. For a FiniteStrictPoset P on n points put one qubit (a single-site monoid M) at each point; an operator A : Fin n -> M is localized in a subset O of P when it is the identity outside O, so the Lean "algebra" of O is the set of elementary tensor operators localized in O, not the full matrix algebra on the qubits in O. (a) Isotony: O1 inside O2 and A localized in O1 imply A localized in O2. (b) Locality: if every point of O1 is spacelike to every point of O2, then O1 and O2 are disjoint and operators localized in O1 and in O2 commute under the sitewise product. (c) The spacelike relation of CausalOrder.lean is symmetric (spacelike_symm) and irreflexive (spacelike_irrefl) and not transitive: on the four-element N poset 0<2, 1<2, 1<3, points 1 and 0 are spacelike, 0 and 3 are spacelike, and 1<3 are related. The content of Haag-Kastler locality (commutation forced by causal separation of dynamics) is absent because this net has no dynamics.
nodes.bottleneck: Not proved in Lean: the statements for the full local matrix algebras A(O) (linear spans of elementary tensors, for example 2^|O| x 2^|O| matrices): that commutation of elementary tensors extends by bilinearity to the algebras and that A(O1) is a subalgebra of A(O2) as matrix algebras; the single-site monoid M is generic and is not instantiated at 2x2 matrices. The net is kinematical: dynamics, a time-slice property and covariance are not modelled, so the statement is the finite shadow of two axioms and nothing more.

nodes.statement: Imported property: in a net of local algebras on Minkowski space with a translation action whose generators have positive spectrum (spectrum condition) and a vacuum vector, the vacuum is cyclic for every local algebra, and under further hypotheses separating for the algebra of a region with spacelike complement. The proof uses analytic continuation of translations, hence a continuous translation group and its generator (Stone theorem) on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Both are open nodes of the repository. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/algebraic components and non-equivalence fences: (1) over any semiring R and for any dimensions dA, dB (even when dA < dB), if Fin dA is inhabited then CyclicForA Omega implies SeparatingForAc Omega via matrix associativity (X * Omega) * Y = X * (Omega * Y), so any nonzero right-kernel vector or identically zero column precludes cyclicity even when dA < dB; (2) discharging the open finite items of TFQ-2107, none of |000>, |GHZ_3>, or |W_3> is cyclic on any single site (s in {0, 1, 2}), |000> has neither a left inverse nor cyclicity on any pair of sites while |GHZ_3> and |W_3> are both cyclic and separating on every pair of sites, all three states have full complementary rank 1 and are cyclic on the full 3-site algebra, and across the 4-qubit 2+2 bipartition neither |0000> nor |GHZ_4> is cyclic whereas the 2-Bell-pair cluster state has full complementary rank 4 and is both cyclic and separating; and (3) on a finite N-site ring, cyclicShift N aliases with period N, translation-invariant constant vectors have zero discrete momentum difference, and the translation-invariant 3-qubit product vacuum |000> fails cyclicity on every proper subsystem.

nodes.statement: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. Let Omega be a dA x dB matrix over a semiring R (the amplitude matrix of a vector in H_A tensor H_{A^c}; for qubits dA = 2^|A| and dB = 2^|A^c|, but the qubit tensor-factor bookkeeping is not formalised). Omega is cyclic for End(H_A) when every dA x dB matrix is X Omega for some X. (a) If Omega has a left inverse L with L Omega = I_dB (full column rank dB, which over a field is full rank of the reduced state on A^c) then Omega is cyclic and Omega is separating for End(H_{A^c}) (Omega Y = 0 implies Y = 0). (b) Conversely, cyclic implies a left inverse whenever dB <= dA (an injection Fin dB -> Fin dA is supplied). (c) A nonzero vector in the right kernel of Omega makes Omega not separating. (d) Exact 3-qubit instances over Z for the product vector |000>, GHZ = |000>+|111> and W = |100>+|010>+|001>: explicit nonzero right-kernel vectors for every single-site unfolding (2 x 4), explicit integer left inverses of every pair-of-sites unfolding (4 x 2) for GHZ and W, and a zero column in every pair-of-sites unfolding of |000>.
nodes.bottleneck: Not proved in Lean: separating implies full column rank (so the three-way equivalence is not complete); the identification of full column rank with full rank of the reduced state; the qubit subset bookkeeping; the conclusion "not cyclic" for the single-site cases (cyclic implies left inverse is proved only for dB <= dA, and a single site has dA=2 < dB=4; the kernel vectors give non-separating only) and for |000> on pairs (a zero column is exhibited but "zero column implies no left inverse implies not cyclic" is not stated as a theorem); that |000> is cyclic for the full algebra. nodes.statement: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin (1987) propose that spacetime at the smallest scales is a discrete structure, a causal set: a locally finite set with a partial order encoding past and future. They examine how a Lorentzian manifold can approximate such a set, note that effective dimensionality can vary with length scale, and sketch a quantum dynamics. Sorkin's Valdivia notes (2003) are a later survey. This node records the proposal.

nodes.statement: Reading of definitions. A causal set in the sense of the source is a locally finite partially ordered set; in the strict-order form its relation is irreflexive and transitive, and local finiteness is automatic on a finite set. The Python class CausalSet in code/python/src/general_relativity/causal_set.py builds a poset from relations, takes the transitive closure and refuses cycles. Narrowed to its exact finite/rational algebraic shadows: (1) over Q, the GKPW scalar mass-dimension quadratic gkpwMassSq(d, Delta) = Delta(Delta - d) = mSq satisfies the shadow involution Delta |-> d - Delta, (2 Delta - d)^2 = d^2 + 4 Delta(Delta - d), and the Breitenlohner-Freedman lower bound -(d^2)/4 <= Delta(Delta - d) with double root Delta = d/2 at saturation and no rational root strictly below -(d^2)/4; (2) in 't Hooft double-line counting with lambda = g_YM^2 N and Euler characteristic chi = V - E + F = 2 - 2g, the ribbon weight satisfies (g_YM^2)^(E - V) N^F * N^(E - V) = lambda^(E - V) N^F, suppressing the genus-1 torus vacuum graph (V=2, E=3, F=1) relative to the planar dipole (V=2, E=3, F=3) by N^2; and (3) for any finite isometric bulk-to-boundary encoding V^T V = I_b, the pushforward iota_V(O_bulk) = V O_bulk V^T and pullback pi_V(O_bdry) = V^T O_bdry V satisfy pi_V(iota_V(O_bulk)) = O_bulk, iota_V(A) iota_V(C) = iota_V(A C), and <V psi, O_bdry(V psi)> = <psi, pi_V(O_bdry) psi>, whereas for b = 1 < B = 2 (V = [[1],[0]]) V V^T != I_2 and the nonzero boundary operator O_perp = [[0,0],[0,1]] pulls back to 0 and has no bulk preimage.

nodes.statement: Ryu and Takayanagi (2006, arXiv:hep-th/0603001, Section 1 eq. (1.5) p. 2) propose that the entanglement entropy S_A of a spatial subregion A in a (d+1)-dimensional CFT dual to static AdS_{d+2} is given by S_A = Area(gamma_A) / (4 G_N^(d+2)), where gamma_A is the static minimal bulk d-surface anchored on partial A, and check in Section 2 (eqs. (2.1), (2.5)-(2.6) p. 3) that in AdS_3/CFT_2 the geodesic length reproduces S_A = (c/3) log((L/(pi a)) sin(pi l / L)) under the Brown-Henneaux relation c = 3R / (2 G_N^(3)). This node records the proposal as published.

nodes.statement: Imported formula, as the source states it at leading order in Newton's constant: S(A) = Area(minimal surface anchored on the boundary of A) / (4 G). It presupposes the von Neumann entropy of a boundary reduced state on a continuum Hilbert space and the area of a surface in a bulk geometry. The repository has an exact von Neumann entropy dichotomy for algebraic spectra and an exact rational Regge area proxy that is not the Einstein-Hilbert action; neither is a minimal-surface area in a bulk geometry. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/rational algebraic shadows and scope fences: (1) over Q, substituting the regulated AdS_3 geodesic length 2 R_AdS * logFactor into rtLeadingEntropy(area, G_N) = area / (4 G_N) reproduces the 2D CFT Calabrese-Cardy coefficient (c / 3) * logFactor under the Brown-Henneaux relation c = 3 R_AdS / (2 G_N^(3)) and eliminates both bulk couplings in S_A / c = logFactor / 3, while submodular surface pasting yields Strong Subadditivity S(ABC) + S(B) <= S(AB) + S(BC) and all 380 proper contiguous boundary intervals of the 20-qubit 6-pentagon HaPPY patch satisfy complement symmetry A <-> A^c; (2) under BakerCitedInput (EntropyDichotomy.lean), no mixed algebraic spectrum can have natural-log von Neumann entropy equal to a rational RT ratio area / (4 G_N), equality holds at G_N > 0 iff the state is pure and area = 0, and stabilizer bit counts require dividing by log 2; and (3) on the orthogonal_pentatope chart of TFQ-0100, the 6 right-triangle hinges have Cayley-Menger squared area 1/4 and the 4 equilateral-triangle hinges have squared area 3/4 (total 9/2) with no rational linear area A in Q satisfying A^2 = 3/4, the flat-chart Regge proxy (kappa = 0) vanishes identically whereas all 380 HaPPY intervals satisfy 1 <= S(A) <= mincut(A), and under length rescaling L -> lam * L the Regge proxy scales as lam^4 against lam^2 for 2-surface area and lam^0 for bond counts.
imported_structure: von Neumann entropy of boundary regions on a continuum Hilbert space (assumption)
bulk geometry with minimal surfaces (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: No source supplies a dictionary from the repository's finite areas to the surface areas of the formula; under BakerCitedInput mixed algebraic spectra have transcendental natural-log entropy, and the TFQ-0100 rational Regge proxy scales as lam^4 and vanishes on flat charts.

nodes.statement: Formalized finite statement. The [[5,1,3]] code of Laflamme, Miquel, Paz and Zurek has stabilizer generators XZZXI, IXZZX, XIXZZ, ZXIXZ and logical operators XXXXX and ZZZZZ. Its Choi state is the six-qubit stabilizer state with generators g tensor I (four of them), XXXXX tensor X and ZZZZZ tensor Z. Checked in Lean 4 on Pauli operators modulo phase (GF(2) symplectic vectors): the six generators pairwise commute and generate a group of 64 distinct elements, with weight distribution 1 element of weight 0, 45 of weight 4 and 18 of weight 6 (the hexacode six-qubit state), so every non-identity element has weight at least 4, which is the perfect-tensor condition (every bipartition with at most three legs on one side has a maximally mixed marginal); for all twenty 3|3 bipartitions the stabilizer subgroup supported on one side is trivial, so the entropy is 3 bits by the stabilizer formula S(A) = |A| - log2 |G_A|; and in the five-qubit code the normalizer of the 16-element stabilizer has order 64 and its 48 elements outside the stabilizer (the nontrivial logical operators, modulo phase) have minimum weight 3. The reading of weights and local stabilizer subgroups as marginals and entropies is the standard stabilizer-formalism dictionary and is not formalised on density matrices.
nodes.bottleneck: Checked in Lean 4 by exhaustive GF(2) symplectic enumeration over the 64-element stabilizer group, the 20 bipartitions and the 1024-element five-qubit Pauli group. A finite stabilizer enumeration is not a statement about AdS/CFT.

nodes.statement: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for a hand-encoded model. Contract six copies of the six-leg perfect tensor on the {5,4} pentagon tiling: one central tensor and its five edge-neighbours, which are not adjacent to each other, so the patch has 20 dangling boundary legs (4 per outer tensor) and 6 bulk legs, every bulk leg fixed in the logical zero state. In Lean the 20-qubit boundary stabilizer is given by 20 explicit generators (15 local to the five outer blocks and 5 pushed through the internal bonds from the central tensor): they pairwise commute and have full GF(2) rank 20. For all 380 proper contiguous boundary intervals A (20 starting positions, lengths 1 to 19), with S(A) = rank(G restricted to A) - |A| in bits and mincut(A) the minimal number of bonds cut separating A from its complement in the six-tensor star graph: S(A) <= mincut(A) on all 380 intervals, S(A) = mincut(A) on exactly 340 intervals, and S(A) = mincut(A) - 1 on exactly 40. The Ryu-Takayanagi equality therefore fails on this patch for 40 intervals; it is not a statement that holds for every region.
nodes.bottleneck: Not proved in Lean: that the 20 explicit generators are the boundary stabilizer of the contracted six-tensor network with bulk legs fixed at logical zero (they are entered by hand from the pushing rules of the code generators); that mincut as computed (a minimum over side assignments of the six tensors) is the minimal curve cut in the planar dual; the list of the 40 intervals where equality fails (only the counts are stated). The correspondence to a continuum minimal-surface area is the imported formula and is not part of the target.

nodes.statement: Formalized finite statement. For the [[5,1,3]] code, each of the ten 3-qubit subsets T of physical qubits supports a representative of each of the three nontrivial logical classes (the cosets of the stabilizer by XXXXX, ZZZZZ and YYYYY, the product class), and no 2-qubit subset supports a representative of any of them. Equivalent statement also checked in Lean 4: all 105 non-identity Pauli errors of weight 1 or 2 anticommute with a stabilizer generator, so none lies in the normalizer and erasure of any two qubits is correctable (the Knill-Laflamme condition). All operators are Pauli operators modulo phase. This is the smallest exact instance of the subregion-reconstruction picture of bulk operators.
nodes.bottleneck: Checked in Lean 4 over the 16-element stabilizer, its three logical cosets, all 10 triples, all 10 pairs and all 105 low-weight Pauli errors. The identification with bulk operator reconstruction in AdS/CFT is the imported picture of the source.

nodes.statement: No source read for this change derives AdS/CFT, or its continuum entropy formula, from a finite stabilizer-code tensor network. The HaPPY codes are discrete kinematic models of the bulk-to-boundary map on a hyperbolic tiling with no Lorentzian time, no dynamics, no gravitational action and no large-N limit. nodes.statement: Penrose (1971) starts from angular momentum, whose spectrum is discrete, and asks whether space can be built up by applying the rules for combining angular momenta; the construction is the origin of spin networks. This node records the chapter by title and publication details.

nodes.statement: Rovelli and Smolin (1995, arXiv:gr-qc/9505006, Phys. Rev. D 52, 5743) construct an independent basis of states in both the loop representation (Section 3 pp. 12-16) and the SU(2) connection representation (Section 4 pp. 17-24) that solves the SU(2) Mandelstam identities (Section 2 eq. (21) and conditions i-ii p. 12), labelled by imbedded graphs whose edges carry SU(2) representations (twice-spins p_l) and whose higher-valence vertices carry virtual trivalent trees/intertwiners (Appendix A pp. 36-38), and show in Section 6 (pp. 26-29) that these spin-network states are orthonormal with respect to the Ashtekar-Lewandowski Haar measure. This node records the paper as published.

nodes.statement: Rovelli and Smolin (1995, arXiv:gr-qc/9411005, Section 1 eqs. (1)-(2) p. 4 and Section 4 eqs. (47)-(48) p. 28) and Ashtekar and Lewandowski (1997, arXiv:gr-qc/9602046, Section 3.3 eq. (3.20) p. 16 and Section 4.1 eqs. (4.7)-(4.9), (4.12) pp. 18-19) compute discrete spectra for loop-quantum-gravity area (and volume) operators. In the convention {A_a^i(x), E_j^b(y)} = G delta_a^b delta_j^i delta^3(x,y) used in both papers, the general area eigenvalue is (l_P^2 / 2) sum_v sqrt(2 j_v^(d)(j_v^(d)+1) + 2 j_v^(u)(j_v^(u)+1) - j_v^(d+u)(j_v^(d+u)+1)) (eq. (4.9) of gr-qc/9602046), which for simple transverse punctures without tangential edges (j^(d)=j^(u)=j_i, j^(d+u)=0) equals l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)) = (l_P^2 / 2) sum_i sqrt(p_i(p_i+2)) with p_i = 2 j_i (eq. (2) and eq. (47) of gr-qc/9411005; eq. (4.12) of gr-qc/9602046); as Ashtekar and Lewandowski note in Section 3.3 footnote 6 (p. 16) and Engle et al. write in arXiv:0711.0146 Section V eq. (36) (p. 11), restoring the 8 pi G gamma factor from the gravitational action and Barbero-Immirzi parameter gamma multiplies this spectrum by 8 pi gamma, giving 8 pi gamma l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)). (The nonzero trivalent volume formula in eq. (1) and eq. (37) of gr-qc/9411005 was corrected in the erratum Nucl. Phys. B 456 (1995) 753, where trivalent vertices have zero volume.) This node records both papers and their normalization conventions.

nodes.statement: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the formal radical basis. With the dimensionless area a = sum over punctures of sqrt(j(j+1)) for spins j in {1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3}, each term is c_j sqrt(s_j) with squarefree radicand s_j in {2, 3, 6, 15, 35}: sqrt(3)/2, sqrt(2), sqrt(15)/2, sqrt(6), sqrt(35)/2 and 2 sqrt(3) for j = 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3 (radicands 3, 2, 15, 6, 35, 3); Lean checks k(k+2) = m_k^2 d_k with d_k squarefree for the twice-spins k = 1..6, and holds each term as a vector in the formal Q-module on the basis (sqrt2, sqrt3, sqrt6, sqrt15, sqrt35)/2. On that module: (i) the 210 puncture multisets of size at most 4 (the empty one and 209 nonempty ones) have 209 distinct reduced vectors, the zero vector included (208 nonzero); (ii) the unique collision is one puncture of spin 3 with four punctures of spin 1/2 (2 sqrt(3) = 4 x sqrt(3)/2); (iii) for a single puncture the squared area j(j+1) = k(k+2)/4 is at least 3/4, strictly increasing in k, with minimum 3/4 at j = 1/2 (area sqrt(3)/2).
nodes.bottleneck: Not proved in Lean: that the formal vector is the real area (no real square root occurs in the module) and that two multisets have equal real area if and only if their vectors agree, which needs the linear independence over Q of sqrt(2), sqrt(3), sqrt(6), sqrt(15), sqrt(35) (stated in the module header, not a Lean theorem); the agreement of the hand-entered punctureArea table with the m_k, d_k table beyond inspection; the minimum over multisets of several punctures (only single punctures). nodes.statement: Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Section 1 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61) establishes by geometric quantization of the 8-sphere and stationary phase on the symplectic reduction that for an admissible 6-tuple of integers a, b, c, d, e, f (where a = 2j labels the (a+1)-dimensional irreducible representation of SU(2)) whose side lengths form a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron tau of positive volume V(tau) > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the rescaled 6j symbol {ka, kb, kc; kd, ke, kf} has the k -> infinity asymptotic expansion sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(tau) k^3)) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (k a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) + O(k^{-5/2}). Since a tetrahedron of side lengths j_r = a_r/2 has volume V_j = V(tau)/8, substituting 2 / (3 pi V(tau)) = 1 / (12 pi V_j) and (a_r + 1)/2 = j_r + 1/2 recovers the Ponzano-Regge prefactor (12 pi V_j)^{-1/2}. This node records the paper's theorem.
nodes.bottleneck: Record only. Audited against arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61 on 2026-10-22.

nodes.statement: For rational gamma and rational k, the imported Euclidean labels are j+ = |1 + gamma| k / 2 and j- = |1 - gamma| k / 2. When 0 < gamma < 1 they equal (1 + gamma) k / 2 and (1 - gamma) k / 2, their sum is k, and their difference is gamma k. When gamma > 1 they equal (1 + gamma) k / 2 and (gamma - 1) k / 2, their difference is k, and their sum is gamma k. At gamma = 1/2 and k = 2 the labels are 3/2 and 1/2, the sum is 2, and the difference is 1, which is not 2. At gamma = 3 and k = 2 the labels are 4 and 2, the difference is 2, and the sum is 6, which is not 2. At gamma = 1 and k = 2 the labels are 2 and 0, and both the sum and the difference equal 2. The imported Lorentzian pair is (n, rho) = (2 k, 2 gamma k), with rho = gamma n = 2 gamma (n / 2). At gamma = 1/2 and k = 2 this pair is (4, 2), the index j = n / 2 equals 2, and gamma j equals 1, so rho = 2 gamma j rather than gamma j. The number of unordered pairs among five indices is 10. A Spin(4) 15j contraction, booster factors, a continuum Lie-group representation, a spin-network boundary space, a sum over spins, a continuum limit, a semiclassical limit, and a cosmological constant stay imported and are not constructed. nodes.statement: No construction turns PGW-GO-ADMISSION-GATE into a finite semi-simplicial set or a finite globular set. That gate keeps a two-valued admission record with a reached result: reaching leaves not-admitted, and admission is not one of the four kinds of change. A finite semi-simplicial set of dimension at most N is finite sets X_0, ..., X_N and face maps d_i from X_n to X_{n-1} such that d_i composed with d_j equals d_{j-1} composed with d_i whenever i < j. It carries no degeneracy maps. A finite globular set is finite sets with source and target maps s, t from X_{n+1} to X_n such that s composed with s equals s composed with t, and t composed with t equals t composed with s. Neither family is defined from the admission record.

nodes.statement: The horn Lambda^k[n] is the union of all faces of the standard n-simplex except the face opposite vertex k. The horn is inner when 0 < k < n and outer when k = 0 or k = n. A Kan condition asks for a filler of every horn. A quasicategory asks for a filler of every inner horn, in the sense of Joyal, Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 175 (2002) 207-222. Which of these fillers a finite object derived from Genesis admission would have is open. No filler is exhibited and no counterexample is exhibited, because no such finite object is constructed.

nodes.source_status: Prose under hypotheses (i), (ii) and (iii) in the statement. Those hypotheses do not mention the priced admission language. No Lean declaration.
nodes.statement: Let S be a theory in classical first-order logic with a primitive recursive coding of its syntax. Write code(psi) for the code of a sentence psi and num(n) for the numeral of a natural number n. Assume (i) consistency: there is no sentence psi such that S derives both psi and the negation of psi. Assume (ii) a primitive recursive relation Proof such that psi is a theorem of S exactly when Proof(p, code(psi)) holds for some natural number p, and Proof is represented at standard numerals: for all natural numbers p and s, S derives the sentence expressing Proof(num(p), num(s)) when the relation holds and derives its negation when the relation fails. Assume (iii) that S derives every true Delta_0 sentence of this coding; that the substitution function subst, sending the code of a formula with one free variable and a number n to the code of the sentence obtained by substituting num(n) for that variable, is represented in S; that the primitive recursive function neg on codes, with neg(code(psi)) equal to code(the negation of psi), is represented in S; and that for each standard natural number n, S derives both that every w with w < num(n) equals one of num(0), ..., num(n-1), and that every w satisfies w < num(n) or w = num(n) or num(n) < w. Then there is a sentence phi such that S derives neither phi nor the negation of phi. The diagonal lemma from representation of subst supplies, for the negation of the Rosser formula RosserProv(v) given by existence of a u such that Proof(u, v) and such that Proof(w, neg(v)) fails for every w < u, a sentence phi such that S derives the biconditional of phi and the negation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))). If S derives phi, a standard derivation code p, clause (i), numeral-wise representation of Proof, and the schema that every number below num(p) equals one of num(0), ..., num(p-1), yield a derivation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))) and then of the negation of phi. If S derives the negation of phi, a least standard derivation code q of that negation, numeral-wise representation of Proof, the same bounded schema at q, and the schema that every number is below num(q), equal to num(q), or above num(q), yield a derivation of the negation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))) and then of phi. Either case contradicts (i). Separately, drop (i) and (ii) and keep (iii): if a formula Tr(x) is such that S derives the biconditional of Tr(num(code(psi))) and psi for every sentence psi, the same diagonal lemma applied to the negation of Tr supplies a sentence lambda for which those biconditionals yield a derivation of both lambda and its negation, so S is inconsistent. Both conclusions use only the hypotheses just stated and classical first-order logic.
nodes.bottleneck: The two limit statements are conditional on the hypotheses in the statement. The priced admission language is not defined and is not shown to meet (i), (ii) or (iii). Nothing is formalised in Lean. Admitting a later theory is a priced import record, not a derivation from the core.

nodes.statement: Definition A1 of the source note. Fix a finite set M of measurements with finite outcome sets and a cover C of M by maximal contexts, and write E(U) for the set of outcome assignments on U. An observer tuple is O = (K, Adm, norm, Term, L). K = (M, C, E). Adm is the convex hull conv(A) of the vectors (delta_g restricted to C) over all contexts C, for g in E(M). The norm is the l1 norm on the stacked context distributions. Term maps the defect and the claim to a status: defect 0 gives ExactRepair, defect above 0 with a support-level global section gives ClosedResidual, and otherwise OpenObstruction. L is the diagnostic layer. The defect of a claim e = (e_C), one distribution per context, is Delta_O(e) = min over p in Adm of the l1 norm of (e - p). The five components are a projection of the four packets of WDP chapter 10 (presentation, memory, evaluator, policy) and of the chapter 15 grade. The monograph defines no five-tuple of its own; the ledger row records a search for "5-tuple" that returned nothing.
nodes.bottleneck: A reading of WDP-CH10-D01 to D04, not a derivation. WDP chapter 15 has no node in this graph, so the layer component has no repository node to attach to. No source relates the L1 observer axioms H1 to H5 to this five-component tuple.

nodes.statement: In Lean (LggrFiniteResults), a finitely supported measure with natural-number weights is a list of (value, weight) pairs, and pushforward along f maps each value by f and keeps its weight. Then: push of the identity is the identity (push_id); push along g after f equals push along the composite (push_comp); total mass is unchanged (mass_push); and the weight at b of push f p equals the mass of the entries of p whose image is b (weightAt_push). The note reads marginalisation of a context distribution as such a pushforward along the restriction map, so these are the identity and composition laws of the functor from the opposite of the context poset to probability vectors (Lemma B2). That reading is not a Lean statement. Not covered: rational weights, normalisation to probability vectors, the context poset, and the Rust types. The ledger row states the same narrowing.

nodes.statement: In Lean (LggrFiniteResults), take a length n > 0 and edge parities b : Nat -> Bool. Let holonomy b k be the exclusive or of b 0, ..., b (k-1), and call g a section when, for every i < n, the exclusive or of g i and g ((i+1) mod n) equals b i. Then (section_exists_iff_holonomy_zero) a section exists if and only if holonomy b n = false. Further (no_joint_measure_when_holonomy_one), if holonomy b n = true then no finitely supported natural-weight measure on assignments Nat -> Bool with positive total mass has, for every i < n, zero pushforward weight on every pair of values (g i, g ((i+1) mod n)) whose exclusive or differs from b i. These are the clause "G(e) is nonempty iff the holonomy h is 0" and the clause "holonomy 1 forbids a positive-mass joint measure with parity-supported marginals" of Proposition B6. Not in Lean: the arc-cover clause, the noncontextual-fraction clause and the Cech-cohomology reading.

nodes.statement: Proposition B3(1). For an empirical model e = (e_C) on a finite scenario, let A be the matrix whose column g, for g in E(M), is the stacked vector of the point masses of g restricted to each context, and let NCF(e) = max of the sum of lambda_g over lambda >= 0 with A lambda <= e. Then these are equivalent: e has a global section (a probability vector d on E(M) with marginal e_C on every context C); e lies in conv(A); NCF(e) = 1. This is the local-hidden-variable condition. Instances recomputed exactly: the mixture (1/2)(delta_g1 + delta_g2), with g1 = (0,0,0,0) and g2 = (1,0,0,1) on (a, a', b, b'), has NCF 1; the noisy PR box (1 - lam) PR + lam U at lam = 1/2 has NCF 1 and a distribution as a global section.

nodes.statement: Proposition B3(3). Write G(e) for the set of g in E(M) with e_C(g restricted to C) > 0 for every context C. Then e is strongly contextual (G(e) is empty) if and only if NCF(e) = 0: if lambda_g > 0 is feasible then e_C(g|C) >= lambda_g > 0 for every C, so g is in G(e); conversely g in G(e) makes lambda = (min over C of e_C(g|C)) delta_g feasible with positive weight. Instance recomputed exactly: the PR box on the Bell scenario (contexts ab, ab', a'b, a'b', each uniform on the two outcome pairs with parity 0, 0, 0, 1) has |G| = 0 and NCF 0. The four parity constraints x_a + x_b = 0, x_a + x_b' = 0, x_a' + x_b = 0 and x_a' + x_b' = 1 sum to 0 = 1 modulo 2, so none of the 16 assignments satisfies all.

nodes.statement: Proposition B4(1). Let S(U) be the set of assignments s on U whose restriction to every maximal context C inside U lies in the support of e_C; then S(M) = G(e). Over the cover of M by its maximal contexts, every matching family (s_C in S(C), agreeing on overlaps) glues to exactly one element of S(M). So a descent classifier on that cover reports no NoGlobalExtension, its fibers are in bijection with G(e), and strong contextuality appears as zero matching families, not as a failed gluing. Instances recomputed exactly: the PR box has 0 matching families; the noisy PR box at lam = 1/2 has 16, each with exactly one gluing.

nodes.statement: Existence witness. On the Bell scenario let e = (1/2)(delta_g1 + delta_g2) with g1 = (a, a', b, b') = (0,0,0,0) and g2 = (1,0,0,1). Then NCF(e) = 1 and G(e) has 2 elements. nodes.statement: Proposition B5. Let N be the nerve of the maximal-context cover and take cochains valued in the presheaf U -> Q^E(U), with (delta0 alpha)_(C,C') the restriction of alpha_C to the overlap minus the restriction of alpha_C', and delta1 the alternating sum of restrictions on triples. Instances recomputed exactly: the Bell nerve has four edges (a 4-cycle) and no triple, so delta1 delta0 = 0 is vacuous there; on the cover {0,1}, {0,2}, {0,3} (one nerve triple, overlap {0}) delta1 delta0 alpha = 0 for a non-constant alpha while a 1-cochain supported on one pair has delta1 beta = [1, 0]; delta0 e = 0 for the PR box and is nonzero at the pair (0,1) for a model whose a-marginal differs between the contexts ab and ab'; the unit cochain (1, 1) on the first edge of the Bell nerve has Phi_1 = 2, by the value 2 at alpha = 0 and a dual witness of sup norm 1 that annihilates delta0, and Phi_1 is again 2 after adding delta0 of a coboundary.

nodes.statement: Assumed from Vorob'ev (Theory of Probability and its Applications 7 (1962) 147-163, doi:10.1137/1107014), as the note states it: if the hypergraph (M, C) is GYO-acyclic (it reduces to nothing by removing ears and absorbed vertices, equivalently it has a join tree), then every no-signalling model has a global section given on a join tree T by d(g) = (product over C of e_C(g|C)) / (product over the edges (C, C') of T of e_(C intersect C')(g|C intersect C')), with 0/0 = 0. The note gives an induction sketch, not a full proof. The converse (for every non-acyclic hypergraph some no-signalling family has no global section) is not implemented; the PR box on the 4-cycle is one instance.

Let O' leave one of K, Adm, norm, Term undeclared, and require that an evaluation's receipt for a claim agree across every admissible completion of the undeclared component. nodes.statement: Axis 3 of WDP-CH14-T01 under three hypotheses. (i) NS-14: an injective renaming sigma of presentation tokens commutes with the transition step and with full-history replay. (ii) CL-13 (passage_charge_const): a quantity conserved by internal transitions is constant on reachable states and equals its genesis value. (iii) The verdict V reads a history only through a declared export Exp, so V = Vbar o Exp, with Exp(sigma(H)) = Exp(H) for every injective renaming sigma; this is the identical-accessible-exports premise of Proposition 3.1 of the Argon synthesis. Then V(sigma(H)) = V(H), because V(sigma(H)) = Vbar(Exp(sigma(H))) = Vbar(Exp(H)) = V(H). Without (iii) the statement is false (node OPS-REFUTED-AXIS3-WIDE). A drop in the internal defect Delta_O stays computable and renaming-invariant; whether a drop is a repair or a reinterpretation is a question about the grounding map of the tokens, which no export-reading verdict decides.

nodes.statement: At head 0a0502646 of the source repository the following were wrong. (N4) Scenario::section_count multiplied arities without a check, and the limit was compared afterwards: 64 binary singletons (2^64 assignments) wrapped to 0 in a release build, so global_support returned an empty support and is_strongly_contextual returned true. (N5) ObserverDraft::declare accepted empty and whitespace strings, and the five strings were free text copied into the receipt: a norm "L2", a terminal "always OpenObstruction" and a layer "authoritative" each yielded the l1 value, ExactRepair and authority None. (N7) delta0 checked only the number of entries, delta1 and flatten1 ignored extraneous keys and pairs outside every triple, and the only delta1 delta0 = 0 test ran on the Bell nerve, which has no triple. Recomputed here: 2^64 is 0 modulo 2^64.

records.summary: Narrowed finite case, status unchanged. On the directed path with integer edge weights a on 0 to 1 and b on 1 to 2, the length-1 path sum from 0 to 2 is 0 and the length-2 path sum is a*b. The unnormalized sector mask (w0, w1) maps to (0, w1): it is supported on the second coordinate, keeps that coordinate, is idempotent, and sends (w0, 0) to (0, 0). For every integer t, the Cayley column squared length (1 - t*t)^2 + (2*t)^2 equals (1 + t*t)^2, while the Euler column squared length 1 + t*t equals 1 if and only if t = 0. At t = 1 the Cayley value is 4. At t = 2 the Euler squared length is 5 and the inflation (1 + 2*2) - 1 is 4, and the Cayley value is 25. The integer matrix with rows (2, 0) and (0, 3) has entrywise distance 1 from the matrix with rows (2, 0) and (0, 2); the latter has both row sums 2, and the former has row sums 2 and 3, so distance 1 does not authorize an exact scaled stochastic kernel. A general instrument, a general finite path sum, a unitary group, the passage from stochastic kernels to completely positive maps, and every continuum generator stay unproved.

records.obligation: The sufficient packages add explicit structure: a Gaussian-rational linear lift plus finite zero-probability calibration, or nonvanishing plus all-state fixed-frame tomographic statistics. Static Born readout, reversibility, report-swap covariance, norms, basis and real pair statistics and orthogonality are jointly insufficient in dimension two. Campaign hypothesis map on Q(i)^n: a supplied linear lift with finite orthogonality calibration and a nonzero anchor preserves transition probabilities; fixed-frame statistics for all basis, real pair and imaginary pair probes in every nonzero state, together with nonvanishing, also suffice and fix every ray. On Q(i)^2, reversible ray dynamics can preserve norms, basis and real pair statistics, report-swap covariance and orthogonality while changing a transition probability from 9/10 to 1/10. A noncircular operational principle excluding hidden sectors is open; general tensor-cone uniqueness and operational classification remain open (FQ-GAP-TENSOR-UNIQUENESS). records.summary: Under calibration, a nonzero observation and descent of an admitted operation family, irreducibility of that family on the global state space forces injectivity of the observation (Schur-type; tomography_of_irreducible, calibrated_tomography). The existence of such a family is equivalent to local tomography, so this re-expresses rather than derives local tomography. Converse (OperationalFilterFamily): for a calibrated observation, irreducibility of the lifted coordinate (product-test) resets, and descent of all visibly normalized global resets, are each equivalent to local tomography (product_resets_irreducible_iff, global_reset_descent_iff_tomography). Under explicit closure rules (sequential admission, generating cone, preparability of all normalized states, bounded globally separating admitted effects) test-then-prepare resets are constructed as a positive, subnormalized, irreducible family (normalized_reset_family); this construction does not discharge the descent premise non-circularly. With the same-family dimension law K(d,n) = n + d binom(n,2), d > 0, local tomography selects d = 2 (OperationalFieldSelection.selected_parameter). The classical doubled-pair control satisfies calibration, factorization and descent yet violates irreducibility and tomography. Narrowest claim of the filter-family run: Under explicit closure rules (sequential admission, generating cone, preparability of all normalized states, bounded globally separating admitted effects), test-then-prepare resets form a positive, subnormalized, irreducible family. For a calibrated observation, irreducibility of the lifted coordinate resets, and descent of all visibly normalized global resets, are each equivalent to local tomography. So resets cannot non-circularly discharge the descent-plus-irreducibility premise of OperationalTomography.

records.name: forced-separation-lift-not-unique
records.obligation: Refuse any answer to a separation task computed only from the collapsed quotient, require an added separating observation, and keep every tied separating predicate as a branch unless a declared minimality or initiality policy selects one.
records.summary: Suppose an external task requires <a> and <ab> to differ while the current regime has <a> ≈ₙ <ab>. Every operation f on the quotient S_n/≈ₙ gives f([<a>]) = f([<ab>]), so no operation on the current quotient answers the task on every input, and a refinement adding at least one observation o with o(<a>) ≠ o(<ab>) is forced; the analysis gives this as an argument with proof. The lift is not unique: under a supplied string decoder, 'payload has more than one position' and 'payload contains b' both separate <a> from <ab> but disagree on <aa> (true and false), and full inscription identity also separates the pair while carrying more than one bit. A canonical tower therefore needs a declared minimality or initiality policy, such as fewest new predicates, minimum description length, maximal preservation of old equivalences, a free or initial completion, or retention of every tied minimum branch.

records.name: replay-necessity
records.obligation: Reject any auditor that certifies the adopted state from a view π under which two admissible histories with different states coincide, and give it the replayed history or a summary on which σ is constant per fiber.
records.summary: Let H be the possible histories, σ(h) the state that history h produces and π(h) the part of h an auditor sees, for example only the last turn. If π(h₁) = π(h₂) but σ(h₁) ≠ σ(h₂), no auditor A that sees only π reports σ(h) for every h, because A(π(h₁)) = A(π(h₂)) would give σ(h₁) = σ(h₂). The trial failures motivate the theorem: the blind auditor flagged the licensed words 'We' (Trial 1) and 'rule' (Trial 2) as imports, so an audit needs two levels; in Trial 2, Prompt 14's false attribution was answered without objection, so claim provenance is a check separate from claim correctness, Result 15 lost the state, saying the regime contains only <> after <a> had been supplied; and the two-level auditor, shown only that turn, answered None. State certification therefore needs replay information that separates the relevant histories, and on a declared finite population a summary on which σ is constant per fiber of the view can stand in for the raw history.

records.name: metatheory-object-language-split
records.obligation: Keep every glyph, count, order and string-equality test in the metatheory, and let object-language observables read only admitted data indices, forms, instances, rules and requirements.
records.summary: The sealed manuscript declares two levels. The metatheory holds presentation tokens (strings), event sequences, indices, finite data structures and arithmetic; the object language holds only what a regime admits. Token glyphs, component counts, order, concatenation, multiplicity, substring structure, matching and string equality live in the metatheory unless an admitted judgment internalizes a distinction. Presentation identity (token equality) is metatheory only, internal identity is the datum index, and no semantic interpretation is ever assigned.

records.name: regime-isomorphism-unordered-pairs
records.obligation: Compare regimes by datum and form bijections that preserve arities, instances, rules and sorted requirement pairs, with tokens erased, and keep the unordered-requirement convention explicit.
records.summary: A regime isomorphism is a pair of bijections on datum and form indices that preserves form arities, ordered instance arguments, uniform-rule membership and the separation requirements read as unordered pairs; mapped requirement endpoints are sorted before comparison, and presentation tokens are erased first. Because requirements are unordered, exchanging the endpoints of a requirement can identify two responses; a relation preserving directed requirements would be a different convention. The Lean structure Iso states these fields over the admitted index ranges, and sortPair is shown to equal (min, max) and to be symmetric.

records.name: challenge0-inertia-second-token
records.obligation: Show that genesis and every instance-free, rule-free regime derive nothing, and that two admitted data require a datum admission of a token different from the first.
records.summary: At Challenge 0 the only object-language inscription is the opaque whole <>. In the token-erased Lean model nothing is derivable at genesis (genesis_underivable), and nothing is derivable in any regime with no instances and no rules (underivable_of_empty); the Challenge 0 computation records zero contexts and an empty derivable set in both readings. That no successor is internally forced is a property of the declared grammar, whose only state changes are external-event-indexed admissions, not a theorem about a forcing predicate. In the token-aware model a history whose datum admissions all carry one token leaves at most one admitted datum (single_token_carrier_bound), so a state with two data needs the admission of a second, different token (second_token_required).

records.name: contexts-plugging-profiles
records.obligation: Enumerate well-formed contexts with at least one hole, plug by filling every hole with one datum, decide derivability by instance membership or a uniform rule only, and compare profiles.
records.summary: A context is an admitted form with a slot tuple of its arity in which every filled slot names an admitted datum and at least one slot is a hole; plugging a datum fills every hole with that same datum. Derivability is membership in the admitted instances or coverage by a uniform all-tuples rule, and no other inference exists. The profile of a datum is the set of well-formed contexts whose plugging is derivable. Two data are collapsed when their profiles are equal and separable when some well-formed context is derivable for one and not the other; that is the declared sense used for every separation requirement.

records.name: collapse-without-instances
records.obligation: Show that a regime whose instance list is empty collapses every pair of data, whatever its forms and uniform rules.
records.summary: With no admitted instances, the derivability of a plugged context depends only on its form, so every pair of data is observationally collapsed (collapsed_of_no_insts). Uniform rules do not change this: a ruled form makes every plugging derivable alike. Retaining another datum alone therefore need not increase expressive power.

records.name: challenge2-admitted-but-collapsed
records.obligation: Replay the recorded reading L and reading F histories to R2L and R2F, show every admitted pair collapsed in both, and exhibit one datum admission that changes the regime and leaves the pair collapsed.
records.summary: At Challenge 2 both <a> and <ab> are supplied and retained, so reading L admits (<a>, <ab>) and reading F admits (<>, <a>, <ab>). In both readings every admitted pair is observationally collapsed (R2L_collapsed, R2F_collapsed): two externally distinct inscriptions remain internally indistinguishable. The countermodel admission_without_expressive_increase admits a fresh datum, a real state change, while the pair stays collapsed, a counterexample to the claim that a new external inscription necessarily increases internal expressive power. The recorded Challenge 0-3 histories replay exactly to the Challenge 3 regimes R2L and R2F (historyL_replays, historyF_replays).

records.name: context-count-formula
records.obligation: Count the contexts of each admitted form as (n+1)^a − n^a, sum over forms, and check the count against an explicit context enumeration.
records.summary: For a regime with n admitted data, a form of arity a has (n+1)^a − n^a well-formed contexts: each slot is a hole or one of n data, less the n^a hole-free tuples, so |Ctx(R)| = Σ_f ((n+1)^{a_f} − n^{a_f}), with distinct form identifiers kept disjoint even when their arities coincide. The companion Lean module establishes the per-form count for the recursive word enumeration (contextWords_length), characterizes its members as exactly the well-formed words of that length containing a hole (contextWords_mem), and shows the enumeration has no repetitions (contextWords_nodup). The standalone replay checks the formula against the frozen Python enumeration in 35 cases (n from 0 to 4, arity 1 to 7), and Python and Rust enumerate the contexts independently.

Under RegimeExt (equal datum counts and form tables, and membership-equal instance, rule and requirement collections) every stated observable transports: derivability, context well-formedness, collapse, separability, item and delta application, and response validity (derivable_ext through validResponse_ext). records.name: responses-costs-mu1-mu2
records.obligation: Apply response items in order, cost them by mu1 and by lexicographic mu2, and accept a response only when it applies, separates the target and keeps every prior requirement separated.
records.summary: A response (delta) is an ordered finite list of NewDatum, NewForm(arity), NewInst(form, args) and NewRuleAll(form) items applied in order; an instance may name a form added earlier in the same list, and the reverse order is an ill-formed admission. The declared costs are mu1 = item count and mu2 = (item count, sum of new-form arities) compared lexicographically, where the sum counts every NewForm item, including distinct forms of equal arity. A valid response to Separate(i, j) applies, separates the target, and keeps every previously imposed requirement separated, because requirements are persistent constraints.

Instantiating R2L_collapsed and R2F_collapsed, the current regime fails this: no witness context exists. The quotient barrier then applies: every function out of a quotient by a relation is constant on related elements (quotient_barrier, quot_barrier), and on the collapse classes of R2L any operation takes equal values on data 0 and 1 (barrier_R2L). An operation defined only on the current abstraction therefore cannot recover the required distinction, and a response has to change the regime.

records.name: orbit-branching-repairs-least-pair

On the regression regime (four data, one unary form, instances on data 2 and 3) both the regime and its renaming by the double transposition 0↔2, 1↔3 collapse the pair (0, 1), yet the renaming carries (0, 1) to (2, 3) (least_pair_selection_not_congruent); that the two same-index choices give non-isomorphic children is a computational test. The repair branches once per automorphism orbit of collapsed pairs. Under datum renamings with forms fixed, the selection-free transition relation over every collapsed pair and every valid response transports (transStep_rename_fwd, transStep_image_total), and valid-response counts over caller-supplied candidate lists transport (validCount_rename).

Derivability of instances of the old forms is unchanged by this extension, so old witnesses survive (derivable_extend). The standalone replay checks fresh-mark preservation for 3,996 targets across 1,436 regimes, and no terminal_no_response node occurs in any exported run.

records.name: pruning-lemmas-cost-two
records.obligation: Show that rule items never occur in a minimum valid response and that unreferenced fresh data, unreferenced fresh forms and instances not mentioning a target datum cannot change the target pair's collapse.
records.summary: A separation witness never inhabits a uniformly ruled form, so shrinking the final rule set preserves every separation (separable_of_subrules). With the item-level bridge applyDelta_dropRules, a delta containing a uniform-rule item is never minimal: dropping its rule items leaves a valid, strictly shorter delta with the same new-form arity sum (rule_item_never_minimal). The mention lemma shows that appending instances that mention neither datum of a pair leaves that pair's collapse unchanged (collapsed_append_unmentioning), and under the well-formedness conjuncts a fresh unreferenced datum or form leaves the collapse of every existing pair unchanged (collapsed_fresh_datum, collapsed_fresh_form).

records.name: count-invariance-transport

records.summary: Observational collapse is invariant under a renaming of datum indices with forms fixed: the renamed regime collapses the renamed pair exactly when the original regime collapses the original pair (collapsed_rename). For any caller-supplied candidate pair list with deciders that track collapse, the collapsed-pair counts before and after renaming agree (collapsedCount_rename). Collapse also transports across a full two-bijection regime isomorphism (collapsed_transport) and under the combined datum-and-form action (collapsed_renameDataForm). Requirements never enter collapse, so the renaming action leaves them alone.

records.name: policy-endpoint-all-separated

The companion theorem policy_terminal_separates shows that a well-formed policy terminal whose imposed requirements are all separated separates every admitted pair: an unresolved pair would have the fresh-mark response of mark_progress, contradicting terminality. Together with the round bound, an unguarded maximal run of the declared closure policy cannot continue indefinitely and cannot stop on an unresolved pair for lack of a response.

The sealed answer is that no object-language endogenous demand generator was derived: a collapsed pair is not an active obstruction by itself, and the declared closure policy only reissues the admitted requirement pattern. Under that policy the fixed finite datum set reaches the all-pairs-separated fixpoint within n(n−1)/2 rounds, the size of the requirement language (allPairs_length). At the fixpoint no unresolved requirement exists in that language, so any further requirement needs a fresh datum (external supply) or a new requirement kind (external goal).

Worked cases: on the path 0 → 1 → 2, δ = (2, 3) = d₀(0, 2, 5) is exact; on the hollow cyclic triangle (01, 12, 20) every repair of δ = (1, 1, 1) still sums to 3, a quotient obstruction that is not contextuality without a measurement cover and an empirical model.
