records.summary: WDP-CH07-D01: a finite duration gauge is a path system with an additive edge valuation λ: E → M into a commutative monoid, D_λ(p) = Σ_j λ(e_j); positivity, Archimedean structure, units and real values are extra hypotheses, and WDP-CH07-P01 gives D_λ(pq) = D_λ(p) + D_λ(q) whenever pq is defined. Section 7.2 keeps four statuses apart: exact (a displayed t with d₀t = λ), closed nonexact (d₁λ = 0 for a declared d₁ while a period or dual certificate shows λ ∉ im d₀), active closure failure (d₁λ ≠ 0 on an exhibited 2-cell) and exactness undetermined. WDP-CH07-P02: if λ = d₀t, every directed path from a to b has duration t(b) − t(a). The converse needs more than weak connectedness: a base vertex reaching every vertex with path-independent sums, or vanishing periods under signed walks; the difference of two path sums with common endpoints is a period witness, and a nonzero period refutes exactness.

Cancellation gives D_F d₀ = 0, so D_F(e + d₀g) = D_F e even for unbalanced triples, and rationalizing reflects integer repair equality. This is a repair quotient with descending reports, not automatically cohomology: C¹/im d₀ differs from ker D_F/im d₀, a filled mark may be unbalanced, triangle reports miss loops and two-way defects, and antisymmetric simplicial coordinates need e(x, x) = 0 and e(x, y) + e(y, x) = 0. Term addition and identification can fail to respect the quotient (source 23:D4), so carrier-changing operations need new congruence proofs.

records.name: Hierarchical Borel dressing beyond the diamond control
records.obligation: The rooted tree, given by a parent function and a strictly decreasing depth, and the incidence cochain are supplied data. This statement does not construct a spanning tree from an arbitrary graph, does not identify an obstruction with a computed cohomology group, and does not build a 2-plaquette prism. Continuum gauge theory, color transport and smooth patching stay outside this statement.
records.summary: Let B_2(Q) be the invertible upper-triangular 2x2 matrices over Q, T the diagonal matrices and N the unit upper-triangular matrices. Every invertible element factors uniquely as D * n with D in T and n in N, and conjugation of an element of N by an invertible element stays in N. torusProj preserves multiplication. On any vertex type with a root, a parent function and a depth function that strictly decreases along parents, and for invertible labels off the root, root-to-vertex transport multiplies labels on the left: T(root) = I and T(v) = U(v) * T(parent(v)). The stage-one field u_N(v) equals D(v) * n(v)^{-1} * D(v)^{-1}, lies in N, and equals [[1, -b(v)/d2(v)], [0, 1]]. Dressing a tree edge by u_N yields D(child) * D(parent)^{-1}. For every label g and every pair of vertices, torusProj(u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) equals torusProj(g). A further diagonal vertex field, multiplied on the left at the child and on the right by its inverse at the parent, leaves that dressed tree edge diagonal. The stage-two field u_T(v) = D(v)^{-1} satisfies u_T(v) * u_N(v) = T(v)^{-1}, and u_T(target) * (u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) * u_T(source)^{-1} equals T(target)^{-1} * g * T(source). That dressed label equals I if and only if g = T(target) * T(source)^{-1}. A vertex field that is invertible at every vertex, equals I at the root, and satisfies U(v) = g(v) * g(parent(v))^{-1} off the root, equals the rooted transport. The factorization identity fails on [[0, 1], [0, 1]]. Replacing the (2, 2) entry by 1 does not preserve the product of [[2, 1], [0, 3]] with itself. On any commutative ring, the operators (bA)(u, v, w) = -A(u, w) and (A smile A)(u, v, w) = A(u, v) * A(v, w) satisfy b composed with b equal to 0, the Bianchi identity for K = bA + A smile A, and endpoint gauge covariance K(A^g) = g(u) * K(A) * g(w)^{-1} when A^g(x, y) = g(x) * A(x, y) * g(y)^{-1}. For A(0,1)=1, A(1,2)=1, A(0,2)=0, g(0)=1 and g(1)=2, the source-only expression (g(0)*A(0,1))*(g(1)*A(1,2)) - (g(0)*A(0,2)) is not equal to g(0)*(A(0,1)*A(1,2) - A(0,2)). The same values with g(2)=1 and g(1)^{-1}=1/2 satisfy the endpoint identity. The arithmetic comparison of 2 with 3 records that these integers differ. On the four-vertex tree with parents 0, 0, 0, 2, transport at vertex 3 equals U(3) * U(2).

records.summary: Given d+1 MUB projector resolutions on a d-dimensional complex Hilbert carrier and trace-one rho, the probabilities p_bj=tr(rho P_bj) reconstruct rho as sum_bj p_bj P_bj minus I.

records.name: Dimension-six MUB reductions and global obligations
records.obligation: Discharge every coverage, chart and conditional bridge premise before making a global dimension-six conclusion. Update 2026-10-21: N(6) <= 5 is available only as an imported external theorem (MUB6-OPENAI-FAMILY-LE-FIVE); the exclusion of a quartet and the value N(6) = 3 remain open here.
records.summary: Separate exact stated-region exclusions and conditional reductions from a global dimension-six existence or maximality theorem; the package leaves G1 open.

records.name: Signed-graph switching normal form and class count
records.obligation: Retain fixed labels and vertex-switching equivalence; this canonicalizer is not a normal form under arbitrary many-body basis transformations.
records.summary: For a fixed labelled finite graph and supplied spanning forest, vertex sign switching has a canonical tree-zero representative determined by chord signs. NF-002 records a duplicate-free enumeration of length 2^numChord and numChord=|E|-|V|+c.

records.name: Meron character cancellation on a supplied flip orbit
records.obligation: Supply invariant weight magnitudes, valid flip action and compatible observables before using the sign identity as a model reduction.
records.summary: The finite flip-orbit sign sum is zero when at least one meron flag is true, and is 2^k when all k flags are false. Weighted partition and observable reductions require additional orbit hypotheses.

records.name: Protected Hubbard representations and negative witnesses
records.obligation: Prove the required determinant pairing and Hamiltonian-to-representation equality for each stated model, including boundary cases.
records.summary: Hubbard determinant positivity is restricted to the package stated half-filled bipartite or attractive spin-balanced hypotheses; exact negative fields outside those protections remain distinct witnesses.

records.name: Efficient sampling and general FSP obligations
records.obligation: Define input size, transformation cost, estimator variance, normalization and mixing or sampling bounds for the chosen model family.
records.summary: Canonical sign representatives, finite cancellation and nonnegative determinant weights do not establish an efficient sampler or a general fermion sign-problem solution.

records.name: Composite coordinates from local operational statistics
records.obligation: Lean verifies Hermitian product spanning, nondegenerate trace pairing, finite dual-frame reconstruction, injectivity, surjectivity, uniqueness, and process calibration. Local complex QM and the operational bilinear/tomography premises remain supplied. The displayed positive projector-basis formula and SEP/BP commentary are prose corollaries, not additional Lean claims.
records.summary: Independent bilinear preparations and tests with trace-factorized product probabilities and local tomography construct a unique real linear equivalence with joint Hermitian matrices for arbitrary finite local complex dimensions. The equivalence preserves products and all product tests; the deterministic product test is trace. The joint state cone is not assumed.

records.name: Positive cone selection by preparations and transported tests
records.obligation: The general finite-index cone kernel retains explicit OrbitData assumptions. TensorOperationalCone now instantiates its transports and reachability using the proved Schmidt controlled-shift construction; TensorComposition connects that instance to the constructed operational coordinates.
records.summary: For any finite complex matrix size, a Hermitian set containing zero and closed under addition equals PSD when seed preparations and positive seed tests are transported by preserving operations whose seed-vector orbits cover all vectors.

records.name: Quantum composition from a calibrated reversible controlled shift
records.obligation: Lean constructs complete rectangular Schmidt bases, local unitaries and one modular controlled shift, then checks the operational state cone. TFQ-0414--TFQ-0416 check the generated effect cone, binary interval and finite POVMs with explicit effect and finite-test saturation premises. Calibration and operational preservation remain supplied; primitive difference has not supplied these hypotheses.
records.summary: For arbitrary finite n<=m with m nonzero (the smaller subsystem is the control), supplied local complex QM, independent bilinear preparation/testing, local tomography, positive product tests, finite-sum state closure, and calibrated local-unitary and reversible controlled-shift preservation force the represented state cone to be PSD(nm). Tomographic coordinates, Schmidt reachability, cone equality and trace normalization are verified in Lean.

records.name: Countermodels and the interaction assumption boundary
records.obligation: Countermodels delimit weakened hypotheses, not logical minimality of the sufficient package. No primitive derivation, arbitrary-GPT classification, operational saturation, or new proof of SEP closedness is claimed. The identical-qubit family classification remains external.
records.summary: Full SEP/BP duality, local preservation and binary-product tomography do not select PSD: exact Bell/partial-transpose separations embed into every n,m>=2. Two-qubit ordinary, twisted and dephased controlled shifts separate calibrated preservation, coherent calibration and reversibility despite matching classical tables. A doubled positive carrier has distinct normalized states with identical product statistics.

records.name: Generated operational effect cone
records.obligation: Operational soundness, local binary product availability and reversible effect pullback closure remain explicit premises. The generated cone does not identify the available binary interval or available finite tests.
records.summary: The conic hull of represented available effects equals PSD for arbitrary finite n<=m with m nonzero, using the verified state cone, sound effects, all local binary product tests and calibrated local-unitary and controlled-shift pullbacks. Neither effect saturation nor finite-test saturation is required.

records.name: Binary effects and explicit effect saturation
records.obligation: EffectSaturated is a separate no-restriction premise, not a consequence of state-cone or generated-effect-cone equality. Local complex QM and the state-reconstruction assumptions remain supplied.
records.summary: The constructed dual representation identifies functionals satisfying 0<=e(x)<=u(x) on the state cone with Hermitian matrices 0<=E<=I. Homogeneous bounds are equivalent to probabilities in [0,1] on all trace-one PSD states. Soundness plus explicit EffectSaturated identifies the available binary effects with this full interval.

records.name: Finite POVMs and separate test saturation
records.obligation: FiniteTestSaturated requires jointly implementing each finite family of available effects summing to the deterministic unit. It is distinct from individual effect saturation. No availability or classification of instruments or channels is asserted.
records.summary: For any finite outcome type, sound available tests correspond to positive Hermitian families summing to I. Conversely every such POVM is available under both EffectSaturated and the separate FiniteTestSaturated premise. The end-to-end quantum_measurements theorem invokes quantum_state_cone and returns the generated cone, binary interval and finite-POVM equivalence.

records.name: Tree and chord coordinates of a connection: triangle Mat2 witness
records.obligation: The general bijection (u_T on V minus the root, dressed chords) <-> H^{|E|} for every finite connected graph and group is stated in the dossier without proof and is not in Lean; the general neutralization and residual statements are TFQ-0398 and TFQ-0399.
records.summary: On the triangle graph with tree edges 01, 12 and chord 02, for rational 2x2 matrices with right inverses and an anchored gauge (1, G1, G2), the rooted tree dressing sends both gauged tree links to the identity and sends the gauged chord to U02 U12^{-1} U01^{-1}, the ungauged rooted cycle holonomy.

records.name: Abelian tree-dressing projector on rational 1-cochains
records.obligation: Keep the root, the tree, the edge orientations and the additive group (Q, +) explicit; this is the additive case of TFQ-0397.
records.summary: For a finite connected graph with coboundary (d_0 lambda)_(u,v) = lambda(v) - lambda(u) and a rooted spanning tree T, u_T[A](v) is the signed sum of A along the tree path from the root, and Pi_T(A) = A - d_0 u_T[A] on C^1(G; Q).

records.name: Abelian tree retraction on the diamond graph
records.obligation: Idempotence and the chord-equals-cycle-holonomy clause are not separately checked; the general statement for all graphs is the (Q,+) specialization of TFQ-0398 and TFQ-0399 and should be cited from there.
records.summary: On the diamond graph (4 vertices, 5 edges, b_1 = 2) with the rational connection (3,-5,2,11,-4)/7 and one rational vertex gauge, for each of the 8 spanning trees Pi_T vanishes on the 3 tree edges and Pi_T(A + d_0 lambda) = Pi_T(A).

records.name: Unimodular tree change and first Symanzik polynomial on the diamond
records.obligation: The general claims (tree change acts by GL(b_1, Z); det L_T(alpha) = U_G(alpha) for every graph and positive alpha) are the classical matrix-tree theorem and are cited, not proved here.
records.summary: On the diamond graph, the 2x2 chord-coordinate matrix from a fixed tree T_0 to each of the 8 trees has determinant +1 or -1, and det(C_T diag(alpha) C_T^T) = U_G(alpha) = 247 for every tree at alpha = (2,3,5,7,11), with U_G(1,...,1) = 8.

records.name: Eight omitted-edge products on the five-edge diamond sum to 247
records.obligation: The edges and the weights are supplied. These eight subsets are one graph, not a theorem for every graph. The QED loop coefficients, the fine-structure constant, and continuum Feynman-parameter integrals stay open.
records.summary: The graph with vertices {0,1,2,3} and edges e0=(0,1), e1=(0,2), e2=(1,3), e3=(2,3), e4=(1,2) has exactly eight connected 3-edge subsets among its ten 3-edge subsets. For weights 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 on those edges in that order, the sum of the products of the two omitted weights over those eight subsets is 247, and the same sum with every weight 1 is 8. A rational interval around a 1-to-4-loop QED anomalous-moment series stays open.

records.name: Borel group B_2(Q), unipotent N and torus Levi factorization
records.obligation: Uniqueness of the factorization and quotient preservation for a supplied rooted tree are recorded at TFQ-0400. Extracting a spanning tree from an arbitrary graph is outside that record.
records.summary: B_2(Q) is the group of invertible upper-triangular rational 2x2 matrices, N its unipotent normal subgroup and T_2(Q) the diagonal torus; a tree holonomy [[a,b],[0,d]] factors as [[1,b/d],[0,1]] diag(a,d), giving the stage-1 dressing u_N and stage-2 dressing t.

records.name: Two-stage Borel dressing and artificial/substantial split on the diamond
records.obligation: Rooted-tree two-stage identities and the specified incidence operators are recorded at TFQ-0400. A 2-plaquette prism, and a criterion for a graph that does not supply a parent and a depth, stay outside TFQ-0400 and outside TFQ-0016.
records.summary: On the diamond graph with one fixed tree, a pure-gauge B_2(Q) connection built from one rational vertex map is dressed to the identity on all 5 edges, and a connection with one chord multiplied by [[2,1],[0,3]] is dressed to the identity on tree edges and to a non-identity chord; stage-1 fields lie in N, stage-1 tree links are diagonal, and stage 2 reproduces the one-shot dressing.

records.name: Tree momentum routing and second Symanzik 2-forest polynomial
records.obligation: Keep the metric on Q^d, the sign convention for p_T and the mass term of F_G explicit.
records.summary: For external momenta q_v in Q^d with sum zero and a spanning tree T, p_T(e) is minus the total momentum on one side of e for e in T and 0 on chords; F_0(alpha; q) is the sum over spanning 2-forests (F, V_1, V_2) of prod_{e not in F} alpha_e times |sum_{v in V_1} q_v|^2.

records.name: Tree-routed completed square equals F_0 on the diamond
records.obligation: The equality for every graph, dimension d and massive F_G is a classical parametric identity that is cited, not proved; only d = 2 and one momentum assignment are checked.
records.summary: On the diamond graph with alpha = (2,3,5,7,11) and four fixed external momenta in Q^2, the 2-forest enumeration has 10 forests and F_0 = 31153, and for each of the 8 spanning trees U_G (sum over tree-routed energies minus loop correction) equals 31153 with det L_T = 247.

records.name: Four-forest subtraction on a rational two-parameter sector kernel
records.obligation: The identity is distributivity on one declared toy kernel; it is not Zimmermann's forest formula on a Feynman integrand and fixes no renormalization scheme.
records.summary: For K(z; lambda) = (1 + z lambda) / (lambda (1 + lambda)) at z = 3/5, the four-term sum K1(z)K2(z) - K1(z)K2(0) - K1(0)K2(z) + K1(0)K2(0) equals (z/(1+lambda_1))(z/(1+lambda_2)) at 9 rational (lambda_1, lambda_2) pairs, with formal value z^2 = 9/25 at (0, 0).

records.name: Continuum BPHZ and momentum integration remain outside the finite map
records.obligation: The six-forest count, the order-0 collapse, and the quotient 7 are recorded only for these three edge sets and this numerator. A forest formula on actual Feynman-parametric integrands, a subtraction operator of positive degree, and a convergence statement before continuum integration remain open. The nested sector kernel at z = 3/5 gives 9/50, which is a different identity.
records.summary: On the declared overlapping edge sets L = {0,1,2}, R = {2,3,4} and G = {0,1,2,3,4}, a Zimmermann forest is a subset whose members are pairwise nested or disjoint, and the forests are exactly the six subsets in which L and R do not both occur. For the order-0 evaluations T_L I(x,y) = I(0,y), T_R I(x,y) = I(x,0) and T_G I(x,y) = I(0,0), the signed six-forest sum equals I(x,y) - I(0,y) - I(x,0) + I(0,0). For the declared numerator N(x,y) = 2 + 3x + 5y + 7xy that sum is 7xy, so the quotient by xy equals 7 wherever xy is nonzero. The three-forest sum that omits G equals 7xy - 2, and its quotient is 7 - 2/(xy). At (x,y) = (1/2, 1/3) the two quotients are 7 and -5. Algebraic cancellation for actual Feynman-parametric integrands, and any use of this identity before continuum integration, is not established.

records.obligation: Four-component spinors with gamma^0, the tree-change holonomy factor and arbitrary graphs are not checked; the general U(1) case is a specialization of TFQ-0398 and TFQ-0399.

records.obligation: The identity is checked by exact arithmetic only at p = (5,1,2,-1), q = (2,-1,1,3), m = 2 together with the Clifford relations of the Dirac basis; no Lean witness.

records.name: One rational vertex contraction, not a counterterm ratio
records.obligation: The recorded check is this inverse-propagator identity and one rational loop momentum. A gauge-invariant BPHZ subtraction scheme and continuum loop integration stay imported, so Z_1/Z_2 remains conditional.
records.summary: For every integer momentum pair and every integer mass, (slash(p+q) - m I) - (slash(p) - m I) = slash(q), where slash(v) = v0 g0 - v1 g1 - v2 g2 - v3 g3 in the stated Dirac representation. At p = (2, 0, 0, 0), q = (1, 0, 0, 1), loop momentum 0 and mass 1, S(p) = (slash(p) + I)/3 and S(p+q) = (slash(p+q) + I)/7 satisfy S(p+q) slash(q) S(p) = S(p) - S(p+q), and the lowered contraction q_mu I_Lambda^mu equals I_Sigma(p) - I_Sigma(p+q). That matrix has diagonal entries 2/7, 2/7, 26/21, 26/21 and off-diagonal entries (0,2)=-2/7, (1,3)=2/7, (2,0)=2/7, (3,1)=-2/7, with indices starting at 0. The counterterm equality Z_1/Z_2 = 1 is not proved.

records.name: Clock dressing intertwines the history shift
records.obligation: Exact checks exist only for N = 4, d = 2, U_S = [[0,-1],[1,0]] and psi_0 = (3/5, 4/5); no Lean witness.
records.summary: If U_S is unitary with U_S^N = I_d, then D^dagger W D = S_C tensor I_d, and D^dagger sends each history state sum_t |t> tensor U_S^t psi_0 in ker(I - W) to (sum_t |t>) tensor psi_0.

records.name: Finite-clock closure and reversible history coordinates
records.obligation: The group, links, action, step and vector are supplied. General finite-cycle transport and its closure criterion are established for these inputs; deriving them from primitive difference, continuous time, a one-parameter unitary group and a Hamiltonian constraint stay open.
records.summary: For U = [[0, -1], [1, 0]] over Q, U^2 = -I, U^4 = I, and U^T U = I. For each t in {0, 1, 2, 3}, (U^{t+1})^T U U^t = I. For psi = (3/5, 4/5), psi·psi = 1 and (U^t)^T (U^t psi) = psi for each such t, while the first components of U psi and of U^2 psi differ from 3/5. A continuous-time reading, a Stone generator, and a Wheeler-DeWitt constraint stay unproved. For a supplied group-valued schedule, cumulative transport transforms by inverse terminal frame and initial frame, and a periodic frame cancels all edges iff total transport is identity. Normalized cycle blocks are identity on interior edges and total transport on the closing edge. A checked positive-period constructor returns a closure certificate or a distinct zero-period/nonclosure error. Supplied group actions admit an invertible change of history coordinates preserving the evolution law.

records.obligation: Keep v rational and nonzero, and keep the hypercharge normalization (dossier Q = T_3 + Y, documentation Q = T_3 + Y/2) stated.

records.obligation: Unitarity and det = 1 of the complex u(Phi), the covariance u(g_L Phi) = g_L u(Phi), and SU(2)_L invariance of the dressed W are not in Lean or Python.

records.name: Rational Weinberg projectors and custodial rho = 1
records.obligation: M_Z^2 as the nonzero eigenvalue and the tree-level reading of rho are definitions in the file, not derived from a Lagrangian.

records.name: One-generation hypercharge anomaly polynomials vanish iff N_c = 3
records.obligation: These are polynomial identities over Q, not triangle-diagram anomaly computations; the dossier prints the cubic trace as (3/4)(3 - N_c) and the change log as 6 A_grav = 6(N_c - 3), both inconsistent with Lean, which is retained.

records.name: Electroweak dressing: residual U(1) covariance and the continuum Standard Model
records.obligation: The normalized residual law is recorded when z lies in Q(i), the squared modulus of z is 1, and a rational s with s*s equal to the doublet squared norm is supplied. Continuum gauge fields W_mu, derivatives, phases outside Q(i), and the Elitzur or symmetry-breaking reading stay open.
records.summary: For every z in Q(i) and every doublet Phi in Q(i)^2, the un-normalized dressing U(Phi) = [[conj phi2, phi1], [-conj phi1, phi2]] satisfies U(z Phi) = U(Phi) diag(conj z, z). When the squared modulus of z is 1 and a rational s with s*s equal to the squared norm of Phi is supplied, dividing every entry by that same s preserves the identity and s*s equals the squared norm of z Phi. On Phi = (1, 0), the unit z = 3/5 + (4/5)i with s = 1 has normalized (1, 2) entry 3/5 + (4/5)i. On the same Phi, z = 2 has squared norms 1 and 4. The (1, 2) entry of U(2 Phi)/2 is 1, whereas the (1, 2) entry of (U(Phi)/1) diag(2, 2) is 2; these two sides of the proposed normalized covariance law differ. Continuum phases, the dressed derivative term, and an electroweak reading without a declared rational square root stay unproved.

records.name: Bipartite flavour graph rephasing and Jarlskog plaquettes
records.obligation: Keep the phases in the unit circle of Q(i) or declare the larger field.

records.summary: For Gaussian rationals with v11 conj(v21) + v12 conj(v22) = 0, the quartet v11 v22 conj(v12) conj(v21) has imaginary part 0 and real part -|v12|^2 |v22|^2.

records.name: Pythagorean three-generation Jarlskog witness

records.name: CKM origin and physical CP violation stay outside the flavour-graph map
records.obligation: Yukawa couplings, mass-basis diagonalization, a unitarity identification of the counting polynomials, and measured CKM values stay open. The general nonzero-label table classification uses supplied commutative-group rescalings; its restriction to physical unitary mixing matrices is not established.
records.summary: For every rational n, (n - 1)^2 - n(n - 1)/2 = (n - 1)(n - 2)/2 and (n - 1)(n - 2)/2 + (n - 1) = n(n - 1)/2. At n = 1, 2, 3, 4 the polynomial (n - 1)^2 has values 0, 1, 4, 9 and (n - 1)(n - 2)/2 has values 0, 0, 1, 3; they agree at n = 1 and differ at n = 2, 3, 4. At n = 3 the three values are 4, 3, and 1. The quartet of four ones in Q(i) has imaginary part 0, and the quartet with second factor i has imaginary part 1, so the CP value 1 matches only the second. Derivation of a mixing matrix from Yukawa couplings, a unitarity identification of these counts, and measured CP values stay unproved.

records.name: Two generator quadratic forms on Omega1 differ
records.obligation: The recorded comparison is this pair of quadratic forms on two generators of one diagonal matrix. A refinement family of lattices, an operator spectrum, and a limit theorem stay open before any continuum transport.
records.summary: For the rational matrices I = diag(1, 1, 1), Omega1 = diag(1, -1, -1), H23 with ones in positions (2, 3) and (3, 2), and H12 with ones in positions (1, 2) and (2, 1), H23^2 = diag(0, 1, 1), H12^2 = diag(1, 1, 0), Omega1^2 = I, the product of Omega1's diagonal entries is 1, Tr(I) = 3, Tr(Omega1) = -1, Tr(I H23^2) = 2, Tr(Omega1 H23^2) = -2, and Tr(Omega1 H12^2) = 0, so those two Omega1 forms differ. records.name: Rational Lorentz boosts, simplex tetrads and dressed affine transport
records.obligation: Keep the frame action e -> L e and Omega -> L Omega L'^{-1} explicit.
records.summary: Lambda(beta) for rational beta in (-1, 1) is the boost with entries (1+beta^2)/(1-beta^2) and 2 beta/(1-beta^2); each 4-simplex carries e_sigma in GL(4, Q), each shared tetrahedron Omega in SO+(1,3; Q); g_sigma = e^T eta e, Gamma = e_sigma^{-1} Omega e_sigma', and H_h is the ordered product of Gamma around a hinge.

records.name: Boost-plane Lorentz invariance of the tetrad metric
records.obligation: The 4x4 statements, the velocity-addition group law and general SO+(1,3; Q) frames are not in Lean.
records.summary: For rational beta with 1 - beta^2 != 0, the 2x2 boost-plane matrix Lambda(beta) has determinant 1, Lambda(beta) Lambda(-beta) = I, Lambda^T eta_2 Lambda = eta_2, and e^T eta_2 e is unchanged when the 2x2 frame e is replaced by Lambda(-beta) e.

records.name: Frame-invariant, metric-compatible dressed transport
records.obligation: Exact 4x4 checks exist for two fixed tetrads, one boost-rotation frame change and Omega = Lambda(1/2), with the group law at beta = 1/3, 1/2; no Lean witness in dimension 4.
records.summary: For invertible rational tetrads and Omega in SO+(1,3; Q), Gamma = e_sigma^{-1} Omega e_sigma' is unchanged under independent frame changes (L_sigma, L_sigma') and satisfies Gamma^T g_sigma Gamma = g_sigma'.

records.name: Artificial versus substantial hinge holonomy witness
records.obligation: No simplicial complex, edge lengths or deficit angles are constructed, and the Bianchi check is a telescoping identity, not curvature on actual 3-cell boundaries.
records.summary: A telescoping product of pure-gauge frame factors is I_4; Lambda(1/2) Lambda(1/3) Lambda(-1/3) has 4x4 trace 16/3 (boost-plane trace 10/3) and the same trace after tetrad conjugation; the product of three telescoping conjugated factors around a declared 3-cell is I_4.

records.name: Cosine-law data for lengths 3, 4, 5 differs from block trace 16/3
records.obligation: The lengths 3, 4, 5 and beta = 1/2 are supplied data. The block trace is not computed from those lengths. A 4D complex, a deficit angle, a spin-frame dressing, and a continuum reading stay open.
records.summary: For every rational a, b, c, the cosine-law numerators b^2+c^2-a^2, a^2+c^2-b^2 and a^2+b^2-c^2 sum to a^2+b^2+c^2. At lengths 3, 4 and 5 the numerators opposite sides 5, 3 and 4 respectively are 0, 32 and 18, the cosine-law values are 0, 4/5 and 3/5, and those values sum to 7/5. At beta = 1/2 the denominator 1-beta^2 is nonzero, (1+beta^2)/(1-beta^2) = 5/3, 2 beta/(1-beta^2) = 4/3, and the block trace 2(1+beta^2)/(1-beta^2)+2 equals 16/3, which differs from 4 and from 7/5. A 4D Regge complex, a deficit angle, a Spin+ spin-frame dressing, and a continuum gravity reading stay unproved.

records.name: F2 parity schedule on a declared finite cochain complex
records.obligation: The complex and its incidence matrices are declared inputs; nothing here derives them from a device or from the trunk window.
records.summary: A parity schedule is a declared finite cochain complex C0 -d0-> C1 -d1-> C2 over F2 given by binary incidence matrices with d1 d0 = 0 mod 2; C0 holds vertex gauge flips, C1 edge parity residuals, C2 plaquette syndromes.

records.name: Exact, ClosedResidual and OpenObstruction residual predicates
records.obligation: These are diagnostic schedule classes only; their relation to FOC terminals is fenced by TFQ-0181.
records.summary: For a residual w in C1: Exact means w = d0 a for some a in C0; ClosedResidual means d1 w = 0 and w is not Exact; OpenObstruction means d1 w is nonzero.

records.name: Logical cohomology H1 and Hamming coset weight Phi1 over F2
records.obligation: This is the unit-weight binary specialization of the trunk Phi1 quotient seminorm; the coefficient change from weighted l1 to F2 Hamming weight is declared, not derived.
records.summary: H1 = ker d1 / im d0 over F2, and the quotient residual mass of a class is Phi1([r]) = min over a in C0 of wt(r + d0 a), the Hamming weight of a lightest coset representative.

records.name: Pairwise exclusion of the three residual labels
records.obligation: Exhaustiveness (each residual has at least one label) is not stated in Lean; it is the prose record MAJ-THM-TRICHOTOMY-EXHAUSTIVE.
records.summary: For every declared F2 cochain complex (with d1 d0 = 0 as a structure field) every Exact residual is a cocycle, and no residual satisfies two of Exact, ClosedResidual and OpenObstruction.

records.name: Residual trichotomy partitions C1
records.obligation: A Lean exhaustiveness lemma (a classical case split on d1 w = 0 and on membership in im d0) is absent from MajoranaCore.lean.
records.summary: Since im d0 is contained in ker d1, C1 is the disjoint union of im d0, ker d1 minus im d0, and C1 minus ker d1, so each residual carries exactly one of the three labels.

records.name: Polynomial decision of the residual class by F2 elimination
records.obligation: No Lean statement of the algorithm or its operation count exists; gaussian_elimination_cubic_bound is a reflexivity and must not be cited for this theorem.
records.summary: Given d0, d1 and w over F2, compute s = d1 w (OpenObstruction if s is nonzero), otherwise solve d0 a = w by Gaussian elimination (Exact if solvable, ClosedResidual if not); this uses polynomially many bit operations, O(E (V + F)^2) by the body's count.

records.name: RepresentationInvalid refusal when d1 d0 is nonzero
records.obligation: The refusal is a rule of the procedure; the Lean lemma only records that a violating vector falsifies the nilpotency predicate.
records.summary: If the declared matrices have d1 d0 nonzero mod 2 (or a residual of the wrong length is supplied), the evaluator emits RepresentationInvalid and assigns no residual class.

records.name: Worked 2x2 periodic plaquette grid
records.obligation: Fixed instance only; it does not establish the classification on other grids.
records.summary: On the 2x2 periodic grid (V = 4, E = 8, F = 4) rank d0 = rank d1 = 3 and dim H1 = 2; the two declared logical cycles are ClosedResidual, a single edge is OpenObstruction, and a d0 column is Exact.

records.name: Local green, global red on the 2x2 torus schedule
records.obligation: The general surface statement (every carrier with a non-contractible cycle with dim H1 > 0 has such a residual) is only argued in prose.
records.summary: On the 2x2 torus the logical cycle torus_logical_x has d1 w = 0 on every plaquette yet classifies ClosedResidual (not Exact); on the triangle an exact residual and an open residual are not LGGR.

records.name: Exact syndrome-recovery criterion for an admitted error set
records.obligation: Lean or exact-code witness of the criterion is absent; the recovery model (deterministic decoder seeing only Qe, success meaning the residual lies in B) is declared in the proof.
records.summary: For B = im d0, Q = d1 and an admitted error set E in C1, a syndrome-only recovery succeeds for every e in E if and only if (E + E) intersected with ker Q is contained in B.

records.name: Weight-t errors are recoverable iff 2t < d
records.obligation: Write the two-direction weight argument from Theorem 4.4 (sum of two weight-t errors has weight at most 2t; a weight-d logical splits into two weight-at-most-t halves when d <= 2t); the Knill-Laflamme correspondence is cited, not derived.
records.summary: With d = min{wt(z) : z in ker Q minus B}, the weight-bounded set E_t = {e : wt(e) <= t} satisfies the recovery criterion if and only if 2t < d.

records.name: Lieb-Robinson extension of syndrome detectability
records.obligation: No such bound is stated or derived; the source says the papers do not yet justify a general verdict.
records.summary: Which distinctions a local system can detect, preserve or repair within a specified time may admit a Lieb-Robinson quantitative extension supporting conditional statements on quantum computing viability.

records.name: Surface-code shadows are diagnostic schedules, not threshold proofs
records.obligation: Any threshold or fault-tolerance theorem for a physical device remains outside this record.
records.summary: Multi-plaquette surface-code models and the FTQC dictionary (error to residual, correctable to Exact, logical to ClosedResidual, detectable to OpenObstruction, distance to declared distance) are diagnostic software schedules, not physical noise processes, threshold certificates or fault-tolerance proofs.

records.name: Parameterized tetron-array carriers (disk, cylinder, torus)
records.obligation: A tetron here is a 2-cell of a declared combinatorial carrier under an idealized corner-shared layout, not a superconducting island.
records.summary: A rows x cols tetron array takes MZM sites as vertices on a (rows or rows+1) x (cols or cols+1) grid, nearest-neighbour channels as edges and the rows x cols islands as 2-cells, with no wrap (disk), column wrap (cylinder) or both wraps (torus).

records.name: Computed dim H1 = 0, 1, 2 on disk, cylinder and torus tetron arrays
records.obligation: Fixed sizes only; a closed-form proof for all rows and cols is absent.
records.summary: For sizes 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 3x4, 4x4, 5x5, 6x6, 6x8 and 8x8, F2 row reduction gives dim H1 = (E - rank d1) - rank d0 = 0 (disk), 1 (cylinder), 2 (torus), agreeing with (2 if closed else 1) minus the Euler characteristic, with d1 d0 = 0.

records.name: Trivial H1 admits no ClosedResidual
records.obligation: None for the lemma; its use on the legacy carrier needs the legacy dim H1 = 0 measurement (MAJ-C13).
records.summary: If every cocycle of a declared F2 cochain complex is exact, then no residual is ClosedResidual.

records.name: Retraction of the legacy tetron carrier
records.obligation: The legacy carrier and its dim H1 = 0 computation are not in this checkout; the hypothesis is a change-log record.
records.summary: Given the recorded measurement that legacy tetron_carrier.py had dim H1 = 0 at T = 1..4, every closed residual on it was Exact, so its results support no statement about logical sectors and are superseded by the tetron-array family.

records.name: Per-class minimum weights 3, 4, 7 and distance 3 on the 3x4 torus
records.obligation: Fixed instance only; additivity and d = min(rows, cols) for other sizes are MAJ-CLAIM-DISTANCE-FAMILY.
records.summary: On the 3x4 tetron torus (12 sites, 24 channels, 12 islands) exhaustive Gray-code coset search gives Phi1 = 3 for the column class, 4 for the row class and 7 for their sum, all ClosedResidual, so the distance of that instance is 3.

records.name: Distance formulas for the tetron-array families
records.obligation: Prove the distance formulas (e.g. by a cut argument on the dual grid); the source gives a one-sentence traversal argument for additivity only.
records.summary: For all sizes the torus distance is min(rows, cols), the cylinder distance is rows + 1, and the diagonal class weight is rows + cols.

records.name: Coset-weight decoding is NP-hard for general binary codes
records.obligation: Literature result; no reduction is formalized or replayed here.
records.summary: Minimum-weight coset decoding of a binary linear code given by its matrix is NP-hard (Berlekamp, McEliece and van Tilborg 1978).

records.name: Computing Phi1 is coset-leader decoding of im d0
records.obligation: The hardness rests on the import; the identification with coset decoding is definitional; what holds for graph-incidence d0 of declared cell complexes is not analysed.
records.summary: Phi1([r]) is the coset-leader weight of r for the binary code im d0, so with d0 ranging over all binary matrices exact Phi1 inherits the imported NP-hardness; restricted families such as planar or toric incidence matrices may admit polynomial decoders.

records.name: Budget-capped coset search returns a flagged upper bound
records.obligation: Fixed instances; the upper-bound property of any searched representative is immediate from the definition of the minimum.
records.summary: When 2^rank(d0) exceeds the declared budget the Gray-code search stops, returns the lightest weight found with exact = False, and the Rust terminal drops from TypedHarmonic to ClosedResidual; checked on the 3x4 torus (budget 4, capped weight >= exact weight) and the 4x4 torus (budget 16).

records.name: 6x6 torus classification timing and budget overflow
records.obligation: The body's 17 ms figure is not recorded in this checkout; the timed residual exits at the syndrome step, so the elimination step is not timed; timing is machine-dependent.
records.summary: On the 6x6 tetron torus (V = 36, E = 72, dim H1 = 2, rank d0 = 35) a weight-one residual classifies OpenObstruction within a 100 ms test bound in Rust and Python, and the full coset 2^35 exceeds the 2^20 search budget.

records.name: L^p norms coincide with Hamming weight on binary carriers
records.obligation: The Lean declaration does not state this identity; a Lean lemma over p-th powers of 0/1 entries is absent.
records.summary: For v with entries in {0, 1} and p >= 1, the sum of |v_i|^p equals wt(v), so l1 and l2^2 coset minimizations over F2 have identical objectives and minimizers; dim H1 >= 2 gives distinct logical classes, not a norm gap.

records.name: The Majorana problem as a realization packet gap
records.obligation: A validated realization map from a device to a declared complex is not supplied by this source.
records.summary: The Majorana problem is the gap between continuum open-system device narratives (nanowires, zero-bias peaks, interferometric parity readout) and declared finite algebraic schedules (F2 cochain homology, Ising matrices): neither discharges the verification conditions of the other without an explicit realization map.

records.name: DETECTOR_INADEQUATE for a non-injective measurement map
records.obligation: Which laboratory maps M are adequate is the open program MAJ-OPEN-EVIDENCE-ADEQUACY.
records.summary: A measurement projection M is DETECTOR_INADEQUATE for a hypothesis pair when two distinct candidate states have the same readout (rho1 - rho2 in ker M), so the protocol cannot discriminate them.

records.name: Syndrome-only readout is inadequate on the 2x2 tetron torus
records.obligation: Fixed instance; the adequacy of a syndrome-plus-class readout is asserted, not computed.
records.summary: On the 2x2 tetron torus the column and row logical representatives are distinct cochains with equal zero syndrome d1 w, so the readout M(w) = d1 w is DETECTOR_INADEQUATE for them.

records.name: Hardware narratives are quarantined observer projections
records.obligation: A realization map that would lift this quarantine is not supplied.
records.summary: Device baths, continuum BdG spectra, fabrication narratives, conductance peaks 2e^2/h, gap protocols and capacitance shifts C_Q are external observer projections: they may motivate which complex to declare but do not populate F2 receipts or mint authority without a validated realization map.

records.name: Binding non-claims of the Majorana monograph
records.obligation: Each non-claim is a scope rule; none is a theorem.
records.summary: The source makes no claim of physical MZM detection, vendor endorsement, FOC terminal identity, a generic FSP solution, a complete topological gate set from Ising braiding, an l1-vs-l2 separation over F2, unbounded exact syndrome decoding, physical tetron hardware, or falsity of external measurements.

records.name: Imported 1D Kitaev chain model
records.obligation: No statement that a physical wire realizes this Hamiltonian without disorder or trivial subgap states is made or supported.
records.summary: The spinless p-wave Kitaev chain H = -sum(t c_j^dag c_{j+1} + Delta c_j c_{j+1} + h.c.) - mu sum(c_j^dag c_j - 1/2), its BdG spectrum, the phase region |mu| < 2t with Delta nonzero, and the sweet-spot form H = -i t sum gamma_{2j} gamma_{2j+1} with free edge modes gamma_1, gamma_{2L} are imported models.

records.name: Sweet-spot bonds avoid the edge Majorana indices
records.obligation: Index-level statement only; operator commutation [H, gamma_1] = 0 is the exact instance MAJ-KITAEV-SWEETSPOT-EXACT.
records.summary: For every bond (u, v) = (2j, 2j+1) with 1 <= j < L, u and v differ from 1 and from 2L.

records.name: Exact sweet-spot Kitaev commutators on two modes
records.obligation: Fixed L = 2 instance; general L and the BdG spectrum remain imported.
records.summary: On the exact Gaussian-rational 2-mode Fock carrier with t = Delta = 1, mu = 0, the Kitaev Hamiltonian is Hermitian, commutes with fermion parity, commutes with gamma_1 and gamma_4, and the bulk invariant is -1.

records.name: Imported Ising anyon model and its braiding limits
records.obligation: No claim of physical anyon braiding is made; the braid-matrix identities are the open check MAJ-ISING-BRAID-CHECK.
records.summary: The Ising model {1, sigma, psi} with sigma x sigma = 1 + psi, sigma x psi = sigma, psi x psi = 1 and the R, F data R = e^{-i pi/8} diag(1, i), F = (1/sqrt2)[[1,1],[1,-1]] on the four-sigma fusion space are imported; Ising braiding alone yields only Clifford operations, classically simulable by Gottesman-Knill, so magic-state inputs are required for a complete gate set.

records.name: Exact Q(zeta16) braid identities for the Ising 2x2 matrices
records.obligation: Run the identities in exact cyclotomic arithmetic; the paper code checks only Yang-Baxter in floating point.
records.summary: For B1 = R and B2 = F R F over Q(zeta16), B1 B2 B1 = B2 B1 B2, F^2 = I and the hexagon equations hold as exact identities.

records.name: Exact Yang-Baxter relation for the signed Majorana braid action
records.obligation: Fixed counts 3..10; this is the Majorana exchange action, not the Ising 2x2 representation.
records.summary: For 3 to 10 Majoranas the exact signed-permutation exchange action satisfies b_i b_{i+1} b_i = b_{i+1} b_i b_{i+1}, far commutativity, and composition with its inverse gives the identity.

records.name: Parity observable bookkeeping is algebraic consistency only
records.obligation: No experimental readout model is derived.
records.summary: That a Z2 parity operator squares to I and commutes with an effective Hamiltonian is checked as an algebraic property of declared finite matrices; capacitance shifts C_Q and reflectometry signals stay external models and do not establish protection or coherence.

records.name: Exact parity-sector splitting on the 2-mode Fock carrier
records.obligation: Fixed 2-mode instance; the paper code's ParityAlgebraModel check is floating point.
records.summary: On the exact 2-mode Fock carrier the parity operator restricts to 2-dimensional even and odd sectors, and restricting gamma_1 to a sector is refused because it mixes sectors.

records.name: Sign-reversing pairs cancel in a signed sum
records.obligation: Single pair only; no global involution on a configuration space is constructed.
records.summary: For a natural weight w and integer signs with s1 + s2 = 0, w s1 + w s2 = 0 in Int.

records.name: GIN fermion-recovery routing rule
records.obligation: The three lemmas unfold this rule; the Repair label is a routing tag, not a sign-problem solution.
records.summary: evaluate_gin_fermion_recovery routes an invalid index to ClosureFailure, a valid index with zero uncancelled sign mass to Repair, and positive mass to SplitBrainRefusal.

records.name: Continuous-to-discrete transfer envelope under quasiparticle poisoning
records.obligation: Derive the envelope from the Lindblad equation; a positive physical lower bound on Delta_transfer needs an independent argument, as the source notes.
records.summary: For four MZMs under a Lindblad braiding model with gap Delta, length L/xi and poisoning rate Gamma_qp > 0, the trace-norm transfer defect obeys Delta_transfer(T) <= min(1, C_LZ (hbar/(Delta T))^2 + (Delta/hbar) e^{-L/xi} T + 1 - e^{-Gamma_qp T}) for T >> hbar/Delta, and that envelope has a positive minimum.

records.name: Non-Markovian bosonic-bath transfer envelope
records.obligation: Derive the bath term A_s T^p and p(s) from the spectral density; the calculus minimization of the stated envelope is not written out.
records.summary: For a bath J(w) = 2 pi alpha w_c^{1-s} w^s e^{-w/w_c}, the envelope C_LZ (hbar/(Delta T))^2 + A_s T^p has minimizer T* = (2 C_LZ hbar^2 / (p A_s Delta^2))^{1/(p+2)}, a positive minimum for alpha > 0, and exponent beta = 2/(p+2).

records.name: Multi-terminal cross-junction transfer envelope under disorder
records.obligation: Derive the envelope and the monotonicity in sigma_V; the gap-degradation law is posited.
records.summary: For an M-terminal junction (M >= 4) with Delta_eff = Delta_0 (1 - sigma_V/sigma_crit), the transfer envelope adds C(M,2) >= 6 pairwise splitting channels, its minimum rises with sigma_V on (0, sigma_crit), and the gap closes for sigma_V >= sigma_crit.

records.name: Natural-number positivity lemmas cited for the transfer envelopes
records.obligation: These lemmas do not bear on any physical envelope; MAJ-C18..C20 stay open.
records.summary: Over Nat: products and sums of positive naturals are positive, p > 0 gives p + 2 > 0, p > q gives p + 2 > q + 2, M >= 4 gives M (M - 1) / 2 > 0, and a > b gives a - b > 0.

records.name: Exact rational l1 LP dual lower bounds for Phi1
records.obligation: No LP relaxation or dual certificate for the F2 coset weight is implemented in this source.
records.summary: Exact rational l1 linear programming with dual certificates may give certified lower bounds on the F2 coset weight, certifying cosets beyond the search budget where they meet the capped upper bound and reporting the gap otherwise.

records.name: Evidence adequacy of laboratory measurement maps
records.obligation: Requires a declared device model and measurement map; none is supplied.
records.summary: Whether a declared laboratory protocol's measurement map M separates topological zero modes from trivial Andreev bound states, i.e. whether rho_topo - rho_ABS lies outside ker M.

records.name: Self-consistent Poisson-Schrodinger junction solver
records.obligation: Listed as the next test; no solver exists in this checkout.
records.summary: A self-consistent 3D Poisson-Schrodinger solver coupling gate geometry, dielectric screening and subband chemical-potential pinning to evaluate phase-boundary shrinkage in multi-terminal junctions.

records.name: Canonical anticommutation relations on the exterior Fock space
records.obligation: Mechanize the CAR identities on the exterior algebra; the statistics choice (exterior versus symmetric algebra) is an admitted postulate, and identifying modes with spin-1/2 particles needs the relativistic spin-statistics theorem, outside this finite setting.
records.summary: On an admitted N-dimensional complex inner-product space V with orthonormal basis e_i, creation c_i^dagger = e_i wedge - and interior annihilation c_i on the exterior algebra of V (dimension 2^N) satisfy {c_i, c_j} = 0 and {c_i, c_j^dagger} = delta_ij; in particular (c_i)^2 = 0.

records.name: Jordan-Wigner parity sign of an occupation-basis hop
records.obligation: The general Jordan-Wigner bijection c_j = (prod_{k<j} -sigma^z_k) sigma^-_j between spin-1/2 chains and CAR operators is a standard result imported here, not derived or mechanized in this checkout.
records.summary: In the increasing occupation ordering on 6 modes, the sign of the hop c_target^dagger c_source on every occupation bitmask equals the product of the Jordan-Wigner parities of the annihilation and the creation step, checked exhaustively over all 2^6 states and ordered mode pairs.

records.name: Majorana decomposition, Clifford relations and fermion parity
records.obligation: Standard algebra imported, not derived here; the trunk mechanizes only the two-generator case (DS-QM212-MAJORANA-PROBLEM). Parity superselection is a physical postulate, not a consequence of the algebra. CampaignMajoranaCliffordParity supplies CAR-conditional self-adjointness, anticommutators, equality of generated complex subalgebras, occupation projections, the signed local parity identity and ordered parity action on supplied common occupation eigenvectors. A formal one-mode positive trace-one density matrix need not commute with parity. The all-mode abstract Clifford identification, source CAR/Fock refinement and occupation-basis completeness remain outside these witnesses; no physical superselection law is inferred.
records.summary: For N CAR modes, gamma_{2j-1} = c_j + c_j^dagger and gamma_{2j} = -i(c_j - c_j^dagger) are self-adjoint with {gamma_a, gamma_b} = 2 delta_ab, generate the Clifford algebra on 2N generators, and P = prod_j (-i gamma_{2j-1} gamma_{2j}) is the fermion parity (-1)^N_op.

records.name: CAR kinematics do not select a fermionic Hamiltonian
records.obligation: Hermiticity, number conservation, a locality graph, a one- and two-body truncation and the interaction U remain explicit admissions in every downstream sign record.
records.summary: The CAR constrain the operators c_i, not the Hamiltonian: H = 0, free hopping -t sum c_i^dagger c_j and the Hubbard H(t, U) are distinct Hermitian number-conserving operators on the same CAR Fock space, so a physical Hamiltonian is an added admission (explicit 2-site Hubbard matrix computed by hand).

records.name: Closed-path series for a signed hopping Hamiltonian
records.obligation: The sign of a closed term is a property of the supplied magnitudes, parities and representation; vertex sign gauges remove all negative entries exactly when every configuration cycle is even (FSP-SWITCHING-NORMAL-FORM). Trotter slicing and its error are separate.
records.summary: For a finite self-adjoint H with H_xx = V_x, H_xy = -a_xy (-1)^{eps_xy} (a_xy > 0, eps symmetric), beta >= 0 and E* >= max V_x, Z = e^{-beta E*} sum_m beta^m/m! sum over closed length-m configuration paths of prod K_{x_{j+1} x_j} with K = E* I - H, and each nonzero closed term has sign (-1)^{sum of eps along the path}.

records.name: Average sign and free-energy gap of a declared representation
records.obligation: Exponential decay in beta N is a hypothesis (Delta f bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in N and beta), not a theorem; Z_abs is an operational absolute ensemble, not in general a physical bosonic system.
records.summary: For a declared path representation with weights W(c), <Sign> = Z / Z_abs with Z = sum sigma(c)|W(c)| and Z_abs = sum |W(c)|; when Z > 0, Delta f := -(1/(beta N)) log <Sign> >= 0, so <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) holds by definition.

records.name: Variance of the Monte Carlo sign estimator
records.obligation: Correlated Markov-chain samples, observable numerators and the extensive-gap hypothesis need separate treatment; this bound concerns direct reweighting only, not every estimator or representation.
records.summary: For M_s independent samples from |W|/Z_abs, the sign mean has variance (1 - <Sign>^2)/M_s, so relative error epsilon needs M_s >= (1 - <Sign>^2)/(epsilon^2 <Sign>^2); if <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) this is Omega(exp(2 beta N Delta f)).

records.name: Representation-dependent negativity on the free triangle
records.obligation: Frustration alone does not imply disjoint weight spectra or hardness (ledger GIN-C4, INV-DISJOINT-SPEC); the general Lean lemma covers only the step from disjoint spectra to no weight-preserving sign-reversing involution.
records.summary: For the 3-site spinless triangle, t = 1, U = 0, two fermions, beta = 2 and three Euler slices, the occupation-basis expansion has 27 paths, 6 negative of weight 8/27 and positive weights in {4/9, 1}, so no equal-weight pairing exists there; in the one-body eigenbasis H is diagonal with E in {-1, -1, 2} and Z = 2e^2 + e^-4.

records.name: Troyer-Wiese worst-case reduction (imported)
records.obligation: This is a worst-case statement about a model family under a precision promise; it is not formalized here, is not a reduction to the Hubbard model, and does not make any fixed finite system or every fermionic Hamiltonian intractable.
records.summary: Troyer-Wiese (2005): the NP-complete decision whether a 3D +-J Ising spin glass has ground energy below a threshold reduces in polynomial time to estimating the thermal energy of the frustrated quantum model -sum J_ij sigma^x_i sigma^x_j at beta J >= N ln 2 + ln(12N); a deterministic polynomial estimator for that family would give P = NP, a randomized one NP subset of BPP.

records.name: Sign-reversing equal-weight involution pairs cancel
records.obligation: Summing pairs to get sum_c w(c) sign(c) = 0 on a finite set is a prose orbit-partition step (manuscript Section 4.2), not mechanized; observable numerators need A o tau = A; the involution is sufficient, not necessary (INV-INVOL-CANC).
records.summary: For any carrier with weights in N and signs +-1, an involution tau with w(tau c) = w(c) and sign(tau c) = -sign(c) has no fixed point and each pair satisfies w(c) sign(c) + w(tau c) sign(tau c) = 0; zero signed sum does not require such a pairing (+2, -1, -1), and a cancelling doublet can carry a nonzero observable numerator.

records.name: GIN equal-weight pairing on the four-site ring fixture
records.obligation: Pairing is on exact weight fibers of enumerated paths, not a spectator-preserving symmetry (INV-GIN-PARITY); it does not preserve general observables, and path enumeration grows exponentially. CT-AUX update stability for multi-orbital models has no evidence here.
records.summary: For the four-site periodic ring, U = 0, two spin-up fermions, beta = 3/2 and four Euler slices, all 32 negative Euler-transfer paths are matched to disjoint positive paths of exactly equal rational weight within one weight fiber, and a posting-list query over k modes uses k posting-list operations.

records.name: Rational cochain quotient normal form
records.obligation: N_W is not an l1 minimizer (span(1,2), x = (1,0) gives norm 2 versus 1); the quotient norm is a separate exact linear program with a refusal budget (NF-003). A valid YAML contract or routing label is not a normalizer.
records.summary: For d0 in Q^{m x n} and W = im d0, N_W(x) = x - sum_i x_{p_i} r_i (nonzero RREF rows r_i of d0^T with pivots p_i) is sound, idempotent and complete for x ~ y iff x - y in W, and is independent of the generating matrix; Lean checks the three laws for the fixed integral image span(1, 2) in Z^2.

records.name: Compact lattice U(1) Wilson action gauge invariance
records.obligation: Lean: CampaignFspU1WilsonAction.fsp_u1_wilson_action states gauge invariance (for every g: V -> U(1) and for every angle shift A_ij -> A_ij + theta_i - theta_j) and nonnegativity for beta_g >= 0, for any vertex type and any finite family of closed paths; the periodic hypercubic lattice (ZMod L)^d is one instance. beta_g >= 0 is required: one self-link plaquette with phase -1 and beta_g = -1 gives S = -2. Links are functions of ordered vertex pairs, so for L <= 2 the two parallel links between neighbours are identified. No fermion-sign consequence, continuum limit, reflection positivity, transfer matrix or non-abelian action is claimed. Audited PROVED_LEAN applies only to the narrowed DAG statement; the source record FSP-DERIV-032 claims strict positivity and a Haar-measure bound, neither established here.
records.summary: With link phases U_ij = exp(i A_ij) on ordered vertex pairs and oriented closed-path products U_p over a finite plaquette family, the Wilson action S = beta_g sum_p (1 - Re U_p) is invariant under local U(1) gauge transformations and is nonnegative for beta_g >= 0.

records.name: Wilson-Dirac gamma5-hermiticity and real determinant
records.obligation: A single-flavor det D_W can be negative; the JSONL claim that det D_W is nonnegative is only the two-flavor square. The gamma5 adjoint, reality of det D_W, and the two-flavor square for this operator are not Lean theorems in this checkout. Euclidean Clifford data in dimensions 2 and 4 are checked in Lean. An exact check on one periodic 2x2 lattice, mass -1, U(1), finds det = -3.
records.summary: The Wilson-Dirac operator satisfies gamma5 D_W gamma5 = D_W^dagger, so its nonreal eigenvalues come in conjugate pairs and det D_W is real; for two degenerate flavors det(D_W)^2 >= 0.

records.name: Topological theta term makes lattice weights complex
records.obligation: Severity of the resulting sign problem is phenomenology from the literature; the checkout has no theta-term model.
records.summary: Adding S_theta = i theta Q_top with real lattice charge Q_top multiplies the Boltzmann weight by exp(-i theta Q_top), which is nonreal unless theta Q_top lies in pi Z for every configuration, so positive-weight importance sampling is lost for generic theta != 0.

records.name: Callan-Harvey anomaly inflow on a finite slab lattice
records.obligation: Construct a regulated chiral boundary determinant whose projector, basis or measure depends on the gauge field (domain-wall or overlap/Ginsparg-Wilson type), derive from the same fermions the bulk Chern-Simons term they induce, and show that the two gauge variations cancel. The fixed-basis Wilson-slab test cannot register an anomaly, because site-matched fixed bases give similarity-invariant determinants; its bare lifted CS candidate is neither induced by the fermions nor well defined on U(1) links (an integer lift of the same links changes it by 1/8). The continuum Callan-Harvey mechanism remains a literature import.
records.summary: Target: on a finite slab lattice the chiral variation of the boundary fermion determinant cancels the bulk Chern-Simons variation. Not established in this checkout. One tested candidate does not realize it, as expected: on open Wilson slabs with U(1) links, the gauge change acts on the Wilson matrix by a diagonal similarity, so the full, interior, boundary Schur and fixed site-matched chiral-block determinants are gauge invariant by construction, while a lifted cup-product CS term whose coefficient is not derived from the fermions changes by 1/32. This is a fixed-basis truncation of a vector-like regulator, not an obstruction to lattice inflow.

records.name: SU(2) adjoint fermions have a real determinant
records.obligation: For a single Majorana adjoint flavor the measure is a Pfaffian whose sign can change; reality is not positivity. CampaignFspSu2AdjointRealDet.lean establishes the 3x3 SO(3) adjoint representation of unit quaternions, Z_2 center blindness R(-q) = R(q), the antiunitary intertwiner reality identity C conj(D) = D C -> Im(det D) = 0, reality of the 4D lattice adjoint Wilson-Dirac determinant wilsonDiracAdjoint4_det_im_zero, a negative-determinant witness (det = -1 < 0), and the 2x2 and 4x4 skew-symmetric Majorana Pfaffian square identities and sign-flip pairs. Full continuum SU(2) path-integral construction and general 2n x 2n Berezin Grassmann integration remain literature imports.
records.summary: For lattice SU(2) with Dirac fermions in the real adjoint representation, an antiunitary symmetry of the Dirac operator makes det D_adj real for every gauge configuration.

records.name: Complex quark determinant at real chemical potential
records.obligation: Standard continuum/thermodynamic QCD chemical-potential sign-problem framework imported; lean4/CampaignFspQcdChemicalPotentialDet.lean establishes the exact gamma_5-chemical-potential determinant conjugation identity (det D(mu))* = det D(-mu*), reality at mu = 0 and purely imaginary mu = i mu_I, the Hasenfratz-Karsch and Kogut-Susskind staggered operator identities, the explicit SU(3) clock link U = diag(i,i,-1) with Im Tr(U) = 2 != 0, the 6x6 chiral SU(3) determinant witness det D_SU3(2) = 63/8 - 27i and det D_SU3(1/2) = 63/8 + 27i, and the diagonal SU(2) reality contrast, while checks/independent/fsp-qcd-chemical-potential-det.py checks 1D and 2D staggered SU(3) vs SU(2) lattices.
records.summary: For lattice Dirac operators with chemical potential, gamma5 D(mu) gamma5 = D(-mu*)^dagger, hence det D(mu)^* = det D(-mu*); for real mu != 0 this relates D(mu) to D(-mu) only and det D(mu) is in general complex.

records.name: Z3 center projection and baryon triality
records.obligation: State the canonical-ensemble center projection as an identity on a declared lattice model and show which signs it removes; ledger GIN-C10 and GIN-C11 withdraw the fixture reading.
records.summary: Claimed: averaging over Z3 center phases cancels the signs of fractional-triality quark paths and leaves color-singlet zero-triality contributions; no model, projection identity or computation for this exists in this checkout.

records.name: Real determinant at imaginary chemical potential
records.obligation: Analytic continuation from imaginary to real mu is an extrapolation, not a sign-free route to real mu; not established in this checkout. CampaignFspImaginaryMuRealDet covers arbitrary finite bipartite transport blocks at unit fugacity: staggered adjoint symmetry, determinant reality, two-flavor nonnegativity and positive-mass staggered positivity. Its centerSum_periodic concerns a declared finite center-orbit sum only; it supplies no QCD measure, spin-taste reconstruction, phase transition or analytic-continuation theorem. The full node remains imported.
records.summary: At mu = i mu_I with real mu_I, gamma5 D(i mu_I) gamma5 = D(i mu_I)^dagger, so det D(i mu_I) is real; nonnegativity needs two degenerate flavors (or a staggered operator m + K with K anti-Hermitian, m > 0), and Z(mu_I) has Roberge-Weiss periodicity 2 pi T / 3.

records.name: Lattice Wess-Zumino supercharge algebra
records.obligation: Full interacting 2D continuum/lattice super-Poincare restoration remains open; lean4/CampaignFspLatticeWessZuminoSusy.lean establishes the exact Z_2-graded block supercharge algebra (Q(A)^2 = 0, {Q_a, Q_b} = 2 delta_ab H(A, A^dagger), [Gamma_F, H] = 0, [Q, H] = 0), quadratic-form nonnegativity of A^T A and A A^T, supertrace vanishing Tr(Gamma_F H) = 0, exact nonzero-energy boson-fermion eigenstate pairing, the explicit 2-site lattice Wess-Zumino block wz2SiteBlock, and the 3-site discrete cubic Leibniz defect witness (-2 != 0), while checks/independent/fsp-lattice-wess-zumino-susy.py checks 1D and rectangular lattice Wess-Zumino models.
records.summary: Claimed: a finite-lattice 2D N=1 Wess-Zumino model with supercharges obeying {Q_a, Q_b} = 2 delta_ab H, H >= 0 and exact boson-fermion pairing of nonzero levels; no such lattice construction exists in this checkout, and lattice discretizations generally keep at most a subalgebra exact.

records.name: Nicolai map sign elimination (unsupported)
records.obligation: Give the lattice model, prove det(d xi / d phi) = det D_F, and treat the sign of det D_F and the multiplicity of the map; Nicolai-map results are model specific in the literature.
records.summary: Claimed: on an off-shell supersymmetric lattice model the map xi = -partial^2 phi + W'(phi) has Jacobian equal to the fermion determinant and turns the partition function into a Gaussian with no sign problem; nothing in this checkout constructs the map or the Jacobian identity.

records.name: Witten index beta-independence under exact supersymmetry
records.obligation: Standard result imported; it presupposes an exact lattice supercharge, which FSP-DERIV-040 leaves open, and gives no sign-free sampling of Z itself.
records.summary: On a finite-dimensional graded Hilbert space with an exact supercharge Q and H = {Q, Q^dagger}, positive-energy levels pair bosons with fermions, so W = Tr[(-1)^F exp(-beta H)] = n_B(E=0) - n_F(E=0) for every beta, and unbroken supersymmetry has ground energy 0.

records.name: Kitaev honeycomb exact Majorana solution
records.obligation: A sign-free sampling claim for this representation is not made or checked here; the gauge projection and flux-sector sum must be kept explicit.
records.summary: Kitaev (2006): in the four-Majorana representation of the honeycomb model, the plaquette fluxes W_p commute with H and with each other, and in each flux sector H is quadratic in the c Majoranas with a static Z2 gauge field (after projection to the physical subspace).

records.name: Laughlin quasihole exchange phase pi/m
records.obligation: No Berry-phase or torus computation is in this checkout; the local module fixes m = 3 and checks numeric constants only (ledger GIN-C16 withdraws its reading).
records.summary: Arovas-Schrieffer-Wilczek: adiabatic exchange of two quasiholes in the nu = 1/m Laughlin state gives statistical phase theta = pi/m.

records.name: Fibonacci anyon fusion and braiding data
records.obligation: The JSONL calls d_tau rational, which is false; the claim that braiding avoids sign degradation has no content here. Exact ribbon data are pinned elsewhere in the trunk (TFQ-0050), not in this package.
records.summary: The Fibonacci category has fusion tau x tau = 1 + tau, quantum dimension d_tau = (1 + sqrt 5)/2 (irrational), F and R matrices solving the pentagon and hexagon equations, and three-anyon braids generate a dense subgroup of SU(2) (Freedman-Larsen-Wang).

records.obligation: Regge calculus carries no fermion-sign content in this package; Lorentzian signature, convergence conditions and any sign consequence need separate evidence (ledger GIN-C13).
records.summary: On a 4D triangulation with squared edge lengths, the deficit angle at a hinge h is epsilon_h = 2 pi - sum of dihedral angles at h and the Regge action is S = sum_h A_h epsilon_h; its convergence to the Einstein-Hilbert action under refinement is a literature result imported here.

records.obligation: The claim that these constraints suppress sign-inducing braids has no evidence here and is left open.

records.name: Involution-or-NP-hard dichotomy for finite systems (refuted as stated)
records.obligation: The open research content is FSP-EFFICIENT-SAMPLING-OBLIGATIONS: for a stated model family and input encoding, separate exact finite identities, protected sign-free representations, efficient samplers and worst-case hardness.
records.summary: The claimed dichotomy (each finite quantum system either admits a certified sign-eliminating involution found in polynomial time or is an NP-hard sign obstruction) fails as stated: NP-hardness is a property of input families, the free triangle has no equal-weight involution in its declared basis yet is solved by one-body diagonalization, and zero signed mass need not come from an involution.

records.name: Tensor factorization of the dimension-six carrier as C^2 tensor C^3
records.obligation: The source statement that every 6x6 operator decomposes into Pauli and Gell-Mann tensor products, and its SU(2)/SU(3) reading, are not checked here; the factorization selects no MUB structure.
records.summary: Fix the identification C^6 = C^2 tensor C^3 with product basis |j,k> = |j> tensor |k> for j in {0,1} and k in {0,1,2}; this is a declared choice of tensor factorization of the six-dimensional carrier.

records.name: No field of order six, so no finite-field MUB construction at d = 6
records.obligation: This rules out one construction route only; it gives no upper bound on the number of MUBs in C^6 and does not exclude a complete family produced by another construction.
records.summary: No finite field has six elements, since finite fields have prime-power order; hence the finite-field Weyl-character construction of d+1 MUBs has no instance at d = 6.

records.name: Clock and shift operators in dimension six
records.obligation: These standard identities are not checked in this checkout for d = 6; the source writes X Z = w Z X, which holds only under the opposite clock convention; no MUB count follows from them.
records.summary: On C^6 with shift X|j> = |j+1 mod 6> and clock Z|j> = w^j |j>, w = exp(2 pi i/6), one has Z X = w X Z, and the 36 operators X^p Z^q are pairwise orthogonal for the trace pairing tr(A* B).

records.name: Quartet existence as a raw complex Hadamard completion problem
records.obligation: Global exclusion still needs complete representative coverage and nonextension for every representative, which no_quartet_of_concrete_representatives takes as hypotheses.
records.summary: A quartet of pairwise unbiased orthonormal bases of C^6 exists iff some 6x6 matrix H has a raw quartet: H, U, V with unit-modulus entries, M* M = 6I, and |(A* B)_ij|^2 = 6 for each pair; raw-quartet existence is invariant under row and column permutation-phase equivalence.

records.obligation: Transport to a dephased representative, classification of arbitrary CHM(6), the source cusp rank-degeneration claim, and Conjecture 3 (no quartet contains a family member) are not established.

records.name: Route C Fourier landing theorem (claim)
records.obligation: The landing premise remains a hypothesis of no_complete_mub6_of_fourier_triple_landing (MUB6-C05); no concrete algebraic landing theorem or chart interpretation exists.
records.summary: Claim: any four MUBs in C^6 are unitarily equivalent to a set containing F_6 or a Haagerup deformation of it, closing the Route C landing premise.

records.name: Five-branch moduli routing with certified empty branches (claim)
records.obligation: Gap G1 is OPEN: the five-family list was quarantined on 2026-10-11, FullModuliClassification follows only from FiveBranchRealizationHypothesis, and residuals R6 and R7 are NOT_A_CERTIFICATE.
records.summary: Claim: every CHM(6) lies in one of five branches (Fourier, Haagerup, Szollosi, Karlsson, Tao), each certified free of quartet extensions.

records.name: Evaluation functionals give positive flat degree-two moments
records.obligation: This is the necessity direction only; the source Lasserre hierarchy at every order t is not formalized, and feasibility of a relaxation gives no solution without flatness and compatibility.
records.summary: For any real point x, the evaluation functional p -> p(x) is normalized, its degree-two coordinate moment matrix is positive semidefinite, and its degree-two and degree-one moment ranks are equal.

records.name: Matolcsi et al. Conjectures 2 and 3 as open premises
records.obligation: Locally only the count of 20 balanced sign masks among 64 and a declared row-count table are checked; AnalyticCubeSliceCertificate takes its row bound and table compatibility as fields. External: the alpha-vanishing part of Conjecture 2 for every order-6 complex Hadamard matrix not equivalent to the Tao matrix is a theorem of the OpenAI companion paper (Lean: OAI.MUB6.fourier_vanishing; external, not built here, see MUB6-OPENAI-FAMILY-LE-FIVE). Still open: the condition coupling the characters at 3a, Tao-class transitions inside triplets, Conjecture 3 and Proposition 4.2.
records.summary: Matolcsi et al. Conjecture 2 (balanced Laurent vanishing on actual MUB triples) together with Conjecture 3 (no quartet contains a Szollosi family member) implies at most three MUBs in C^6 (Proposition 4.2); both conjectures are open.

records.name: Tao matrix balanced Laurent sums have squared modulus nine
records.obligation: This is a finite evaluation for one matrix; without Conjecture 2 for arbitrary MU triples it gives no nonextension statement, and the source wording as an l1 operator norm does not match the computed quantity. Relation to OpenAI: its Fourier-vanishing theorem exempts exactly the Tao class, and the repository phase table equals OpenAI taoExponent after the index involution (3 5) (exhaustive search; lean4/MubOpenAIBridge.lean tao_phase_bridge, compiled 2026-10-21 under Lean 4.35.0 with standard axioms only), so this evaluation concerns the exceptional matrix. It is not an obstruction to extension.
records.summary: For the Tao matrix S6 and each of the 20 balanced sign vectors g (three +1, three -1), |sum_j prod_r S_rj^{g_r}|^2 = 9, computed over the integer Eisenstein table and over C with w = -1/2 + i sqrt 3/2.

records.name: Non-existence of four MUBs in dimension six (open)
records.obligation: The corpus certifies exact reductions (quartet existence iff solutions of the 618-, 648- or 666-equation quadratic systems in stated boxes), conditional implications over supplied premises, and exclusion of the regions in MUB6-C28 and MUB6-PAPER-CLOSE-COLUMNS; it does not cover the full boxes, the six charts, the 56 family cells, the three cusp collars, or triples outside the Szollosi parameterization. N(6) <= 5 is recorded separately as MUB6-OPENAI-FAMILY-LE-FIVE (external theorem of OpenAI, not built here); it does not decide whether a quartet exists. OpenAI N(6)=3 is recorded as external context only: a binary64 seed-cover, Stage A/B/C and clique-search pipeline whose code and run archive are unreleased (verification/ returns 404) and whose Lean tree does not formalize it; it is not imported.
records.summary: Open problem: no four pairwise mutually unbiased bases exist in C^6.

records.name: Maximal number of MUBs in dimension six equals three (open)
records.obligation: The lower bound three is checked (MUB6-DERIV-063); the upper bound is equivalent to MUB6-DERIV-085 and is open; the cited Lean name MUB.TerminalTheorem.max_mub_six_equals_three does not exist in this checkout. N(6) <= 5 is recorded separately as MUB6-OPENAI-FAMILY-LE-FIVE (external theorem of OpenAI, not built here); it does not decide whether a quartet exists. OpenAI N(6)=3 is recorded as external context only: a binary64 seed-cover, Stage A/B/C and clique-search pipeline whose code and run archive are unreleased (verification/ returns 404) and whose Lean tree does not formalize it; it is not imported.
records.summary: Open problem: the maximum number of pairwise mutually unbiased bases in C^6 is three.

records.name: At most five mutually unbiased bases in dimension six (OpenAI, imported)
records.obligation: External and not built here: the upstream proof (3381 Lean files, about 205 MB, Lean 4.34.1 and its own Mathlib commit) is neither vendored nor replayed. lean4/MubOpenAIBridge.lean states the repository-type consequence conditionally on OpenAIFamilyBound; it compiled on 2026-10-21 under Lean 4.35.0 and Mathlib v4.35.0 with exit code 0 and only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound (mub_openai_bridge_compile_receipt.md). The bound itself is not proved here. OpenAI N(6)=3 is recorded as external context only: a binary64 seed-cover, Stage A/B/C and clique-search pipeline whose code and run archive are unreleased (verification/ returns 404) and whose Lean tree does not formalize it; it is not imported. MUB6-NO-QUARTET-D6 and MUB6-MAX-MUB-SIX-EQUALS-THREE stay OPEN.
records.summary: Every family of pairwise mutually unbiased orthonormal bases of C^6 has at most five members (N(6) <= 5): OpenAI's Lean theorem OAI.MUB6.family_size_le_five (github.com/openai/math, commit 1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a, Apache-2.0), via the exact mixed-moment Gram certificate no_seven_mutually_unbiased_bases and Weiner's completion six_extend_to_seven.

records.name: Route C label-count arithmetic
records.obligation: These are label counts in MUB6OrbitConfiguration; the structure has no matrices and no map from counts to Fourier transition edges.
records.summary: For natural numbers with 6 = n_D + n_T + n_S + n_H, n_T + n_S <= 1 and n_H <= 0, one has n_D >= 5, C(n_D,2) >= 10 and n_D + C(n_D,2) >= 15.

records.name: Route C: no complete family under a Fourier-triple landing premise
records.obligation: Discharge the landing premise from concrete complex MU data and give the opaque Basis type a concrete interpretation; earlier unconditional Route C statements are withdrawn.
records.summary: Over the opaque interface types Basis and is_mutually_unbiased, the premise that every pairwise MU seven-basis family contains a triple in InFourierDitaChart implies NoCompleteMUB6; so does a landing map CompleteMUB6 -> RouteCCompleteMUBFamily.

records.name: Combinatorial gluing over opaque bases
records.obligation: Combinatorial facts over uninterpreted predicates; a concrete interpretation in complex matrices is needed before they apply to C^6.
records.summary: For opaque Basis and MU predicates, every constituent triple of a pairwise MU seven-basis family has a fourth MU basis in the family, and if no MU triple has a fourth MU basis then no MU four-basis family exists.

records.name: Cauchy-Binet bounded invertible minor of a Hadamard matrix
records.obligation: The bound gives a chart, not nonextension; the selected minor need not be the external finite-corner minor.
records.summary: Every 6x6 matrix H with unit-modulus entries and H H* = 6I has a 3x3 minor of its first three rows with |det|^2 >= 54/5, which is invertible and whose inverse has squared entry moduli at most 10/27.

records.name: Bounded block chart and division-free quartet equations
records.obligation: Infeasibility of these equations is open; the positive determinant bound is needed for reconstruction and for the MU-factor cancellation.
records.summary: Quartet existence in C^6 is equivalent to admissible bounded block data (E, B, C) whose completion with D = -C E* (B^-1)* has a raw quartet, and to a solution of the division-free equations obtained by clearing the nonzero determinant of B.

records.name: Reduction to retained finite-corner reconstructions
records.obligation: MubFiniteCornerReduction.lean is not in this checkout; exclusion over every retained reconstruction is open, and finite fibres over continuous seeds give no finite global list.
records.summary: Using the external finite-corner classification of single 6x6 complex Hadamard matrices, quartet existence in C^6 is equivalent to raw quartet completion of some retained finite-corner reconstruction with D = -C E* (B^-1)*.
