Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/algebraic components and non-equivalence fences: (1) over any semiring R and for any dimensions dA, dB (even when dA < dB), if Fin dA is inhabited then CyclicForA Omega implies SeparatingForAc Omega via matrix associativity (X * Omega) * Y = X * (Omega * Y), so any nonzero right-kernel vector or identically zero column precludes cyclicity even when dA < dB; (2) discharging the open finite items of TFQ-2107, none of |000>, |GHZ_3>, or |W_3> is cyclic on any single site (s in {0, 1, 2}), |000> has neither a left inverse nor cyclicity on any pair of sites while |GHZ_3> and |W_3> are both cyclic and separating on every pair of sites, all three states have full complementary rank 1 and are cyclic on the full 3-site algebra, and across the 4-qubit 2+2 bipartition neither |0000> nor |GHZ_4> is cyclic whereas the 2-Bell-pair cluster state has full complementary rank 4 and is both cyclic and separating; and (3) on a finite N-site ring, cyclicShift N aliases with period N, translation-invariant constant vectors have zero discrete momentum difference, and the translation-invariant 3-qubit product vacuum |000> fails cyclicity on every proper subsystem.

records.name: Finite target: cyclicity of a state for a subsystem algebra is a rank condition
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: separating implies full column rank (so the three-way equivalence is not complete); the identification of full column rank with full rank of the reduced state; the qubit subset bookkeeping; the conclusion "not cyclic" for the single-site cases (cyclic implies left inverse is proved only for dB <= dA, and a single site has dA=2 < dB=4; the kernel vectors give non-separating only) and for |000> on pairs (a zero column is exhibited but "zero column implies no left inverse implies not cyclic" is not stated as a theorem); that |000> is cyclic for the full algebra. A Lean proof of the equivalence for general n is open. The relation to the continuum theorem is an analogy: finite dimension has no translation group or spectrum condition.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. Let Omega be a dA x dB matrix over a semiring R (the amplitude matrix of a vector in H_A tensor H_{A^c}; for qubits dA = 2^|A| and dB = 2^|A^c|, but the qubit tensor-factor bookkeeping is not formalised). Omega is cyclic for End(H_A) when every dA x dB matrix is X Omega for some X. (a) If Omega has a left inverse L with L Omega = I_dB (full column rank dB, which over a field is full rank of the reduced state on A^c) then Omega is cyclic and Omega is separating for End(H_{A^c}) (Omega Y = 0 implies Y = 0). (b) Conversely, cyclic implies a left inverse whenever dB <= dA (an injection Fin dB -> Fin dA is supplied). (c) A nonzero vector in the right kernel of Omega makes Omega not separating. (d) Exact 3-qubit instances over Z for the product vector |000>, GHZ = |000>+|111> and W = |100>+|010>+|001>: explicit nonzero right-kernel vectors for every single-site unfolding (2 x 4), explicit integer left inverses of every pair-of-sites unfolding (4 x 2) for GHZ and W, and a zero column in every pair-of-sites unfolding of |000>.

records.name: Epstein and Glaser 1973: the role of locality in perturbation theory
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against the Numdam full text (AIHPA_1973__19_3_211_0); nothing in the paper is used as a premise of a repository theorem.
records.summary: Epstein and Glaser (1973, Ann. Inst. H. Poincare A 19, 211-295, Abstract p. 211, Section 1.1 pp. 214-215, Section 2.1 eq. (9) p. 218, Section 2.2 eq. (30) p. 223, and Section 5 pp. 231-237) give an inductive construction of the perturbation series S(g) = 1 + sum_{n>=1} (i^n / n!) int T_n(x_1,...,x_n) g(x_1)...g(x_n) dx in which each order T_n is constructed from lower orders by causal factorization outside the total diagonal and by splitting causal distributions with scaling degree bounds on the diagonal. This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Imported: causal factorization of the scattering matrix
records.obligation: Audited against Epstein-Glaser (1973) eqs. (9), (30) and Brunetti-Fredenhagen (2000) eq. (2) and Condition P3. The continuum distribution extension has no counterpart in the repository's finite posets.
records.summary: Imported property, audited and corrected against Epstein and Glaser (1973, Section 1.1 condition (C.A.) pp. 214-215, Section 2.1 condition (Caus. 1) eq. (9) p. 218, Section 2.2 eq. (30) p. 223) and Brunetti and Fredenhagen (2000, arXiv:math-ph/9903028, Section 1 eq. (2) p. 4 and Section 3 Condition P3 p. 15): the scattering operator satisfies V(g, h1+h2) = S(g)^{-1} S(g+h1+h2) = V(g, h1) V(g, h2) (and at g=0, S(g1+g2) = S(g1) S(g2)) whenever supp h1 does not intersect the causal past of supp h2, written supp h1 cap (supp h2 + V^-) = empty (which includes spacelike separation as well as causal future separation, not only supp h1 inside the causal future of supp h2). Equivalently at each order n, the time-ordered operator-valued distributions factorize as T(P union Q) = T(P) T(Q) whenever {x_i : i in P} cap ({x_j : j in Q} + V^-) = empty (eq. (30) p. 223; Condition P3 p. 15), and renormalization reduces to extending time-ordered products across the total diagonal. The repository has neither operator-valued distributions nor a continuum Minkowski causal cone. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/algebraic components and non-equivalence fences: (1) over any group G and additive coupling carrier A, the relative Bogoliubov operator bogoliubovV S g h = (S g)^{-1} * S(g + h) satisfies V(g, 0) = 1, the unconditional telescoping cocycle law V(g, h1) * V(g + h1, h2) = V(g, h1 + h2), and the equivalence V(g, h1 + h2) = V(g, h1) * V(g, h2) <-> V(g + h1, h2) = V(g, h2), while on the diamond poset C2 the Epstein-Glaser separation predicate noInCausalPast C2 holds symmetrically for spacelike ([d1], [d2]) and one-way for future-before-past ([d1, d2, d3], [d0]); (2) on the 4-element N poset (0 < 2, 1 < 2, 1 < 3), all 5 linear extensions extN0..extN4 are connected by chains of adjacent spacelike swaps (SpacelikeSwapChain posetN) and have identical ordered products for every spacelike-commuting monoid assignment (discharging the finite-poset connectivity question of TFQ-2110), while anticommuting Pauli operators X, Z on (n0, n3) flip the sign between extN3 and extN4; and (3) coincident pairs (x, x) on a FiniteStrictPoset are never spacelike separated, the 4D Epstein-Glaser polynomial counterterm dimension binom(omega + 4, 4) equals (1, 5, 15, 35, 70) for omega = 0..4, and off-diagonal factorization (x != y) leaves coincident-diagonal contact counterterms c unconstrained.

records.name: Finite target: time-ordered products over linear extensions of a poset
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: that any two linear extensions of an arbitrary finite strict poset are connected by a chain of adjacent spacelike swaps, which is the step that turns swap invariance into independence from the choice of linear extension. Connectivity is exhibited for the two extensions of C2 only; for the N poset the five extensions are counted but their connectivity, and hence the equality of their ordered products, is not stated. The relation to Epstein-Glaser is an analogy.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. For a FiniteStrictPoset P and elements A_x (x in P) of a monoid with A_x A_y = A_y A_x for all spacelike pairs x,y: the ordered product along a listing of P is unchanged by one adjacent swap of spacelike elements, hence by any chain of adjacent spacelike swaps. Exact checks: the diamond C2 has exactly 2 linear extensions among the 24 permutations of its four points, [0,1,2,3] and [0,2,1,3], connected by one adjacent spacelike swap of 1 and 2; the N poset has exactly 5 linear extensions; with integer 2x2 Pauli matrices on C2 the two ordered products agree when the spacelike points 1 and 2 carry the commuting matrices Z and Z, and differ by the sign -1 (and are unequal) when they carry the anticommuting matrices X and Z. The distribution extension and the ultraviolet content of the Epstein-Glaser construction have no finite counterpart.

records.name: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin 1987: space-time as a causal set
records.obligation: Record only. Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 3 p. 6) and Reid (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section II p. 2) were audited in full; the 1987 PRL print article is not held in the checkout.
records.summary: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin (1987) propose that spacetime at the smallest scales is a discrete structure, a causal set: a locally finite set with a partial order encoding past and future. They examine how a Lorentzian manifold can approximate such a set, note that effective dimensionality can vary with length scale, and sketch a quantum dynamics. Sorkin's Valdivia notes (2003) are a later survey. This node records the proposal.

records.name: A finite causal set is a FiniteStrictPoset
records.obligation: Definitional only. Nothing about manifold-likeness, dimension or the continuum limit is asserted.
records.summary: Reading of definitions. A causal set in the sense of the source is a locally finite partially ordered set; in the strict-order form its relation is irreflexive and transitive, and local finiteness is automatic on a finite set. This is the structure FiniteStrictPoset n of lean4/CausalOrder.lean. The Python class CausalSet in code/python/src/general_relativity/causal_set.py builds a poset from relations, takes the transitive closure and refuses cycles. The identification involves no sprinkling, no embedding in a Lorentzian manifold and no dynamics.

records.name: Finite target: ordering fraction, Myrheim-Meyer dimension and Hasse diagrams as exact rationals
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the n x n grid poset (a FiniteStrictPoset on n^2 points) has R(n) strictly related pairs, so (i) is arithmetic on a posited count cross-checked against the diamond only at n=2; the derivation of f(d) from the Gamma-function formula; correctness of the nearest-dimension selector beyond the six listed inputs; that the Hasse relation itself generates the order and is the minimal such relation. Everything is rational arithmetic on named finite posets. The dimension estimator is a heuristic for sprinklings; the finite estimate on a small poset carries no manifold statement.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. The ordering fraction of a finite causal set is the exact rational r = 2R/(n(n-1)), with R the number of strictly related pairs (CausalSet.ordering_fraction); Lean computes r(C1)=2/3 and r(C2)=5/6 from the relation tables of CausalOrder.lean. In Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 7 p. 16), the expected ordering fraction of a Poisson sprinkling into a d-dimensional Minkowski causal interval normalized by binom(N,2) is f(d) = (3/2) Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2 + 1) / Gamma(3d/2 + 1) = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (2 Gamma(3d/2)) (in Reid 2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section III eq. (5) p. 5, normalizing by <N>^2 instead of binom(N,2) gives f(d)/2 = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (4 Gamma(3d/2))), with exact rational values f(1)=1, f(2)=1/2, f(3)=8/35 and f(4)=1/10; in Lean these four values are entered as a table (70 f(d) = 70, 35, 16, 7) and not derived from the Gamma formula. (i) If the n x n grid with the componentwise product order has R(n) = (n(n+1)/2)^2 - n^2 strictly related pairs (a count entered as a definition in Lean, not derived from a poset), then 4 R(n) = n^2 (n-1)(n+3), the ordering fraction is r = (n+3)/(2(n+1)) for all n >= 2 with r(n) - 1/2 = 1/(n+1), the values for n=2..6 are 5/6, 3/4, 7/10, 2/3, 9/14, and r(2) = 5/6 equals the exactly computed r(C2) of the diamond. This is an observation about a lattice, not an instance of the sprinkling theorem. (ii) An exact nearest-dimension selector over d in {1,2,3,4} with tie reporting is defined and checked on the six inputs 5/6, 3/4, 7/10, 1/2, 8/35, 1/10, giving [1], [1,2] (an exact tie), [2], [2], [3], [4]. (iii) The Hasse covering relation of any FiniteStrictPoset is contained in every subrelation E of the order such that every related pair is in E or has an intermediate element (one half of "unique transitive reduction"); C1 has 2 links and C2 has 4; the Mobius tables c1_mu and c2_mu of CausalOrder.lean satisfy the Mobius recursion and c2_mu(d0,d3)=1.

records.name: Maldacena 1997: large N superconformal field theories and supergravity
records.obligation: Record only. The duality is a conjecture supported by checks in the source literature.
records.summary: Maldacena (1997, arXiv:hep-th/9711200, Section 2 eqs. (2.1)-(2.5) pp. 3-5, conjecture p. 9) takes the low-energy decoupling limit of N parallel D3-branes (eq. (2.1)) and conjectures that four-dimensional U(N) N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory is dual to type IIB string theory on AdS_5 x S^5 with radius R^2 / alpha' = sqrt(4 pi g_YM^2 N) (eq. (2.5)) and N units of five-form flux, alongside M2/M5-brane and AdS_3 counterparts in Sections 3-5. This node records the conjecture as published.

records.name: Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten 1998: the correlator dictionary
records.obligation: Record only. The dictionary is not reproduced.
records.summary: Gubser, Klebanov and Polyakov (1998, arXiv:hep-th/9802109, Section 2 eq. (2.5) p. 4 and Section 3 eq. (3.14) p. 8) and Witten (1998, arXiv:hep-th/9802150, Section 2.3 eq. (2.11) p. 11 and Section 2.5 eqs. (2.32)-(2.33) p. 17) formulate the AdS/CFT prescription identifying the CFT generating functional of boundary operators O coupled to boundary sources phi_0 with the bulk partition function <exp int phi_0 O>_CFT = Z_string(phi_0) (approximated at large N by exp(-I_sugra(phi)) on AdS_{d+1}), with conformal dimension Delta(Delta - d) = (m R)^2, Delta = (d + sqrt(d^2 + 4(m R)^2))/2 for a scalar of mass m. This node records the two papers.

records.name: Imported: bulk gravity and boundary conformal field theory are equivalent
records.obligation: The continuum partition-function equality Z_grav[phi_0] = Z_CFT[phi_0], the full AdS_5 x S^5 / N=4 SYM Hilbert space isomorphism, and the continuum inputs FQ-GAP-CONTINUUM-HILBERT-LIFT and TFQ-0085 remain unconstructed; at b < B a finite isometric encoding V^T V = I_b has non-surjective pushforward iota_V and a nontrivial boundary kernel of pi_V.
records.summary: Imported as an assumption, not as a result of this repository: a continuum quantum gravity theory on an asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime has the same generating functional and observables as a conformal field theory on its boundary. Narrowed to its exact finite/rational algebraic shadows: (1) over Q, the GKPW scalar mass-dimension quadratic gkpwMassSq(d, Delta) = Delta(Delta - d) = mSq satisfies the shadow involution Delta |-> d - Delta, (2 Delta - d)^2 = d^2 + 4 Delta(Delta - d), and the Breitenlohner-Freedman lower bound -(d^2)/4 <= Delta(Delta - d) with double root Delta = d/2 at saturation and no rational root strictly below -(d^2)/4; (2) in 't Hooft double-line counting with lambda = g_YM^2 N and Euler characteristic chi = V - E + F = 2 - 2g, the ribbon weight satisfies (g_YM^2)^(E - V) N^F * N^(E - V) = lambda^(E - V) N^F, suppressing the genus-1 torus vacuum graph (V=2, E=3, F=1) relative to the planar dipole (V=2, E=3, F=3) by N^2; and (3) for any finite isometric bulk-to-boundary encoding V^T V = I_b, the pushforward iota_V(O_bulk) = V O_bulk V^T and pullback pi_V(O_bdry) = V^T O_bdry V satisfy pi_V(iota_V(O_bulk)) = O_bulk, iota_V(A) iota_V(C) = iota_V(A C), and <V psi, O_bdry(V psi)> = <psi, pi_V(O_bdry) psi>, whereas for b = 1 < B = 2 (V = [[1],[0]]) V V^T != I_2 and the nonzero boundary operator O_perp = [[0,0],[0,1]] pulls back to 0 and has no bulk preimage.

records.name: Ryu and Takayanagi 2006: holographic entanglement entropy
records.obligation: Record only.
records.summary: Ryu and Takayanagi (2006, arXiv:hep-th/0603001, Section 1 eq. (1.5) p. 2) propose that the entanglement entropy S_A of a spatial subregion A in a (d+1)-dimensional CFT dual to static AdS_{d+2} is given by S_A = Area(gamma_A) / (4 G_N^(d+2)), where gamma_A is the static minimal bulk d-surface anchored on partial A, and check in Section 2 (eqs. (2.1), (2.5)-(2.6) p. 3) that in AdS_3/CFT_2 the geodesic length reproduces S_A = (c/3) log((L/(pi a)) sin(pi l / L)) under the Brown-Henneaux relation c = 3R / (2 G_N^(3)). This node records the proposal as published.

records.name: Imported: entropy of a boundary region equals minimal surface area over 4G
records.obligation: No source supplies a dictionary from the repository's finite areas to the surface areas of the formula; under BakerCitedInput mixed algebraic spectra have transcendental natural-log entropy, and the TFQ-0100 rational Regge proxy scales as lam^4 and vanishes on flat charts.
records.summary: Imported formula, as the source states it at leading order in Newton's constant: S(A) = Area(minimal surface anchored on the boundary of A) / (4 G). It presupposes the von Neumann entropy of a boundary reduced state on a continuum Hilbert space and the area of a surface in a bulk geometry. The repository has an exact von Neumann entropy dichotomy for algebraic spectra and an exact rational Regge area proxy that is not the Einstein-Hilbert action; neither is a minimal-surface area in a bulk geometry. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/rational algebraic shadows and scope fences: (1) over Q, substituting the regulated AdS_3 geodesic length 2 R_AdS * logFactor into rtLeadingEntropy(area, G_N) = area / (4 G_N) reproduces the 2D CFT Calabrese-Cardy coefficient (c / 3) * logFactor under the Brown-Henneaux relation c = 3 R_AdS / (2 G_N^(3)) and eliminates both bulk couplings in S_A / c = logFactor / 3, while submodular surface pasting yields Strong Subadditivity S(ABC) + S(B) <= S(AB) + S(BC) and all 380 proper contiguous boundary intervals of the 20-qubit 6-pentagon HaPPY patch satisfy complement symmetry A <-> A^c; (2) under BakerCitedInput (EntropyDichotomy.lean), no mixed algebraic spectrum can have natural-log von Neumann entropy equal to a rational RT ratio area / (4 G_N), equality holds at G_N > 0 iff the state is pure and area = 0, and stabilizer bit counts require dividing by log 2; and (3) on the orthogonal_pentatope chart of TFQ-0100, the 6 right-triangle hinges have Cayley-Menger squared area 1/4 and the 4 equilateral-triangle hinges have squared area 3/4 (total 9/2) with no rational linear area A in Q satisfying A^2 = 3/4, the flat-chart Regge proxy (kappa = 0) vanishes identically whereas all 380 HaPPY intervals satisfy 1 <= S(A) <= mincut(A), and under length rescaling L -> lam * L the Regge proxy scales as lam^4 against lam^2 for 2-surface area and lam^0 for bond counts.

records.name: Almheiri, Dong and Harlow 2015: bulk locality and quantum error correction
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against the full text of arXiv:1411.7041 on 2026-10-22; the finite 5-qubit reconstruction instance is the separate target ADS-LOGICAL-RECONSTRUCTION-TARGET.
records.summary: Almheiri, Dong and Harlow (2015, arXiv:1411.7041) resolve the radial-commutativity puzzle of bulk local operators by formulating the low-energy bulk Hilbert space as a code subspace H_code inside the boundary CFT Hilbert space: a bulk operator phi(x) in the causal wedge (or entanglement wedge, Section 3.4) of a boundary subregion A can be reconstructed as an operator O_A supported on A that acts identically to phi(x) on H_code (Section 3.1 eq. (3.3) p. 11, equivalent to [O, E_a P E_b^dagger] = 0 on the erasure errors of A^c in Section 3.2 eqs. (3.10), (3.15) pp. 13-15, illustrated by the three-qutrit code in Section 2.2 eq. (2.4) p. 8). This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Harlow 2016: the Ryu-Takayanagi formula from quantum error correction
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against the full text of arXiv:1607.03901 (Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 5.1) on 2026-10-22; the theorem is not formalized in this repository.
records.summary: Harlow (2016, arXiv:1607.03901, Theorem 1.1 pp. 3-4 and Section 5 Theorem 5.1 pp. 20-26) establishes in finite-dimensional operator-algebra quantum error correction that for a code subspace H_code in H_A tensor H_{A-bar} and a von Neumann algebra M on H_code with commutant M' and center Z_M = M cap M', three conditions are equivalent: (i) complementary recovery of M on A and M' on A-bar, (ii) existence of a positive central area operator L_A in Z_M such that for every code state rho-tilde, S(rho-tilde_A) = Tr(rho-tilde L_A) + S(rho-tilde, M) and S(rho-tilde_{A-bar}) = Tr(rho-tilde L_A) + S(rho-tilde, M'), and (iii) conservation of relative entropy S(rho-tilde_A | sigma-tilde_A) = S(rho-tilde | sigma-tilde, M). This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Pastawski, Yoshida, Harlow and Preskill 2015: holographic quantum error-correcting codes
records.obligation: Record only. The abstract itself calls the codes toy models.
records.summary: Pastawski, Yoshida, Harlow and Preskill (2015, arXiv:1503.06237) define a 2n-leg perfect tensor (Section 2 Def. 2 p. 5: proportional to an isometric tensor for every bipartition into k <= n inputs and 2n - k outputs), construct the 6-qubit perfect stabilizer tensor from the [[5,1,3]] code of Laflamme et al. (1996, arXiv:quant-ph/9602019 Table I; HaPPY Appendix A.1 eqs. (A1)-(A7) pp. 24-25), and place it on the {5,4} hyperbolic pentagon tiling to obtain an isometric bulk-to-boundary code (Section 3 Thm. 1 p. 7) in which connected boundary regions of holographic states satisfy S_A = |gamma_A| log v (Section 4.1 Thm. 2 p. 8) and general regions satisfy the greedy-geodesic lower bound (Section 4.2 Thm. 3 eq. (4.10) p. 10). This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Finite target: the five-qubit code gives a six-leg perfect tensor
records.obligation: Checked in Lean 4 by exhaustive GF(2) symplectic enumeration over the 64-element stabilizer group, the 20 bipartitions and the 1024-element five-qubit Pauli group. A finite stabilizer enumeration is not a statement about AdS/CFT.
records.summary: Formalized finite statement. The [[5,1,3]] code of Laflamme, Miquel, Paz and Zurek has stabilizer generators XZZXI, IXZZX, XIXZZ, ZXIXZ and logical operators XXXXX and ZZZZZ. Its Choi state is the six-qubit stabilizer state with generators g tensor I (four of them), XXXXX tensor X and ZZZZZ tensor Z. Checked in Lean 4 on Pauli operators modulo phase (GF(2) symplectic vectors): the six generators pairwise commute and generate a group of 64 distinct elements, with weight distribution 1 element of weight 0, 45 of weight 4 and 18 of weight 6 (the hexacode six-qubit state), so every non-identity element has weight at least 4, which is the perfect-tensor condition (every bipartition with at most three legs on one side has a maximally mixed marginal); for all twenty 3|3 bipartitions the stabilizer subgroup supported on one side is trivial, so the entropy is 3 bits by the stabilizer formula S(A) = |A| - log2 |G_A|; and in the five-qubit code the normalizer of the 16-element stabilizer has order 64 and its 48 elements outside the stabilizer (the nontrivial logical operators, modulo phase) have minimum weight 3. The reading of weights and local stabilizer subgroups as marginals and entropies is the standard stabilizer-formalism dictionary and is not formalised on density matrices.

records.name: Finite target: boundary entropies of a six-tensor patch against minimal cuts
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the 20 explicit generators are the boundary stabilizer of the contracted six-tensor network with bulk legs fixed at logical zero (they are entered by hand from the pushing rules of the code generators); that mincut as computed (a minimum over side assignments of the six tensors) is the minimal curve cut in the planar dual; the list of the 40 intervals where equality fails (only the counts are stated). The correspondence to a continuum minimal-surface area is the imported formula and is not part of the target.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for a hand-encoded model. Contract six copies of the six-leg perfect tensor on the {5,4} pentagon tiling: one central tensor and its five edge-neighbours, which are not adjacent to each other, so the patch has 20 dangling boundary legs (4 per outer tensor) and 6 bulk legs, every bulk leg fixed in the logical zero state. In Lean the 20-qubit boundary stabilizer is given by 20 explicit generators (15 local to the five outer blocks and 5 pushed through the internal bonds from the central tensor): they pairwise commute and have full GF(2) rank 20. For all 380 proper contiguous boundary intervals A (20 starting positions, lengths 1 to 19), with S(A) = rank(G restricted to A) - |A| in bits and mincut(A) the minimal number of bonds cut separating A from its complement in the six-tensor star graph: S(A) <= mincut(A) on all 380 intervals, S(A) = mincut(A) on exactly 340 intervals, and S(A) = mincut(A) - 1 on exactly 40. The Ryu-Takayanagi equality therefore fails on this patch for 40 intervals; it is not a statement that holds for every region.

records.name: Finite target: logical operators of the five-qubit code live on any three qubits
records.obligation: Checked in Lean 4 over the 16-element stabilizer, its three logical cosets, all 10 triples, all 10 pairs and all 105 low-weight Pauli errors. The identification with bulk operator reconstruction in AdS/CFT is the imported picture of the source.
records.summary: Formalized finite statement. For the [[5,1,3]] code, each of the ten 3-qubit subsets T of physical qubits supports a representative of each of the three nontrivial logical classes (the cosets of the stabilizer by XXXXX, ZZZZZ and YYYYY, the product class), and no 2-qubit subset supports a representative of any of them. Equivalent statement also checked in Lean 4: all 105 non-identity Pauli errors of weight 1 or 2 anticommute with a stabilizer generator, so none lies in the normalizer and erasure of any two qubits is correctable (the Knill-Laflamme condition). All operators are Pauli operators modulo phase. This is the smallest exact instance of the subregion-reconstruction picture of bulk operators.

records.name: Gap: repository Regge areas versus the area term of the minimal-surface formula
records.obligation: No source relates the Regge hinge areas of the repository to bond counts of a tensor network.
records.summary: Open question: whether the exact rational Regge proxy of TFQ-0100 (squared hinge areas weighted by a holonomy defect, which is not the Einstein-Hilbert action) can supply the area term of a finite minimal-surface statement. The imported formula uses the area of a minimal surface in a bulk geometry; the HaPPY patch measures a bond count (one bit per bond). Matching the two needs a dictionary from geometry to network that no source supplies. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact non-equivalence fences: (1) on the 20-qubit 6-pentagon HaPPY {5,4} patch (6 tensors, 5 internal bonds, 20 boundary legs), across all 380 proper nonempty contiguous boundary intervals the minimal bond cut intervalMincut takes values {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} with exact multiplicities (50, 90, 110, 100, 30), whereas the 4D orthogonal_pentatope simplex of TFQ-0100 has 6 right-triangle hinges of squared area 1/4 and 4 equilateral-triangle hinges of squared area 3/4 (240 Kuhn pentatopes on closed_s4_cube_boundary) and no single rational constant alpha maps both hinge classes to unit bond weight 1; (2) subdividing a planar surface of linear area A into m equal sub-hinges preserves the linear area sum m * (A / m) = A for all m != 0 but reduces the squared-area sum to m * (A / m)^2 = A^2 / m with strictly positive defect ((m - 1) / m) * A^2 > 0 for all m > 1 and A != 0; and (3) the TFQ-0100 rational Regge proxy scales linearly with bulk holonomy defect kappa ((9/2) * kappa on orthogonal_pentatope, vanishing at kappa = 0 as in ReggePachnerWdw flat_vertex_wdw_closure), whereas intervalMincut 2 len varies across (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) at len in {1, 2, 3, 4, 8} (with intervalMincut 0 4 = 1) as a function of the boundary subregion on a fixed background.

records.name: Gap: finite code checks are not a derivation of AdS/CFT
records.obligation: Recorded as an explicit non-claim and non-equivalence fence so that finite stabilizer-code checks are not read as evidence for continuum AdS/CFT; Lorentzian time evolution, non-flat entanglement spectra, sub-AdS locality, and continuum gravitational dynamics remain open.
records.summary: No source read for this change derives AdS/CFT, or its continuum entropy formula, from a finite stabilizer-code tensor network. The HaPPY codes are discrete kinematic models of the bulk-to-boundary map on a hyperbolic tiling with no Lorentzian time, no dynamics, no gravitational action and no large-N limit. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact non-equivalence fences: (1) every stabilizer reduced state has flat Renyi spectrum S_n / S_1 = 1, whereas a 2D CFT single interval has Calabrese-Cardy / Ryu-Takayanagi Renyi ratio cftRenyiFactor(n) = (1 + 1/n)/2, yielding a strictly positive defect ((n - 1)/(2n)) * S_1 > 0 for all n > 1 and S_1 > 0; (2) on the 20-qubit boundary state of the 6-pentagon {5,4} HaPPY patch (with bulk legs fixed in |0_L>), all 280 contiguous intervals of lengths 1..7 and 13..19 satisfy S(A) = mincut(A), whereas lengths 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 exhibit 5, 10, 10, 10, 5 strict Ryu-Takayanagi deficits (S(A) = mincut(A) - 1, summing to 40), including the explicit 5-fold rotational orbit start = 4*k + 2 at len = 8 and its complement len = 12 (S = 4 < 5 = mincut); and (3) disconnected boundary regions exhibit discrete integer mutual-information jumps (0, 0, 3, 1 bits) while for nBulk < nBdry the bulk code subspace 2^{nBulk} has strictly positive orthogonal codimension 2^{nBdry} - 2^{nBulk} > 0 (30, 1048512, 33552384 for 1, 6, and 11 pentagons).

records.name: Penrose 1971: angular momentum and combinatorial space-time
records.obligation: Record only. The 1971 book chapter has no arXiv record and is not held in the checkout; Penrose's trivalent admissibility rules are verified in Rovelli-Smolin (arXiv:gr-qc/9505006 Section 2 p. 12) and Roberts (arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Section 2 pp. 24-27).
records.summary: Penrose (1971) starts from angular momentum, whose spectrum is discrete, and asks whether space can be built up by applying the rules for combining angular momenta; the construction is the origin of spin networks. This node records the chapter by title and publication details.

records.name: Rovelli and Smolin 1995: spin networks and quantum gravity
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against the full text of arXiv:gr-qc/9505006 on 2026-10-22.
records.summary: Rovelli and Smolin (1995, arXiv:gr-qc/9505006, Phys. Rev. D 52, 5743) construct an independent basis of states in both the loop representation (Section 3 pp. 12-16) and the SU(2) connection representation (Section 4 pp. 17-24) that solves the SU(2) Mandelstam identities (Section 2 eq. (21) and conditions i-ii p. 12), labelled by imbedded graphs whose edges carry SU(2) representations (twice-spins p_l) and whose higher-valence vertices carry virtual trivalent trees/intertwiners (Appendix A pp. 36-38), and show in Section 6 (pp. 26-29) that these spin-network states are orthonormal with respect to the Ashtekar-Lewandowski Haar measure. This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Imported: a kinematical Hilbert space of SU(2) spin networks
records.obligation: The compact-group completion that the structure needs is the SU(2) analogue of the open U(1) circle gap FQ-GAP-U1-CIRCLE.
records.summary: Imported structure: states are graphs whose edges carry SU(2) irreducible representations (spins) and whose vertices carry intertwiners, in a Hilbert space built with the Haar measure on SU(2) (Peter-Weyl). The repository has no compact Lie group and no Haar measure: its circle-group nodes are open, and its spin-foam shadow uses q-deformed labels in cyclotomic fields.

records.name: Rovelli-Smolin 1995 and Ashtekar-Lewandowski 1997: area and volume spectra
records.obligation: Record only. Both normalization conventions (l_P^2 vs 8 pi gamma l_P^2, per Ashtekar-Lewandowski Section 3.3 footnote 6 p. 16) and the general vertex-puncture formula (eq. (4.9) p. 18) were audited against the papers on 2026-10-22.
records.summary: Rovelli and Smolin (1995, arXiv:gr-qc/9411005, Section 1 eqs. (1)-(2) p. 4 and Section 4 eqs. (47)-(48) p. 28) and Ashtekar and Lewandowski (1997, arXiv:gr-qc/9602046, Section 3.3 eq. (3.20) p. 16 and Section 4.1 eqs. (4.7)-(4.9), (4.12) pp. 18-19) compute discrete spectra for loop-quantum-gravity area (and volume) operators. In the convention {A_a^i(x), E_j^b(y)} = G delta_a^b delta_j^i delta^3(x,y) used in both papers, the general area eigenvalue is (l_P^2 / 2) sum_v sqrt(2 j_v^(d)(j_v^(d)+1) + 2 j_v^(u)(j_v^(u)+1) - j_v^(d+u)(j_v^(d+u)+1)) (eq. (4.9) of gr-qc/9602046), which for simple transverse punctures without tangential edges (j^(d)=j^(u)=j_i, j^(d+u)=0) equals l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)) = (l_P^2 / 2) sum_i sqrt(p_i(p_i+2)) with p_i = 2 j_i (eq. (2) and eq. (47) of gr-qc/9411005; eq. (4.12) of gr-qc/9602046); as Ashtekar and Lewandowski note in Section 3.3 footnote 6 (p. 16) and Engle et al. write in arXiv:0711.0146 Section V eq. (36) (p. 11), restoring the 8 pi G gamma factor from the gravitational action and Barbero-Immirzi parameter gamma multiplies this spectrum by 8 pi gamma, giving 8 pi gamma l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)). (The nonzero trivalent volume formula in eq. (1) and eq. (37) of gr-qc/9411005 was corrected in the erratum Nucl. Phys. B 456 (1995) 753, where trivalent vertices have zero volume.) This node records both papers and their normalization conventions.

records.name: Finite target: exact area levels as sums of square roots
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the formal vector is the real area (no real square root occurs in the module) and that two multisets have equal real area if and only if their vectors agree, which needs the linear independence over Q of sqrt(2), sqrt(3), sqrt(6), sqrt(15), sqrt(35) (stated in the module header, not a Lean theorem); the agreement of the hand-entered punctureArea table with the m_k, d_k table beyond inspection; the minimum over multisets of several punctures (only single punctures). The physical constant, the Immirzi parameter and the gauge-invariance constraint on admissible puncture lists are not part of the target.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the formal radical basis. With the dimensionless area a = sum over punctures of sqrt(j(j+1)) for spins j in {1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3}, each term is c_j sqrt(s_j) with squarefree radicand s_j in {2, 3, 6, 15, 35}: sqrt(3)/2, sqrt(2), sqrt(15)/2, sqrt(6), sqrt(35)/2 and 2 sqrt(3) for j = 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3 (radicands 3, 2, 15, 6, 35, 3); Lean checks k(k+2) = m_k^2 d_k with d_k squarefree for the twice-spins k = 1..6, and holds each term as a vector in the formal Q-module on the basis (sqrt2, sqrt3, sqrt6, sqrt15, sqrt35)/2. On that module: (i) the 210 puncture multisets of size at most 4 (the empty one and 209 nonempty ones) have 209 distinct reduced vectors, the zero vector included (208 nonzero); (ii) the unique collision is one puncture of spin 3 with four punctures of spin 1/2 (2 sqrt(3) = 4 x sqrt(3)/2); (iii) for a single puncture the squared area j(j+1) = k(k+2)/4 is at least 3/4, strictly increasing in k, with minimum 3/4 at j = 1/2 (area sqrt(3)/2).

records.name: Ponzano and Regge 1968: semiclassical limit of Racah coefficients
records.obligation: Record only. The 1968 chapter has no arXiv record and is not held in the checkout; its asymptotic formula is verified in Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 p. 22 and Section 6.1 p. 61).
records.summary: Ponzano and Regge (1968) give the leading asymptotic form of the 6j symbol (Racah coefficient) for large spins, with separate forms for the classically allowed and forbidden regions, and introduce a state sum for three-dimensional gravity whose phase matches the Regge action of a tetrahedron. The formula was reached by conjecture and numerical checks. This node records the chapter by title and publication details.

records.name: Roberts 1999: classical 6j symbols and the tetrahedron
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61 on 2026-10-22.
records.summary: Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Section 1 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61) establishes by geometric quantization of the 8-sphere and stationary phase on the symplectic reduction that for an admissible 6-tuple of integers a, b, c, d, e, f (where a = 2j labels the (a+1)-dimensional irreducible representation of SU(2)) whose side lengths form a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron tau of positive volume V(tau) > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the rescaled 6j symbol {ka, kb, kc; kd, ke, kf} has the k -> infinity asymptotic expansion sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(tau) k^3)) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (k a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) + O(k^{-5/2}). Since a tetrahedron of side lengths j_r = a_r/2 has volume V_j = V(tau)/8, substituting 2 / (3 pi V(tau)) = 1 / (12 pi V_j) and (a_r + 1)/2 = j_r + 1/2 recovers the Ponzano-Regge prefactor (12 pi V_j)^{-1/2}. This node records the paper's theorem.

records.name: Imported: Ponzano-Regge asymptotics of the 6j symbol
records.obligation: The asymptotic statement is a limit of real-valued quantities; the repository's exact finite targets do not establish a limit.
records.summary: Imported asymptotic form, audited against Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61): for large spins with edge lengths l_r = j_r + 1/2 = (a_r + 1)/2 (where a_r = 2 j_r), when the six lengths bound a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron of positive volume V > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the 6j symbol behaves asymptotically as (12 pi V)^{-1/2} cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (j_r + 1/2) theta_r + pi/4) (equivalently sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(a))) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) where V(a) = 8 V is the volume for side lengths a_r = 2 j_r), and decays exponentially when the Cayley-Menger squared volume is negative (Lorentzian tetrahedron, Section 6.2 p. 62). The phase is the Regge action of the tetrahedron.

records.name: Finite target: exact classical 6j symbols, orthogonality and the Biedenharn-Elliott identity
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: the Biedenharn-Elliott identity exhaustively for twice-spins 4 to 6 (four instances only); orthogonality for tuples whose intermediate range exceeds twice-spin 6; invariance of P, W^2 and the signed symbol under the symmetry generators, and invariance under the whole group (the closure of the tuple set under the generators is not stated). Exact enumeration with big integers. The classical 6j is not the q-deformed 6j at level 2 recorded in TFQ-0105; the q to 1 limit is not part of the target.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. The Wigner 6j symbol with twice-spins at most 6 is S sqrt(P), where S is Racah's single-sum factor, computed with exact integer factorials, and P is the product of four rational triangle factors; Lean defines the rational square W^2 = S^2 P (sixJSquaredRat) in this way. Checks: (i) the signed Racah factor S is invariant under the four generators of the 24 tetrahedral symmetries (the column swaps 12 and 23 and the double row flips on columns 12 and 23) for all 3,418 admissible 6-tuples with twice-spins at most 6 (the invariance of P under the symmetries is evident, since they permute its four triangle factors, but is not part of the Lean check); (ii) the orthogonality relation sum over x of (x+1)(y+1) {a b x; c d y}{a b x; c d y'} = delta(y,y') in twice-spin labels, for the 1,928 admissible tuples (a,b,c,d,y,y') whose labels and whose intermediate twice-spin x all lie at or below 6; (iii) the Biedenharn-Elliott (pentagon) identity for all 814 admissible 9-tuples with twice-spins at most 3, and for four explicit instances with twice-spins up to 6 (all labels 2; labels 3 with p=q=r=2; (a,b,c,d,e,f,p,q,r) = (4,2,3,3,2,4,3,3,2); and (6,0,6,0,6,0,6,6,6)). Exact arithmetic in the rationals with one square root per symbol.

records.name: Finite target: exact classification of 6j labels by the sign of the Cayley-Menger determinant
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: the exact squared 6j value for every tuple (three witnesses only, so the node does not give "the exact value in each case"); the identity between the 3x3 Gram form used by Lean and the bordered 5x5 Cayley-Menger determinant (an independent exact Python recomputation with the bordered 5x5 determinant reproduces the counts 13,691 / 10,884 / 2,807 and the three witness values); that 288 V^2 = 0 never occurs for any shifted-spin tuple (the module header claims it through a congruence mod 8; only the count 0 for twice-spins <= 8 is a Lean theorem). The Cayley-Menger sign convention follows the P0 mining run of TFQ-0084; the asymptotic comparison is not exact.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. For each admissible 6-tuple (a,b,c,d,e,f) of twice-spins at most 8 (all four triads (a,b,c), (a,e,f), (d,b,f), (d,e,c) admissible), take lengths l = j + 1/2 = (twice-spin + 1)/2. Lean computes 288 V^2 (scaled by 64, as the integer cayleyMengerScaled64) as the 3x3 Gram determinant of the squared edge lengths at the vertex where a, b, f meet, which equals the Cayley-Menger determinant. Across all 13,691 admissible 6-tuples: 10,884 have 288 V^2 > 0 (classically allowed region, a Euclidean tetrahedron exists), 2,807 have 288 V^2 < 0 (forbidden region), and none has 288 V^2 = 0. Exact values of 288 V^2 and of the squared 6j symbol are checked on three witnesses only: (2,2,2,2,2,2) with 729/16 and 1/36; (1,1,2,1,1,2) with -81/16 and 1/36; (2,2,4,2,2,4) with -4375/16 and 1/900. The comparison of magnitudes with the asymptotic formula is numerical and imported, and is not part of the target.

records.name: Turaev and Viro 1992: state sums from quantum 6j symbols
records.obligation: Record only. The paper has no arXiv record and is not held in the checkout.
records.summary: Turaev and Viro (1992) define a purely combinatorial invariant of 3-manifolds as a state sum over a triangulation, built from the quantum 6j symbols of U_q(sl_2) at a root of unity; it does not depend on the triangulation. This node records the paper by title and journal reference.

records.name: Finite target: quantum pentagon identity at q = exp(i pi/4) on labels 0, 1/2, 1
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the transcribed table equals the quantum 6j symbol at q = exp(i pi/4), neither derived from the q-Racah sum nor linked to the Rust function (the module imports H023 and H024 but uses nothing from them); the Z[zeta_12] data of H023 and H024; the dimension-weighted Turaev-Viro form of the identity (the checks are on the unitary-normalized F-symbols). The step from the local identity to invariance on a triangulation is not part of the target.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for a transcribed table. At q = exp(i pi/4) with spin labels 0, 1/2, 1 (twice-spin 0, 1, 2), the normalized recoupling symbol isingF(a,b,c,d,e,f) is entered in Lean as an explicit case table over Q(sqrt 2) (values 0, +-1, +-sqrt(2)/2, transcribed from ising_f in code/rust/src/general_relativity/spin_foam.rs). On that table Lean checks in exact arithmetic over Q(sqrt 2): the quantum dimensions (1, sqrt 2, 1) with d_1^2 - d_0 = d_2 and d_1 d_2 - d_1 = 0 (truncation); exactly 36 nonzero entries among the 729 label 6-tuples; the orthogonality relation sum over f of isingF(a,b,c,d,e,f) isingF(a,b,c,d,e',f) = delta(e,e') for all admissible labels; and the pentagon identity sum over r of isingF(a,b,c,q,p,r) isingF(a,r,d,e,q,s) isingF(b,c,d,s,r,t) = isingF(p,c,d,e,q,t) isingF(a,b,t,e,p,s) across all 3^9 = 19,683 label assignments in {0,1,2}^9 (both sides zero unless the six boundary triads are admissible). The repository's fence (TFQ-0105) refuses an admission of triangulation invariance; this target discharges only the identity on those labels, not invariance of a state sum on a triangulated manifold.

records.name: Engle, Livine, Pereira and Rovelli 2007 and Freidel and Krasnov 2007: spin-foam vertex for four-dimensional gravity
records.obligation: Record only. The constructions are not reproduced.
records.summary: Engle, Livine, Pereira and Rovelli (2008, arXiv:0711.0146, Sections II-IV eqs. (12)-(30) pp. 3-10) define a four-simplex spin-foam vertex amplitude for finite Barbero-Immirzi parameter gamma by imposing the linear simplicity constraint C_f = J_f^(+) - |(1+gamma)/(1-gamma)| J_f^(-) = 0 on Spin(4) representations (eqs. (18)-(20): j^+- = |1 +- gamma| k / 2, embedding the boundary SU(2) spin k into Spin(4) for Euclidean signature and into the SL(2,C) principal series (n, rho) = (2k, 2 gamma k) in Section IV eq. (24) for Lorentzian signature), and Freidel and Krasnov (2008, arXiv:0708.1595, Section II.C Lemmas 2.1-2.4 pp. 10-12 and Section V eqs. (80)-(91) pp. 24-27) construct the coherent-state spin-foam model that coincides with the EPRL vertex for 0 < gamma < 1. This node records the two papers.

records.name: Perez 2013: review of the spin foam approach
records.obligation: Record only.
records.summary: Perez (2013, arXiv:1205.2019, Living Rev. Relativity 16, 3) surveys canonical LQG and Plebanski BF constraints (Part II), 4D BF theory and the Riemannian/Lorentzian EPRL and FK spin-foam models with their large-spin semiclassical asymptotics (Part III, Sections 7-9), 3D Ponzano-Regge and Turaev-Viro state sums (Part IV, Section 10), and open problems on anomalies and discretization/continuum limits (Part V). This node records the review as published.

records.name: Imported: EPRL-FK vertex amplitude for four-dimensional gravity
records.obligation: The checked identities are rational arithmetic for the imported labels j+ = |1 + gamma| k / 2 and j- = |1 - gamma| k / 2, the pair (n, rho) = (2 k, 2 gamma k), and the count of 10 unordered pairs among five indices. They are not a Spin(4) 15j symbol, not a booster contraction, and not a continuum, semiclassical, or cosmological-constant limit. No source maps the finite cyclotomic amplitudes to the EPRL-FK amplitude.
records.summary: For rational gamma and rational k, the imported Euclidean labels are j+ = |1 + gamma| k / 2 and j- = |1 - gamma| k / 2. When 0 < gamma < 1 they equal (1 + gamma) k / 2 and (1 - gamma) k / 2, their sum is k, and their difference is gamma k. When gamma > 1 they equal (1 + gamma) k / 2 and (gamma - 1) k / 2, their difference is k, and their sum is gamma k. At gamma = 1/2 and k = 2 the labels are 3/2 and 1/2, the sum is 2, and the difference is 1, which is not 2. At gamma = 3 and k = 2 the labels are 4 and 2, the difference is 2, and the sum is 6, which is not 2. At gamma = 1 and k = 2 the labels are 2 and 0, and both the sum and the difference equal 2. The imported Lorentzian pair is (n, rho) = (2 k, 2 gamma k), with rho = gamma n = 2 gamma (n / 2). At gamma = 1/2 and k = 2 this pair is (4, 2), the index j = n / 2 equals 2, and gamma j equals 1, so rho = 2 gamma j rather than gamma j. The number of unordered pairs among five indices is 10. A Spin(4) 15j contraction, booster factors, a continuum Lie-group representation, a spin-network boundary space, a sum over spins, a continuum limit, a semiclassical limit, and a cosmological constant stay imported and are not constructed. The finite cyclotomic amplitudes named by TFQ-0198 are not identified with an EPRL-FK vertex.

records.name: Gap: no route from finite recoupling to a continuum or semiclassical limit
records.obligation: Recorded as an explicit non-claim.
records.summary: No source read for this change derives a continuum limit, a semiclassical limit or a physical cosmological constant from the finite recoupling tables of the repository, or from the exact finite targets of this stage. The fences of TFQ-0104 and TFQ-0105 say so; this node records the gap so that the exact 6j, area and pentagon checks are not read as steps toward a limit.

records.name: Finite semi-simplicial or globular shadow of Genesis admission
records.obligation: Missing parent construction: PGW-GO-ADMISSION-GATE is a two-valued admission record, and no source builds a finite semi-simplicial set or a finite globular set from it.
records.summary: No construction turns PGW-GO-ADMISSION-GATE into a finite semi-simplicial set or a finite globular set. That gate keeps a two-valued admission record with a reached result: reaching leaves not-admitted, and admission is not one of the four kinds of change. A finite semi-simplicial set of dimension at most N is finite sets X_0, ..., X_N and face maps d_i from X_n to X_{n-1} such that d_i composed with d_j equals d_{j-1} composed with d_i whenever i < j. It carries no degeneracy maps. A finite globular set is finite sets with source and target maps s, t from X_{n+1} to X_n such that s composed with s equals s composed with t, and t composed with t equals t composed with s. Neither family is defined from the admission record.

records.name: Truncation: components, finite fundamental groupoid, finite n-type presentation
records.obligation: pi_0, the finite fundamental groupoid and a finite n-type presentation stay undefined while GTH-SHADOW has no construction.
records.summary: Let a finite shadow be a finite semi-simplicial set or a finite globular set as in GTH-SHADOW. Its set of path components, pi_0, is the quotient of the 0-cells by the equivalence relation generated by finite 1-zigzags. Its finite fundamental groupoid has the 0-cells as objects and, as morphisms, equivalence classes of finite 1-paths, the equivalence being the one generated by the 2-cells when 2-cells are part of the shadow. A finite n-type presentation keeps cells and face data through dimension n and stops there. None of these quotients or presentations is constructed, because no shadow is constructed from the admission gate.

records.name: Horn fillers of a finite shadow
records.obligation: Which horns would have fillers is open. There is no object of which a filler or a missing filler could be shown.
records.summary: The horn Lambda^k[n] is the union of all faces of the standard n-simplex except the face opposite vertex k. The horn is inner when 0 < k < n and outer when k = 0 or k = n. A Kan condition asks for a filler of every horn. A quasicategory asks for a filler of every inner horn, in the sense of Joyal, Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 175 (2002) 207-222. Which of these fillers a finite object derived from Genesis admission would have is open. No filler is exhibited and no counterexample is exhibited, because no such finite object is constructed.

records.name: Finite model of a fragment with identity types, without univalence
records.obligation: No deep embedding, no finite model and no soundness statement. The fragment excludes univalence. Lean Prop is a different theory.
records.summary: No deep embedding of a dependent type theory, and no finite model of such a theory, is constructed. The fragment in view has identity types and does not include univalence. Lean's impredicative proof-irrelevant Prop is a different theory; this node does not add univalence to that theory and does not interpret it. An intended interpretation would send contexts to finite sets or to finite semi-simplicial data and would send identity types to a stated path relation. No such interpretation is defined, and no soundness statement is derived.

records.name: Imported: a univalent universe is not finite
records.obligation: The assumption is a univalent universe. It is not finite, it is not derived, and any finite identity-type model is only an approximation of it.
records.summary: Assumed, and not derived from Genesis admission or from any finite model: a univalent universe in the sense of the Homotopy Type Theory book (The Univalent Foundations Program, Institute for Advanced Study, 2013), a type U together with a map from the identity type Id_U(A, B) to the type of equivalences between A and B that is itself an equivalence. Such a universe is not a finite set and is not a finite semi-simplicial set of bounded dimension. A finite model of a fragment with identity types, were one later defined, would be only an approximation of this assumption: the assumption is an infinite object, and the finite model would not contain it.

records.name: Imported: an infinity-groupoid is not finite
records.obligation: The assumption is an infinity-groupoid (Kan complex, fillers for every horn). It is not finite, it is not derived, and a finite n-type is only an approximation.
records.summary: Assumed, and not derived: an infinity-groupoid in the sense of a Kan complex, a simplicial set in which every horn has a filler, as used for infinity-groupoids in Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, arXiv:math/0608040. An infinity-groupoid has cells in every finite dimension. It is not a finite semi-simplicial set of bounded dimension. A finite n-type presentation is only an approximation of this assumption: it stops at a fixed dimension and does not supply fillers in all higher dimensions.

records.name: Imported: an (infinity,1)-category is not finite
records.obligation: The assumption is an (infinity,1)-category (inner horn fillers). It is not finite, it is not derived, and a finite inner-horn condition is only an approximation.
records.summary: Assumed, and not derived: an (infinity,1)-category in the sense of a quasicategory, a simplicial set in which every inner horn has a filler. Joyal, Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 175 (2002) 207-222, isolates that inner-horn condition and its relation to Kan complexes. Boardman and Vogt, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 347 (1973), introduced the weak Kan complexes of which this is the later name. Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, arXiv:math/0608040, develops the theory. An (infinity,1)-category is not a finite semi-simplicial set. A finite inner-horn condition on a finite complex, were one stated, would be only an approximation of this assumption.

records.name: Goedel-Rosser and Tarski limit
records.obligation: The two limit statements are conditional on the hypotheses in the statement. The priced admission language is not defined and is not shown to meet (i), (ii) or (iii). Nothing is formalised in Lean. Admitting a later theory is a priced import record, not a derivation from the core.
records.summary: Let S be a theory in classical first-order logic with a primitive recursive coding of its syntax. Write code(psi) for the code of a sentence psi and num(n) for the numeral of a natural number n. Assume (i) consistency: there is no sentence psi such that S derives both psi and the negation of psi. Assume (ii) a primitive recursive relation Proof such that psi is a theorem of S exactly when Proof(p, code(psi)) holds for some natural number p, and Proof is represented at standard numerals: for all natural numbers p and s, S derives the sentence expressing Proof(num(p), num(s)) when the relation holds and derives its negation when the relation fails. Assume (iii) that S derives every true Delta_0 sentence of this coding; that the substitution function subst, sending the code of a formula with one free variable and a number n to the code of the sentence obtained by substituting num(n) for that variable, is represented in S; that the primitive recursive function neg on codes, with neg(code(psi)) equal to code(the negation of psi), is represented in S; and that for each standard natural number n, S derives both that every w with w < num(n) equals one of num(0), ..., num(n-1), and that every w satisfies w < num(n) or w = num(n) or num(n) < w. Then there is a sentence phi such that S derives neither phi nor the negation of phi. The diagonal lemma from representation of subst supplies, for the negation of the Rosser formula RosserProv(v) given by existence of a u such that Proof(u, v) and such that Proof(w, neg(v)) fails for every w < u, a sentence phi such that S derives the biconditional of phi and the negation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))). If S derives phi, a standard derivation code p, clause (i), numeral-wise representation of Proof, and the schema that every number below num(p) equals one of num(0), ..., num(p-1), yield a derivation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))) and then of the negation of phi. If S derives the negation of phi, a least standard derivation code q of that negation, numeral-wise representation of Proof, the same bounded schema at q, and the schema that every number is below num(q), equal to num(q), or above num(q), yield a derivation of the negation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))) and then of phi. Either case contradicts (i). Separately, drop (i) and (ii) and keep (iii): if a formula Tr(x) is such that S derives the biconditional of Tr(num(code(psi))) and psi for every sentence psi, the same diagonal lemma applied to the negation of Tr supplies a sentence lambda for which those biconditionals yield a derivation of both lambda and its negation, so S is inconsistent. Both conclusions use only the hypotheses just stated and classical first-order logic.

records.name: Observer tuple for empirical claims
records.obligation: A reading of WDP-CH10-D01 to D04, not a derivation. WDP chapter 15 has no node in this graph, so the layer component has no repository node to attach to. No source relates the L1 observer axioms H1 to H5 to this five-component tuple.
records.summary: Definition A1 of the source note. Fix a finite set M of measurements with finite outcome sets and a cover C of M by maximal contexts, and write E(U) for the set of outcome assignments on U. An observer tuple is O = (K, Adm, norm, Term, L). K = (M, C, E). Adm is the convex hull conv(A) of the vectors (delta_g restricted to C) over all contexts C, for g in E(M). The norm is the l1 norm on the stacked context distributions. Term maps the defect and the claim to a status: defect 0 gives ExactRepair, defect above 0 with a support-level global section gives ClosedResidual, and otherwise OpenObstruction. L is the diagnostic layer. The defect of a claim e = (e_C), one distribution per context, is Delta_O(e) = min over p in Adm of the l1 norm of (e - p). The five components are a projection of the four packets of WDP chapter 10 (presentation, memory, evaluator, policy) and of the chapter 15 grade. The monograph defines no five-tuple of its own; the ledger row records a search for "5-tuple" that returned nothing.

records.name: Pushforward of natural-number measures is functorial (Lean)
records.obligation: The Lean statement is the narrowed one above. The functor over rational probability vectors is proved in prose in the note (Lemma B2) and its instances on the PR box and the noisy PR boxes are recomputed by the independent check, which does not test the Lean statement. Independently replayed with Lean 4.35.0; the source-bound axiom receipt is dag/research/foc035_observer_presheaf_lean_replay.json.
records.summary: In Lean (LggrFiniteResults), a finitely supported measure with natural-number weights is a list of (value, weight) pairs, and pushforward along f maps each value by f and keeps its weight. Then: push of the identity is the identity (push_id); push along g after f equals push along the composite (push_comp); total mass is unchanged (mass_push); and the weight at b of push f p equals the mass of the entries of p whose image is b (weightAt_push). The note reads marginalisation of a context distribution as such a pushforward along the restriction map, so these are the identity and composition laws of the functor from the opposite of the context poset to probability vectors (Lemma B2). That reading is not a Lean statement. Not covered: rational weights, normalisation to probability vectors, the context poset, and the Rust types. The ledger row states the same narrowing.

records.name: Parity cycles: holonomy and global sections (Lean)
records.obligation: The Lean statement is the narrowed one above; no Lean statement mentions a nerve, a cohomology class or the noncontextual fraction. Independently replayed with Lean 4.35.0; the source-bound axiom receipt is dag/research/foc035_observer_presheaf_lean_replay.json.
records.summary: In Lean (LggrFiniteResults), take a length n > 0 and edge parities b : Nat -> Bool. Let holonomy b k be the exclusive or of b 0, ..., b (k-1), and call g a section when, for every i < n, the exclusive or of g i and g ((i+1) mod n) equals b i. Then (section_exists_iff_holonomy_zero) a section exists if and only if holonomy b n = false. Further (no_joint_measure_when_holonomy_one), if holonomy b n = true then no finitely supported natural-weight measure on assignments Nat -> Bool with positive total mass has, for every i < n, zero pushforward weight on every pair of values (g i, g ((i+1) mod n)) whose exclusive or differs from b i. These are the clause "G(e) is nonempty iff the holonomy h is 0" and the clause "holonomy 1 forbids a positive-mass joint measure with parity-supported marginals" of Proposition B6. Not in Lean: the arc-cover clause, the noncontextual-fraction clause and the Cech-cohomology reading.

records.name: Global section, convex hull and noncontextual fraction 1
records.obligation: Not formalised in Lean (ledger row L035-L1, node OPS-LEAN-GAP). The proof is in the note and is not machine-checked.
records.summary: Proposition B3(1). For an empirical model e = (e_C) on a finite scenario, let A be the matrix whose column g, for g in E(M), is the stacked vector of the point masses of g restricted to each context, and let NCF(e) = max of the sum of lambda_g over lambda >= 0 with A lambda <= e. Then these are equivalent: e has a global section (a probability vector d on E(M) with marginal e_C on every context C); e lies in conv(A); NCF(e) = 1. This is the local-hidden-variable condition. Instances recomputed exactly: the mixture (1/2)(delta_g1 + delta_g2), with g1 = (0,0,0,0) and g2 = (1,0,0,1) on (a, a', b, b'), has NCF 1; the noisy PR box (1 - lam) PR + lam U at lam = 1/2 has NCF 1 and a distribution as a global section.

records.name: Strong contextuality is noncontextual fraction 0
records.obligation: Not formalised in Lean (ledger row L035-L1, node OPS-LEAN-GAP).
records.summary: Proposition B3(3). Write G(e) for the set of g in E(M) with e_C(g restricted to C) > 0 for every context C. Then e is strongly contextual (G(e) is empty) if and only if NCF(e) = 0: if lambda_g > 0 is feasible then e_C(g|C) >= lambda_g > 0 for every C, so g is in G(e); conversely g in G(e) makes lambda = (min over C of e_C(g|C)) delta_g feasible with positive weight. Instance recomputed exactly: the PR box on the Bell scenario (contexts ab, ab', a'b, a'b', each uniform on the two outcome pairs with parity 0, 0, 0, 1) has |G| = 0 and NCF 0. The four parity constraints x_a + x_b = 0, x_a + x_b' = 0, x_a' + x_b = 0 and x_a' + x_b' = 1 sum to 0 = 1 modulo 2, so none of the 16 assignments satisfies all.

records.name: Noncontextual fraction of the noisy PR box
records.obligation: Tested points only. The Rust receipt replay clause of the ledger row is in node OPS-RUST-RECEIPTS-AND-LIMITS.
records.summary: On the Bell scenario let the noisy PR box be e_lam = (1 - lam) PR + lam U, where U puts 1/4 on every local outcome pair. The exact noncontextual fraction is 1/2 at lam = 1/4 and 1 at lam = 1/2, which is 2 lam at both points. The l1 defect to conv(A) is positive at lam = 1/4 and 0 at lam = 1/2, and the global support has 16 elements at both points. The closed form 2 lam for every lam below 1/2 is not claimed.

records.name: Descent over the maximal cover never fails to glue
records.obligation: The reading of the proposition as a statement about the Rust classifier is not checked here (not run here). Not formalised in Lean.
records.summary: Proposition B4(1). Let S(U) be the set of assignments s on U whose restriction to every maximal context C inside U lies in the support of e_C; then S(M) = G(e). Over the cover of M by its maximal contexts, every matching family (s_C in S(C), agreeing on overlaps) glues to exactly one element of S(M). So a descent classifier on that cover reports no NoGlobalExtension, its fibers are in bijection with G(e), and strong contextuality appears as zero matching families, not as a failed gluing. Instances recomputed exactly: the PR box has 0 matching families; the noisy PR box at lam = 1/2 has 16, each with exactly one gluing.

records.name: A noncontextual model that fails descent on an arc cover
records.obligation: An existence claim with one witness. The Rust classifier outcome names (Unique, NoGlobalExtension) are read as: exactly one gluing, no gluing. Not run here for the Rust code.
records.summary: Existence witness. On the Bell scenario let e = (1/2)(delta_g1 + delta_g2) with g1 = (a, a', b, b') = (0,0,0,0) and g2 = (1,0,0,1). Then NCF(e) = 1 and G(e) has 2 elements. Over the arc cover {a, a', b}, {a', b, b'}, which omits the context {a, b'}, there are 4 matching families; 2 of them have exactly one gluing in S(M) and 2 have none. So a noncontextual model can have matching families without a global extension on a cover that omits a context.

records.name: NoGlobalExtension alone is not evidence of contextuality
records.obligation: A reading of two earlier nodes. No cover-independent sound reading of NoGlobalExtension is known to the note.
records.summary: Consequence of nodes OPS-MAXIMAL-COVER-DESCENT and OPS-ARC-COVER-NGE-WITNESS. A descent outcome NoGlobalExtension on a matching family is a statement about the chosen cover, not about the model: on the maximal cover it never occurs, and on the arc cover above it occurs for a model with NCF 1. Strong contextuality is G(e) empty, reported as NCF 0 with a Bell functional as the replayable witness. So the note's local-green-global-red event (a matching family over a cover of M whose descent outcome is NoGlobalExtension) is evidence that the cover's local checks do not reach the global object, and not evidence that no global object exists.

records.name: Cech coboundaries, no-signalling and the quotient defect
records.obligation: Phi_1 is the quotient value of the WDP degree-1 window; no source in this graph identifies the Cech-cochain Phi_1 with PG-WDP-DEGREE1-WINDOW with J the l1 norm, so that route is a gap. Not formalised in Lean.
records.summary: Proposition B5. Let N be the nerve of the maximal-context cover and take cochains valued in the presheaf U -> Q^E(U), with (delta0 alpha)_(C,C') the restriction of alpha_C to the overlap minus the restriction of alpha_C', and delta1 the alternating sum of restrictions on triples. Then delta1 delta0 = 0; for an empirical model e read as a 0-cochain, delta0 e = 0 if and only if e is no-signalling; and Phi_1([omega]) = min over alpha of the l1 norm of (omega - delta0 alpha) is unchanged by omega -> omega - delta0 beta. Instances recomputed exactly: the Bell nerve has four edges (a 4-cycle) and no triple, so delta1 delta0 = 0 is vacuous there; on the cover {0,1}, {0,2}, {0,3} (one nerve triple, overlap {0}) delta1 delta0 alpha = 0 for a non-constant alpha while a 1-cochain supported on one pair has delta1 beta = [1, 0]; delta0 e = 0 for the PR box and is nonzero at the pair (0,1) for a model whose a-marginal differs between the contexts ab and ab'; the unit cochain (1, 1) on the first edge of the Bell nerve has Phi_1 = 2, by the value 2 at alpha = 0 and a dual witness of sup norm 1 that annihilates delta0, and Phi_1 is again 2 after adding delta0 of a coboundary.

records.name: The 0-cocycle test does not separate contextual models
records.obligation: Not a statement about every possible cohomological invariant. Not formalised in Lean.
records.summary: Every no-signalling model, the PR box included, has delta0 e = 0 (node OPS-CECH-COBOUNDARY). So the test delta0 e = 0 does not separate contextual from noncontextual no-signalling models. This is a statement about the test, not about the class of e: in the unaugmented complex H^0 = ker delta0, so distinct no-signalling models are distinct classes. What the class lacks is an invariant that separates conv(A) from its complement; that separation is a positivity constraint. The earlier sentence that the class "carries no information about probabilistic contextuality" is narrowed to this.

records.name: Parity cycles: arc-cover descent and noncontextual fraction
records.obligation: Finite cases n = 3, 4, 5 only. The two clauses proved in Lean for every n are in node OPS-PARITY-HOLONOMY-LEAN; the arc-cover and NCF clauses for general n are not claimed.
records.summary: For n = 3, 4, 5 and every one of the 2^n parity-target vectors t on the n-cycle of binary measurements (contexts {m_i, m_(i+1 mod n)}, each distribution uniform on the two pairs with x_i xor x_(i+1) = t_i), let h be the exclusive or of the t_i. Then |G| is 2 if h = 0 and 0 if h = 1; the arc cover {m_0, ..., m_(n-2)}, {m_1, ..., m_(n-1)} has exactly 2 matching families, both with one gluing if h = 0 and both without a gluing if h = 1; and NCF is 1 if h = 0 and 0 if h = 1. That is 8 + 16 + 32 = 56 cases.

records.name: No-signalling and signed global sections
records.obligation: The equivalence is cited, not derived here. The instance covers one no-signalling model and says nothing about the converse direction or about other models.
records.summary: Assumed from Abramsky and Brandenburger (New Journal of Physics 13 (2011) 113036, arXiv:1102.0264), as the note cites it and does not prove it: an empirical model is no-signalling if and only if it has a signed global section, a function d on E(M) with values in Q, sum 1 and the given marginals. Instance recomputed exactly: the PR box, which is no-signalling, has a signed global section found by exact linear algebra, with sum 1, all 16 marginal equations satisfied and at least one negative entry.

records.name: The Z2 holonomy witness can be silent where the LP is not
records.obligation: Cited, not re-run. No family with a silent Z2 witness is exhibited in this repository.
records.summary: Assumed from Abramsky, Mansfield and Barbosa (EPTCS 95 (2012) 1-14, arXiv:1111.3620), as the note cites it: the Z2 holonomy witness of parity constraints can be silent where the linear-programming witness is not, that is, it has false negatives on other families of scenarios. The note does not compute such a family and does not claim the behaviour away.

records.name: Vorob'ev: acyclic covers glue every no-signalling model
records.obligation: Cited theorem with a proof sketch in the note only. Not formalised in Lean.
records.summary: Assumed from Vorob'ev (Theory of Probability and its Applications 7 (1962) 147-163, doi:10.1137/1107014), as the note states it: if the hypergraph (M, C) is GYO-acyclic (it reduces to nothing by removing ears and absorbed vertices, equivalently it has a join tree), then every no-signalling model has a global section given on a join tree T by d(g) = (product over C of e_C(g|C)) / (product over the edges (C, C') of T of e_(C intersect C')(g|C intersect C')), with 0/0 = 0. The note gives an induction sketch, not a full proof. The converse (for every non-acyclic hypergraph some no-signalling family has no global section) is not implemented; the PR box on the 4-cycle is one instance.

records.name: Product-formula gluing on a three-context path
records.obligation: One path cover. The Rust join-tree code and its refusal of the 4-cycle (NotAcyclic) are not run here. The theorem itself is node OPS-VOROBEV-THEOREM.
records.summary: On the path cover {0,1}, {1,2}, {2,3} of four binary measurements, with parity targets 0, 1, 1, the product formula of node OPS-VOROBEV-THEOREM (join-tree edges ({0,1},{1,2}) and ({1,2},{2,3})) gives a probability distribution on the 16 assignments whose three marginals equal the three given tables exactly, and NCF is 1. The GYO reduction empties the three-context path and the two-context path and does not empty the Bell 4-cycle or a triangle. This is one instance of the cited theorem, not a check of it.

records.name: Conditional underdetermination of the receipt
records.obligation: The norm and Term rows are arithmetic on the defect 2, not receipts of a configurable evaluator: the Rust evaluator implements one norm and one terminal rule. The second receipt of the Adm row is proved, not computed by the Rust code. Not formalised in Lean.
records.summary: Lemma A2. Let O' leave one of K, Adm, norm, Term undeclared, and require that an evaluation's receipt for a claim agree across every admissible completion of the undeclared component. Then no evaluation of O' meets that requirement: for each of the four components there are two admissible completions, agreeing elsewhere, whose receipts for one claim differ. Witnesses on the PR box (Bell scenario, parity targets 0, 0, 0, 1): K, the Bell cover gives defect 2 and the acyclic sub-cover {ab, ab'} gives defect 0; Adm, the noncontextual polytope gives 2 and the no-signalling polytope gives 0, because the PR box is no-signalling; norm, the l1 norm gives 2 and twice the l1 norm gives 4; Term, with defect 2 and empty global support the rule of the note gives OpenObstruction and the rule "defect below 3 gives ExactRepair" gives ExactRepair. The lemma does not say that no function from claims to receipts exists; any one completion defines a function. The layer has no row, because Definition A1 fixes it to diagnostic.

records.obligation: Cited by name, not re-run. The level statement is a typing remark and not a theorem; the Tarski clause is conditional on the arithmetic hypothesis.
records.summary: Axis 2. Let eval_n be the evaluator of a process on carrier K_n. The statement "eval_n is sound" relates eval_n to a standard of correctness for K_n; that standard is not an element of K_n, so the statement is a sentence of a carrier K_(n+1), and the output PASS of eval_n on it has no standing at K_(n+1) (ENC-0195, AuthorityEffect None). The level statement holds by construction of the carrier hierarchy. Imported: the strengthening by Tarski's undefinability theorem, which applies only when K_n interprets enough arithmetic, and the Genesis identifiers ENC-0118 and ENC-0195, cited by name.

records.obligation: Conditional on (iii), and on (i) and (ii) as cited, not re-run. WDP-CH14 has no node in this graph; (iii) is read as the observer-quotient reading of WDP chapter 10.
records.summary: Axis 3 of WDP-CH14-T01 under three hypotheses. (i) NS-14: an injective renaming sigma of presentation tokens commutes with the transition step and with full-history replay. (ii) CL-13 (passage_charge_const): a quantity conserved by internal transitions is constant on reachable states and equals its genesis value. (iii) The verdict V reads a history only through a declared export Exp, so V = Vbar o Exp, with Exp(sigma(H)) = Exp(H) for every injective renaming sigma; this is the identical-accessible-exports premise of Proposition 3.1 of the Argon synthesis. Then V(sigma(H)) = V(H), because V(sigma(H)) = Vbar(Exp(sigma(H))) = Vbar(Exp(H)) = V(H). Without (iii) the statement is false (node OPS-REFUTED-AXIS3-WIDE). A drop in the internal defect Delta_O stays computable and renaming-invariant; whether a drop is a repair or a reinterpretation is a question about the grounding map of the tokens, which no export-reading verdict decides.

records.summary: At head 0a0502646 of the source repository the following were wrong. (N4) Scenario::section_count multiplied arities without a check, and the limit was compared afterwards: 64 binary singletons (2^64 assignments) wrapped to 0 in a release build, so global_support returned an empty support and is_strongly_contextual returned true. (N5) ObserverDraft::declare accepted empty and whitespace strings, and the five strings were free text copied into the receipt: a norm "L2", a terminal "always OpenObstruction" and a layer "authoritative" each yielded the l1 value, ExactRepair and authority None. (N6) Proposition A2 claimed that no claim-to-receipt function exists, carried a layer row whose second completion was not an observer, and said the refusal test dropped five components when it dropped two; and verify_noncontextual_fraction read only lp.value from the embedded solution. (N7) delta0 checked only the number of entries, delta1 and flatten1 ignored extraneous keys and pairs outside every triple, and the only delta1 delta0 = 0 test ran on the Bell nerve, which has no triple. Recomputed here: 2^64 is 0 modulo 2^64.
